raw_module_items.name: Desk ticket list and views are missing Zoho Desk capabilities
raw_module_items.description_html:
Updated 29 Sep 2026: items already implemented were removed after checking the code (client-engine staging, desk main, metadata-engine staging). The original description is kept in the comments.

Summary

The Tickets workspace (Views) compared with Zoho Desk. Custom views, the Unassigned Open / Overdue / Customer Responded / My Team's Open views, Ticket Peek, export from a view and the table options (column picker, reorder, clip/wrap) are now built. The gaps below remain.

Remaining gaps

  1. SLA Violated predefined view — missing; it depends on an SLA engine (see NDC-1785).

  2. Response Overdue and Tickets for Review views — built in the front end but never shown: the metadata-engine catalogue (v13) has no response_due, first_response_at or pending_review fields, and Desk has no draft submit-review / withdraw-review / approve / reject endpoints.

  3. Missed Chats view — only an approximation (open, unassigned chat/phone tickets); there is no real missed-chat signal from SalesIQ.

  4. Collision detection — the banner is built, but Desk has no viewers/heartbeat or viewers/me endpoint and no presence store, so the warning never appears.

  5. Archived views / auto-archive — the Archived view, bulk Archive/Unarchive and the Ticket Archiving settings page are built in the front end, but there is no is_archived field (catalogue v14), no Desk archive / unarchive / archive-settings endpoints and no auto-archive job. /settings/tickets/archiving and the ticket menu's Archive action fail today.

  6. Handshake work mode — only appears when the CRM ⇄ Desk integration is enabled for the tenant. Decide whether it should show without CRM, or enable the integration on the tenant.

Expected result

Parity with Zoho Desk ticket views, or an explicit product decision to leave these out.

Environment

raw_module_items.name: Desk settings links open the In Development page and the workflow editor deep link renders __no-module__
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Two navigation defects found while mapping Desk against Zoho Desk. They are real bugs rather than parity gaps.

Steps to reproduce — dead settings links

  1. Sign in to desk.taviportal.com and open Settings.

  2. Click Developer Hub → Integration Configuration.

  3. Repeat for Developer Hub → Custom Actions, Storage → Usage Overview, Storage → Buckets & S3 and Storage → Storage Requests.

Expected result

Each link opens its settings page, or the link is hidden if the page does not exist in Desk.

Actual result

All five links are returned as active by the settings catalogue, but Desk has no route for them. The router falls through to the catch-all and lands on /hq, which itself shows the "Headquarters – In Development" placeholder. The user is silently taken from Settings to an unrelated page.

Steps to reproduce — workflow editor deep link

  1. While signed in, paste desk.taviportal.com/settings/automation/workflow-rules/new into the address bar.

Expected result

The editor asks for a module, or defaults to Tickets.

Actual result

The heading reads "New Workflow Rule @ __no-module__", the trigger text reads "when a record in __no-module__ is created", and the page fires GET /api/v1/modules/__no-module__/layouts twice, receiving 404 both times. The editor opened from the Workflow Rules list is fine; only the direct URL is affected.

Additional notes

The dead links are Integration Configuration, Custom Actions, Usage Overview, Buckets & S3 and Storage Requests. The settings catalogue is returned by the settings hub endpoint with every entry marked active.

Environment

raw_module_items.name: Attach From Cloud crashes the whole Desk app to a white screen
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Opening the cloud-file picker from a ticket's Attachment tab throws an uncaught JavaScript error and unmounts the entire application. The screen goes blank, the address bar still shows the ticket, and only a browser reload recovers. Any unsaved reply draft on that ticket is lost.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Sign in to Desk and open any ticket.

  2. Select the Attachment tab.

  3. Click Attach From Cloud.

Expected result

A dialog explaining that cloud browsing is not available on this server yet, offering Browse Files as the fallback. The product already ships exactly that message.

Actual result

Within about one second the page is completely blank. The document body drops from 1,271 characters to zero and the application root is emptied, so the interface has unmounted rather than being hidden. The browser console shows the uncaught error "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')". Because the address bar is unchanged there is no indication of what happened.

Additional notes

Reproduced eight times across two independent browser sessions, in both the empty state and with seven files already attached. The following were each ruled out: an expired session, because a check of the signed-in user returned success in the same moment the blank body was observed and the page had rendered fully immediately before; a waiting confirmation dialog, because no dialog was present; a collapsed section, because the whole document body was empty; a click landing on the wrong element, because the resolved button was clicked directly and its text, enabled state and position were all verified; and a slow-loading route, because it reproduced after a fresh page load with a six-second wait, and again twenty minutes later. This is separate from NDC-1781, which records the cloud feature being unavailable — that is expected. Here the placeholder dialog itself crashes the application.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 23 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Contacts with no last name can never be edited from their record page
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Last Name is a mandatory field on the contacts module, but it is not shown anywhere on the customer record page. Any attempt to save from that page therefore fails validation. Eleven of the twelve contacts on the tenant have no last name, so eleven of twelve contacts cannot be edited at all.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open any ticket that was raised by e-mail and click the contact to open its record.

  2. Click the pencil on the Contact Information panel.

  3. Type anything into the Title field and click Save.

Expected result

The change saves, or the form shows the missing required field so it can be filled in.

Actual result

The save is rejected with an inline "Last Name is required." message and nothing is stored. The Last Name field is absent from the panel in view mode, in edit mode, and behind More actions then Edit, so there is no way to supply the value. The request the page sends carries only first name, e-mail, owner and title.

Additional notes

Reproduced three times on the same record, then confirmed independently against the schema and the live data. Last Name is marked required on the contacts module, and eleven of the twelve contacts hold only an approval status, an e-mail address and a first name. Creating a contact without a last name is itself refused, which confirms the field is mandatory on the server and not only in the form. Every affected contact was created automatically from inbound e-mail. The create form does show First Name, Last Name and Account, so the field exists — it is missing from the record page only. No customer record was modified during testing; the row version was unchanged afterwards. Related observation, likely the same cause: the Account field also renders nowhere on a customer record, including on contacts that do have an account.

Environment

Arbitrary text is stored in the ticket due date field. That value then feeds overdue calculations, date-based views and any automation that reads it.

raw_module_items.name: Comments on an activity can be added but never edited or deleted
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A comment added to a task, call or event is permanent. The comment has no edit or delete control, and there is no route behind the interface that would allow either. A typo, or a note added to the wrong record, cannot be corrected or removed.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open any activity from the Activities module.

  2. Add a comment on the Comments tab and save it.

  3. Try to edit or delete it.

Expected result

The comment can be edited and deleted, the way comments on a ticket can.

Actual result

Adding works and reports "Comment added.", but the saved comment carries no controls at all. This is not a control that appears on hover — the full markup of the comment was captured and contains none.

Confirmed independently at the interface level: the notes route answers "method not allowed" on the module path and "not found" on both activity paths, so the read, update and delete operations genuinely do not exist. Only the timeline feed returns the comments. This is not a permissions problem — the account used holds every Desk permission.

raw_module_items.name: Searching for a single underscore returns every ticket
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Searching for a single underscore returns the complete unfiltered ticket list rather than the tickets that contain one. The character is reaching the database as a wildcard instead of being treated as ordinary text.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the ticket list and search within the view for a single underscore character.

  2. Compare the result with no search term at all.

  3. Repeat with two underscores, and with "a" followed by an underscore.

Expected result

Only tickets whose text contains an underscore, or none at all.

Actual result

All 34 tickets are returned — identical to searching for nothing. By contrast two underscores, "a" plus underscore, and a percent sign each return zero results.

Additional notes

The pattern of results suggests the search term is placed into a pattern-matching query without escaping wildcard characters first. The practical impact is small — an agent cannot search for an underscore — but it shows how the query is assembled and the same handling may apply elsewhere.

raw_module_items.name: The attachment size limit shown to agents does not match the limit enforced
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The reply composer tells agents that attachments may total up to 25 MB, but the server refuses anything larger than 16 MiB. A file between the two limits passes the check in the browser and then fails on upload, after the agent has already waited for it.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open a ticket and start a reply.

  2. Attach a file of roughly 20 MB — the composer states the limit is 25 MB, so it is accepted.

  3. Send, or watch the upload.

Expected result

Either the file uploads successfully, or the limit shown matches the limit actually enforced so the agent is told before waiting.

Actual result

The browser accepts the file and the upload is then rejected, reporting that the declared size of 20,982,337 bytes exceeds the maximum allowed for an attachment, which is 16,777,216 bytes.

Additional notes

The real limit is 16 MiB per file. Reproduced twice through the interface and confirmed directly against the upload endpoint. Separately, the Attachment tab has no size check in the browser at all, so an oversized file there fails only after the full upload has been attempted — a 12 MB file took about seventy seconds with no progress shown.

Environment

raw_module_items.name: The ticket History records the creation event with the ticket's current field values
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The "Ticket was created" entry in a ticket's History tab does not report the values the ticket had when it was created. It reports the values the ticket has right now, and it updates itself every time a field changes. The result is that the History tab contradicts itself: the creation row and the change rows directly above it state different things about the same ticket at the same moment. An audit trail that rewrites its own starting point cannot be used to establish what a ticket looked like when it arrived, which is the main reason to keep one.

Steps to reproduce

1. Create a ticket with Status "Open" and leave Priority empty.
2. Open the ticket and change its Status to "On Hold".
3. Change its Status again to "Escalated" and set Priority to "High".
4. Open the ticket's History tab and read the bottom-most entry, "Ticket was created".

Expected result

The creation entry states the values the ticket was created with: Status "Open", and no Priority. Those values never change, because the event they describe has already happened.

Actual result

The creation entry states Status "Escalated" and Priority "high" — the values the ticket holds now. Reading upward from it, the same list correctly records "Status was updated, Old Open, New On Hold" and then "Status was updated, Old On Hold, New Escalated", so the History tab simultaneously says the ticket was created as Escalated and that it was changed from Open to On Hold to Escalated. Reproduced twice on two independently created tickets (#50 and #51).

Additional notes

The creation entry also prints the raw stored value "high" for Priority, where the corresponding change entry one row above prints the display label "High". The underlying data is correct: GET /desk/tickets/{id}/history returns a proper per-field audit with old_value and new_value on every change, so this appears to be the History view rendering the live record for the creation row rather than the values captured in the creation event.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: A Call can never leave a Completed or Cancelled status — it has no Reopen action
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A Call whose status is Completed or Cancelled can never be changed again. Both are terminal statuses with no way back: the record offers no Reopen action, and its Call Status control does nothing when clicked, so there is no route to any other status from the interface. An agent who completes or cancels a call by mistake has to abandon the record and create a replacement. Tasks and Events in the same situation both offer a way back, so the Call is the one activity type where a terminal status is permanent.

Steps to reproduce

1. Go to Activities, then Calls, and create a Call. 2. Set its status to Completed, or to Cancelled — either through the footer actions while the call is still scheduled, or through the API. 3. Open the Call and look for any way to change the status back. 4. Click the Call Status control in the left-hand properties panel. 5. For comparison, set a Task and an Event to Completed and to Cancelled and open each one.

Expected result

A Call in a terminal status is closed for editing, as it should be, and offers a Reopen action that returns it to an editable status — the same pattern Tasks and Events already follow. Once reopened, the status can be changed.

Actual result

The Call offers nothing. On a completed Call and on a cancelled Call alike, the detail page contains no Reopen action and no other action of any kind, and clicking the Call Status control has no effect at all — the page markup is byte-identical before and after the click and no dialog opens. Measured on a completed Call the page stayed at 35,435 bytes across the click, and on a cancelled Call at 38,089 bytes, with zero dialogs in both cases.

Every other activity type offers a way back. A completed Task offers Reopen Task, a cancelled Task offers Mark as Complete, and an Event offers Reopen Event when completed and when cancelled.

Additional notes

The Call Status control is inert in every status, not only the terminal ones — the same click on a scheduled Call is equally a no-op. While a Call is still scheduled that does not matter, because the footer offers Cancel Call, Mark as missed, Reschedule and Start Call; those four actions disappear once the call reaches a terminal status, and the inert control is then all that is left.

A second, opposite inconsistency is worth deciding on at the same time. Tasks and Events do not actually lock their status in a terminal state: clicking the status control on a completed or cancelled one opens the full status picker and allows a direct change, so their Reopen action can be bypassed. If the intended rule is that a terminal status must be reopened before it can change, then the Call needs a Reopen action and the Task and Event status pickers need to stop offering a direct edit. The All Activities list already treats status as read-only — its rows carry no status control at all.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: The ticket History shows only relative times, so the time of day of an audited change cannot be read
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Every entry in a ticket's History tab is timestamped in relative language only — "now", "1 minute ago", "20 hours ago", "yesterday" — and there is no way to obtain the actual time. Hovering an entry produces no tooltip. The date is recoverable from the day heading above each group, so what is lost is specifically the time of day. For an audit trail this matters more than it would elsewhere: establishing whether a status change happened before or after a customer's reply, or whether a change fell inside business hours, is exactly the kind of question the History tab exists to answer, and it cannot be answered here.

Steps to reproduce

1. Open any ticket with a few recorded changes and select its History tab.
2. Read the timestamp on any entry.

3. Hover over the timestamp and wait.

Expected result

The exact date and time are available, whether shown outright or revealed on hover, in the way the Conversation tab already displays "23/09/2026 03:09 ( yesterday )" for each message.

Actual result

Only relative text is shown. Inspecting the elements, each timestamp has a correct datetime attribute, but its title attribute is null, its aria-label is null, and hovering produces no tooltip — the count of [role=tooltip] elements on the page stays at zero. The day heading ("Today (Sep 24)", "Yesterday (Sep 23)") gives the date, so only the time within that day is unavailable.

Additional notes

The exact value is already present in the markup, so this is a presentation gap rather than missing data — the datetime attribute carries full precision, for example 2026-09-24T07:09:55.168299+00:00. The Conversation tab on the same ticket shows both an absolute and a relative time together, which is a reasonable pattern to copy.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: An account record has no Contracts tab, so a contract linked to it cannot be reached from the account
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

An account record shows no Contracts tab, so a contract that belongs to an account cannot be reached from that account. The Contracts module exists and is reachable from the More modules menu, and a contract stores the account it belongs to, so the relationship is modelled — it is simply not surfaced on the account side. The account record does carry a Contacts tab for its other relationship, which makes the omission look like an oversight rather than a deliberate decision.

Steps to reproduce

1. Go to Customers, then Accounts, and open an account. 2. Read the tab strip. 3. Create a contract against that account — through the Contracts module, or via POST /modules/{contracts}/records with account_id set to the account. 4. Reopen the account record and read the tab strip again.

Expected result

The account record offers a Contracts tab listing the contracts linked to it, alongside the Contacts tab that already lists its contacts.

Actual result

The tab strip is Overview, History, Activities, Ticket Interaction, Tickets, Time Entry and Contacts, with no Contracts tab, both before and after a contract is linked. The linked contract was created successfully (HTTP 201, with account_id set to the account under test), so the absence is not a consequence of the module being empty.

Additional notes

This contradicts NDC-1783, which was written on 22 September and records Contracts as one of the tabs "present today", along with CRM and Related. None of those three is present now, while Ticket Interaction, Time Entry and Happiness Rating — listed there as in development — do render as working tabs. The tab set has clearly moved since that ticket was written, so it is worth re-checking NDC-1783 against the current build rather than treating this one as a duplicate of it.

Summary
An account record shows no Contracts tab, so a contract that belongs to an account cannot be reached from that account. The Contracts module exists and is reachable from the More modules menu, and a contract stores the account it belongs to, so the relationship is modelled — it is simply not surfaced on the account side. The account record does carry a Contacts tab for its other relationship, which makes the omission look like an oversight rather than a deliberate decision.
Steps to reproduce
1. Go to Customers, then Accounts, and open an account. 2. Read the tab strip. 3. Create a contract against that account — through the Contracts module, or via POST /modules/{contracts}/records with account_id set to the account. 4. Reopen the account record and read the tab strip again.
Expected result
The account record offers a Contracts tab listing the contracts linked to it, alongside the Contacts tab that already lists its contacts.
Actual result
The tab strip is Overview, History, Activities, Ticket Interaction, Tickets, Time Entry and Contacts, with no Contracts tab, both before and after a contract is linked. The linked contract was created successfully (HTTP 201, with account_id set to the account under test), so the absence is not a consequence of the module being empty.
Additional notes
This contradicts NDC-1783, which was written on 22 September and records Contracts as one of the tabs "present today", along with CRM and Related. None of those three is present now, while Ticket Interaction, Time Entry and Happiness Rating — listed there as in development — do render as working tabs. The tab set has clearly moved since that ticket was written, so it is worth re-checking NDC-1783 against the current build rather than treating this one as a duplicate of it.
Environment
desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: The Conversation tab renders the raw translation key tickets.conversation.showQuoted instead of a label
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

On the Conversation tab of a ticket, the control that expands quoted text is labelled with its own translation key, "tickets.conversation.showQuoted", rather than with any wording a user would recognise. It appears once under every reply that carries quoted text, so a ticket with a normal back-and-forth shows it repeatedly, in the most-used view in the product.

Steps to reproduce

1. Open a ticket whose conversation contains at least one reply quoting an earlier message — ticket #18 on staging has three.
2. Select the Conversation tab.
3. Scroll to any reply that includes quoted text and read the label beneath it.

Expected result

The control reads something like "Show quoted text".

Actual result

The control reads "tickets.conversation.showQuoted". Three occurrences on ticket #18, one per reply carrying quoted text.

Additional notes

The key resolving to itself is the usual sign of a missing entry in the translation file rather than a fault in the view. The interface language was left at the default English throughout.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: E-mail and phone fields accept invalid values through the API
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The browser rejects malformed e-mail addresses and phone numbers and sends no request, but the same values are stored without complaint when they arrive through the API. Data entered by any other route — an integration, an import, an automation — is therefore unvalidated.

Steps to reproduce

1. Update a ticket record through the API, setting the e-mail field to "qa.desk@". 2. Repeat with "@example.com" and with "qa@example". 3. Repeat with the phone field set to "abc", then to a single plus sign. 4. Read the record back.

Expected result

Each value is rejected with a validation error, matching what the browser already does.

Actual result

Every value is accepted and stored exactly as sent. Reading the record back returns "qa.desk@", "qa@example", "abc" and "+" unchanged.

Additional notes

Five of five attempts stored successfully, on a ticket created for the test and deleted afterwards. This gap is specific to the free-text-backed field types. The same testing confirmed that validation elsewhere works correctly: eleven of eleven out-of-range values for status and the other pick lists were rejected, and read-only fields including the ticket number, CRM deal, created-by and resolution were all correctly refused. So the server does validate — it just does not validate e-mail, phone or date fields.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 23 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Reply All after a Forward copies the forward recipient and quotes the private forward to the customer
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

After an agent forwards a ticket to someone else, clicking Reply All adds that person to Cc and puts the agent's private forward note into the reply. If the agent sends it, the customer sees the private note and the other person gets the customer's email.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open a ticket that has a customer email.
  2. Click the arrow next to Reply All and choose Forward.
  3. Enter any other email address, type a short note, and click Send.
  4. Click Reply All on the same ticket.
  5. Look at the Cc field and at the text in the editor.

Expected result

Reply All goes only to the customer and the people already copied on the customer's emails. The forward address is not added, and the forward note is not included.

Actual result

The forward address is added to Cc, and the reply text starts with the private forward note.

Additional notes

The forward is saved as not public (is_public = false), but Reply All still uses it to build Cc and the quoted text. Still happening on the 29 September retest (QA ticket #82).

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Editing a receiving email address always fails with "That operation is not available on this resource"
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

You cannot edit an email address in Settings. Every save fails with an error, so the display name, the department and the acknowledgement option can't be changed.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Email → Addresses.
  2. Click the ⋮ menu on any address and choose Edit.
  3. Change the Display name and click Save.

Expected result

The change is saved.

Actual result

The error "That operation is not available on this resource." appears. The panel stays open and nothing is saved.

Additional notes

The page sends PUT /desk/channels/addresses/{id} and the server answers 405 (method not allowed). The same change sent as PATCH works, so the page and the server use different methods.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: The Suppressions tab always shows "Nothing is suppressed" even when addresses are suppressed
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The Suppressions page is always empty, even when some addresses are suppressed. Admins can't see those addresses or release them.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Make sure at least one address is suppressed (for example, one that bounced).
  2. Go to Settings → Email → Suppressions.

Expected result

Every suppressed address is listed with the reason, the date and a Release button.

Actual result

The page shows "Nothing is suppressed". But the page's own request returns 2 suppressed addresses.

Additional notes

GET /desk/channels/suppressions?limit=50 returns 200 with the list directly in data, but the page reads data.items, so it always sees an empty list. This also matters because when a reply fails, the error message tells the agent to release the address on this page.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Add address accepts invalid email addresses that cannot receive mail
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Add address accepts email addresses that are not valid and can never receive mail.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Email → Addresses → Add address → Create an address on help.taviportal.com.
  2. In Address, type 70 letters "x", pick a department and click Save.
  3. Do it again with the address qa..dots (two dots in a row).

Expected result

Both are refused with a clear message. The part before @ can have at most 64 characters, and it can't have two dots in a row or start or end with a dot.

Actual result

Both addresses are saved and shown as "Receives · Hosted here".

Additional notes

POST /desk/channels/addresses returns 201 for both. Spaces, @ in the name, and duplicate addresses are already refused correctly. The QA addresses were deleted after the test.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: One suppressed Cc address stops the whole reply, so the customer gets nothing
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

If one address in a reply is suppressed, the whole reply fails and the customer gets nothing.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Have one address on the suppression list (for example, one that bounced before).
  2. Open a ticket and click Reply. Keep the customer in Recipients.
  3. Add the suppressed address in Cc, type a message and click Send.

Expected result

The reply goes to the customer. The suppressed address is skipped and the agent is told about it, or the agent is warned before sending.

Actual result

The whole reply is rejected and marked Failed, so the customer receives nothing. There is no warning before sending.

Additional notes

POST /desk/tickets/{id}/replies returns 422: "Email to … is suppressed … release it in the suppression list." That list is always empty in the UI (see NDC-1840), so the agent has no way to fix this.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Forwarding a ticket conversation leaves out the attachments of the forwarded messages
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When an agent forwards a ticket, the files attached to the earlier messages are not included. The person receiving the forward reads about a file they never get.

Steps to reproduce

  1. On a ticket, send a reply with a file attached.
  2. Click the arrow next to Reply All and choose Forward.
  3. Look below the editor for attachments, then send the forward.

Expected result

The attachments are included in the forward, or offered to the agent, like in normal email apps.

Actual result

The forward shows no attachments, and it is sent with 0 files. The reply it quotes has 1 file.

Additional notes

The agent can attach the file again by hand, so no data is lost, but it is easy to miss.

Environment

raw_module_items.name: PRD: Zoho Desk ↔ SalesIQ Integration
raw_module_items.description_html:
PRD: Zoho Desk ↔ SalesIQ Integration

Reference source: Integrating Zoho Desk with Zoho SalesIQ (Zoho official help documentation)
Parity scope: This spec mirrors Zoho's observed behavior for the Desk↔SalesIQ integration. No net-new capabilities or improvements are proposed.

Problem Statement

Support agents using our live-chat module today have no connection to our helpdesk ticketing system. When a chat reveals an issue that needs tracking, follow-up, or escalation, agents must manually re-key the conversation into a ticket, losing chat context (transcript, visitor identity, prior history) in the process. Missed chats disappear entirely, with no ticket created to catch the dropped request. Agents also have no visibility into a visitor's support history while chatting, so they can't tell if this is a repeat issue, an already-open ticket, or a first contact. The cost of not solving this is duplicated agent work, lost missed-chat volume, and support interactions that lack the account context needed to resolve issues efficiently.

Goals

  • Agents can convert any chat into a helpdesk ticket in a single action, without leaving the chat window

  • Missed chats are automatically captured as tickets so no customer request is silently dropped

  • Agents see a visitor's account and ticket context (open tickets, overdue tickets, account/SLA/contract info) inline during a chat

  • Knowledge base content authored once in the helpdesk system is reusable inside the chat widget without duplicate authoring

  • Chats and tickets route to the correct team automatically via department mapping, without manual agent triage

Non-Goals

  • Building a new ticketing system or knowledge base editor inside the chat product — this integration connects to the existing helpdesk system, it does not replace it

  • Two-way live editing of knowledge base articles from inside the chat product — articles remain read-only/preview-only in the chat surface; authoring stays in the helpdesk system

  • Voice/telephony integration (call log and call summary sync) — out of scope for this phase; flagged as a P2 future consideration since Zoho supports it, but it depends on a call/CRM module we have not specced

  • CRM-side lead/contact record sync — Zoho's later features push call data into CRM contact records; we have no CRM module in scope, so this is excluded entirely, not deferred

  • Cross-portal support (linking a chat account to more than one helpdesk portal at a time) — matches Zoho's own one-to-one account linking model

User Stories

As a system administrator

  • As an administrator, I want to link my chat account to our helpdesk account using a shared login email, so that the two systems can share data securely

  • As an administrator, I want the permissions I hold in the helpdesk account to carry over to the chat account automatically, so that I don't have to configure access twice

  • As an administrator, I want to be prompted to re-link if the connected helpdesk account is deleted or disabled, so that the integration never fails silently

  • As an administrator, I want to disable or re-enable the integration at any time, so that I can pause data sharing if needed

As a support team lead

  • As a team lead, I want to configure which chats get auto-converted into tickets (all chats, only attended chats, only missed chats, or none), so that ticket volume matches our team's workflow

  • As a team lead, I want to choose whether a chat converts to a ticket when it's answered or when it ends, so that ticket creation timing matches our process

  • As a team lead, I want to set whether auto-converted tickets start as Open or Closed, so that ticket status reflects whether follow-up is actually needed

  • As a team lead, I want to map each chat department to a helpdesk department (or mark it read-only, unmapped, or "choose on demand"), so that tickets land with the right team

  • As a team lead, I want new chat departments to auto-map to a matching helpdesk department by name, so that I don't have to configure routing manually every time a department is added

As a support agent

  • As an agent, I want to convert a chat into a ticket with one click from the chat window, so that I don't have to re-type the conversation into the helpdesk system

  • As an agent working in a "choose on demand" department, I want to set the priority, status, classification, and destination department when converting a chat, so that the ticket is triaged correctly from the start

  • As an agent, I want to see a visitor's recent tickets, account name, SLA name, contract name, contact owner, total ticket count, and overdue ticket count in the chat sidebar, so that I understand their support history before responding

  • As an agent, I want to search helpdesk tickets by visitor name, ticket number, email, or subject from inside the chat window, so that I can find related context without switching tools

  • As an agent, I want to reopen or close an existing ticket from inside the chat window, so that I can resolve related-issue conversations without creating duplicate tickets

  • As an agent, I want to associate my current chat with an existing ticket, so that repeat conversations about the same issue merge into one thread instead of fragmenting

  • As an agent, I want to edit ticket details (status, due date, notes, replies) directly inside the chat window, so that I don't have to context-switch to the helpdesk system for routine updates

  • As an agent, if a visitor's email isn't captured automatically, I want to manually enter it before converting the chat, so that the ticket still gets created and linked to the right visitor

  • As an agent, I want visitor and helpdesk tags to sync in both directions, so that categorization stays consistent whichever tool I tag from

  • Error/edge case: As an agent, if a chat has no visitor email and I don't add one, I want to see a clear message that the chat cannot be converted yet, rather than a silent failure

As a support agent (knowledge base)

  • As an agent, I want published helpdesk knowledge base articles to appear as searchable articles inside the chat widget, so that visitors get self-service answers without us duplicating content

  • As an agent, I want to preview a synced article inside the chat product, so that I can confirm it displays correctly before pointing a visitor to it

  • Error/edge case: As an agent, if an article hasn't synced yet or was saved as a draft, I want it to simply not appear in the chat widget yet, rather than showing broken or partial content

Requirements

Must-Have (P0)

1. Account linking

  • Administrator can link the chat account to a helpdesk account from Settings, using a shared account email

  • On successful link, the helpdesk portal name and the linking administrator's name are visible in settings

  • If no helpdesk account exists for the email, linking fails with a clear message (no silent failure)

  • If the linking administrator's helpdesk account is later deleted or disabled, the system prompts for re-linking

  • Administrator can change the linked helpdesk portal, and can disable/re-enable the integration at any time

Acceptance criteria:

  • Given an admin with matching helpdesk and chat account emails, when they click "Add" on the integration settings, then the accounts link and the portal name displays in settings

  • Given an admin with no helpdesk account, when they attempt to link, then linking fails with an explanatory error

  • Given a linked integration where the linking admin's helpdesk account is disabled, when any user views integration settings, then a re-link prompt is shown

2. Chat-to-ticket conversion — automatic

  • Team lead can configure which chats auto-convert to tickets: All Chats, Attended Chats, Missed Chats, or None

  • Team lead can configure the conversion trigger: on answering the chat, or on ending the chat

  • Team lead can configure the default status of auto-created tickets: Open or Closed

  • Team lead can enable syncing of visitor post-chat feedback into the created ticket

Acceptance criteria:

  • Given "Missed Chats" is selected, when a chat goes unanswered, then a ticket is automatically created in the helpdesk system

  • Given "None" is selected, when any chat ends, then no ticket is automatically created

  • Given the trigger is set to "While Ending Chat," when a chat ends, then the ticket is created at that point, not while still active

3. Chat-to-ticket conversion — manual

  • Agent can convert any active or ended chat into a ticket via a single control in the chat window

  • If the visitor's email is missing, agent can manually add visitor name, email, and phone number, then convert

  • Converted tickets are viewable both in the helpdesk portal and inline in the chat product

Acceptance criteria:

  • Given an agent is chatting with a visitor with a known email, when the agent clicks "Convert Chat as Ticket" and saves, then a ticket is created and viewable in both systems

  • Given a visitor has no email on file, when the agent attempts conversion, then conversion is blocked until the agent supplies an email via the visitor-edit control

4. Department mapping

  • System detects helpdesk departments with names matching chat departments and auto-maps them on integration

  • Team lead can manually map each chat department to a helpdesk department, or set it to No Integration, Read Only, or Choose on Demand

  • New chat departments auto-map to a same-named helpdesk department if one exists, otherwise default to Choose on Demand

  • For "Choose on Demand" departments, agent can select priority (High/Medium/Low), status (Open/On Hold/Escalated/Closed), classification, and destination department at conversion time

  • "No Integration" departments cannot view or create helpdesk requests; "Read Only" departments can view but not create or edit

Acceptance criteria:

  • Given a chat department and helpdesk department share the same name, when the integration is first enabled, then they are mapped automatically

  • Given a department is set to "No Integration," when an agent chats in that department, then no ticket controls or ticket history are visible

  • Given a department is set to "Choose on Demand," when an agent converts a chat, then they are prompted to set priority, status, classification, and department before the ticket is created

5. In-chat ticket context and actions

  • Agent sees, in the chat sidebar: account name, SLA name, contract name, contact owner, total ticket count, overdue ticket count

  • Agent sees the visitor's recent tickets, and can open one to view details and any associated chat transcript

  • Agent can reopen or close a linked ticket from within the chat window

  • Agent can associate the current chat with an existing ticket (merge), rather than creating a duplicate

Acceptance criteria:

  • Given a returning visitor with prior tickets, when an agent opens the chat, then recent tickets and account metadata display in the sidebar

  • Given an agent viewing an existing request during a chat, when they click "Associate Chat," then the current chat is merged into that existing request rather than creating a new one

Nice-to-Have (P1)

6. In-chat ticket search

  • Agent can search helpdesk tickets by visitor name, ticket number, email, or subject from the chat sidebar

7. In-chat ticket editing

  • Agent can open a full ticket edit view inline (status, due date, ticket fields, notes, email replies) without leaving the chat product

  • Only agents who are also members of the linked helpdesk portal can access ticket editing

8. Scoped ticket views

  • Agent/team lead can choose whether the sidebar shows tickets from "All Departments" or only "Mapped Departments"

9. Knowledge base sync

  • Team lead can enable one-directional sync of helpdesk knowledge base articles into the chat widget's article section

  • Team lead maps helpdesk article categories to chat departments (one category maps to exactly one department)

  • Team lead selects audience for synced articles (All Users, Registered Users, or Both) and initial status (published or draft)

  • Team lead sets sync frequency (Daily, Weekly, Monthly) with time and time zone, plus a manual "Sync Now"

  • Synced articles are tagged to indicate their helpdesk origin and always arrive as drafts requiring publish

  • Only articles in the supported language set sync; unsupported-language articles are silently excluded

  • Article display permission must be "All Users" in the helpdesk system for the article to be eligible for sync

10. Tag sync

  • Team lead can enable bidirectional sync of visitor/contact/lead tags between the chat product and helpdesk tickets

  • Tag changes in either system propagate to the other automatically once enabled

Future Considerations (P2)

  • Call log and call summary sync to helpdesk/CRM: Zoho supports pushing chat summaries, call logs, and call summaries into Desk as comments and into CRM lead/contact notes. This depends on voice/telephony and CRM modules we have not specced yet. Documenting now so the in-chat data model doesn't preclude adding a "push as comment" action later.

  • Multi-portal linking: Supporting more than one linked helpdesk portal per account. Not requested and adds significant complexity to department mapping; revisit only if a customer need surfaces.

Success Metrics

Leading indicators

  • % of eligible chats converted to tickets (auto + manual) within 30 days of launch — target 60%, stretch 80%

  • % of missed chats captured as tickets vs. previously lost entirely — target 95% capture rate

  • Time from chat end to ticket creation for auto-converted chats — target under 1 minute

  • % of agents who use in-chat ticket context (open the sidebar ticket panel) at least once per shift — target 70% within first month

Lagging indicators

  • Reduction in duplicate tickets (same visitor, same issue, multiple open tickets) — target 20% reduction within one quarter, measured via merge/associate-chat usage

  • Agent-reported time saved per ticket-worthy chat (survey-based) — target directional improvement, no numeric baseline yet

  • Support ticket volume attributable to "couldn't find agent/lost chat" complaints — target reduction, tracked via support ticket classification

Measurement method, exact query definitions, and evaluation cadence (1 week / 1 month / 1 quarter post-launch) to be defined with the analytics owner before launch — see Open Questions.

Open Questions

  • [Blocking — Engineering/Product] This integration assumes Departments and ticket layouts already exist as first-class concepts in both the chat product and the helpdesk product. Per the program-level prerequisite already flagged for this initiative, department mapping (Requirement 4) cannot ship until that foundation is in place. Confirm sequencing against the Departments/ticket-layouts workstream.

  • [Blocking — Engineering] Does our architecture support a real-time or near-real-time link between the chat product and helpdesk product (for live ticket sidebar data), or will this require a sync/polling model? This affects whether Requirement 5 can be "live" or must be "last synced at X."

  • [Blocking — Data/Analytics] Who owns defining the exact query and dashboard for the success metrics above, and what tool will source them?

  • [Non-blocking — Product] Should auto-converted ticket status default (Open vs. Closed) be a system-wide setting or configurable per department? Zoho's source docs describe it as a single account-wide setting; confirm we're matching that, not improving on it, per program guiding principle.

  • [Non-blocking — Legal/Data] Tag sync and knowledge base sync move customer data (tags, article content) between two systems automatically. Confirm no data residency or privacy review is needed before enabling by default.

  • [Non-blocking — Engineering] Supported language list for knowledge base article sync — do we adopt Zoho's exact 30-language list, or define our own based on what our helpdesk product supports?

Timeline Considerations

  • Hard dependency: Departments and ticket layouts (already flagged as a blocking prerequisite for the other specced features in this program) must exist before Requirement 4 (department mapping) and, by extension, most of P0 can ship. This integration cannot be fully implemented ahead of that workstream.

  • Suggested phasing:

    • Phase 1: Account linking, manual chat-to-ticket conversion, automatic conversion rules, basic department mapping (P0 items 1–4)

    • Phase 2: In-chat ticket context, search, associate/merge, reopen/close (P0 item 5, P1 items 6 and 8)

    • Phase 3: In-chat ticket editing, knowledge base sync, tag sync (P1 items 7, 9, 10)

  • No external hard deadline identified in the source material or provided by the user; timeline should be set once the Departments/ticket-layouts dependency has a resolved date.

PRD: Zoho Desk ↔ SalesIQ Integration
Reference source: Integrating Zoho Desk with Zoho SalesIQ (Zoho official help documentation)
Parity scope: This spec mirrors Zoho's observed behavior for the Desk↔SalesIQ integration. No net-new capabilities or improvements are proposed.
Problem Statement
Support agents using our live-chat module today have no connection to our helpdesk ticketing system. When a chat reveals an issue that needs tracking, follow-up, or escalation, agents must manually re-key the conversation into a ticket, losing chat context (transcript, visitor identity, prior history) in the process. Missed chats disappear entirely, with no ticket created to catch the dropped request. Agents also have no visibility into a visitor's support history while chatting, so they can't tell if this is a repeat issue, an already-open ticket, or a first contact. The cost of not solving this is duplicated agent work, lost missed-chat volume, and support interactions that lack the account context needed to resolve issues efficiently.
Goals
Agents can convert any chat into a helpdesk ticket in a single action, without leaving the chat window
Missed chats are automatically captured as tickets so no customer request is silently dropped
Agents see a visitor's account and ticket context (open tickets, overdue tickets, account/SLA/contract info) inline during a chat
Knowledge base content authored once in the helpdesk system is reusable inside the chat widget without duplicate authoring
Chats and tickets route to the correct team automatically via department mapping, without manual agent triage
Non-Goals
Building a new ticketing system or knowledge base editor inside the chat product — this integration connects to the existing helpdesk system, it does not replace it
Two-way live editing of knowledge base articles from inside the chat product — articles remain read-only/preview-only in the chat surface; authoring stays in the helpdesk system
Voice/telephony integration (call log and call summary sync) — out of scope for this phase; flagged as a P2 future consideration since Zoho supports it, but it depends on a call/CRM module we have not specced
CRM-side lead/contact record sync — Zoho's later features push call data into CRM contact records; we have no CRM module in scope, so this is excluded entirely, not deferred
Cross-portal support (linking a chat account to more than one helpdesk portal at a time) — matches Zoho's own one-to-one account linking model
User Stories
As a system administrator
As an administrator, I want to link my chat account to our helpdesk account using a shared login email, so that the two systems can share data securely
As an administrator, I want the permissions I hold in the helpdesk account to carry over to the chat account automatically, so that I don't have to configure access twice
As an administrator, I want to be prompted to re-link if the connected helpdesk account is deleted or disabled, so that the integration never fails silently
As an administrator, I want to disable or re-enable the integration at any time, so that I can pause data sharing if needed
As a support team lead
As a team lead, I want to configure which chats get auto-converted into tickets (all chats, only attended chats, only missed chats, or none), so that ticket volume matches our team's workflow
As a team lead, I want to choose whether a chat converts to a ticket when it's answered or when it ends, so that ticket creation timing matches our process
As a team lead, I want to set whether auto-converted tickets start as Open or Closed, so that ticket status reflects whether follow-up is actually needed
As a team lead, I want to map each chat department to a helpdesk department (or mark it read-only, unmapped, or "choose on demand"), so that tickets land with the right team
As a team lead, I want new chat departments to auto-map to a matching helpdesk department by name, so that I don't have to configure routing manually every time a department is added
As a support agent
As an agent, I want to convert a chat into a ticket with one click from the chat window, so that I don't have to re-type the conversation into the helpdesk system
As an agent working in a "choose on demand" department, I want to set the priority, status, classification, and destination department when converting a chat, so that the ticket is triaged correctly from the start
As an agent, I want to see a visitor's recent tickets, account name, SLA name, contract name, contact owner, total ticket count, and overdue ticket count in the chat sidebar, so that I understand their support history before responding
As an agent, I want to search helpdesk tickets by visitor name, ticket number, email, or subject from inside the chat window, so that I can find related context without switching tools
As an agent, I want to reopen or close an existing ticket from inside the chat window, so that I can resolve related-issue conversations without creating duplicate tickets
As an agent, I want to associate my current chat with an existing ticket, so that repeat conversations about the same issue merge into one thread instead of fragmenting
As an agent, I want to edit ticket details (status, due date, notes, replies) directly inside the chat window, so that I don't have to context-switch to the helpdesk system for routine updates
As an agent, if a visitor's email isn't captured automatically, I want to manually enter it before converting the chat, so that the ticket still gets created and linked to the right visitor
As an agent, I want visitor and helpdesk tags to sync in both directions, so that categorization stays consistent whichever tool I tag from
Error/edge case: As an agent, if a chat has no visitor email and I don't add one, I want to see a clear message that the chat cannot be converted yet, rather than a silent failure
As a support agent (knowledge base)
As an agent, I want published helpdesk knowledge base articles to appear as searchable articles inside the chat widget, so that visitors get self-service answers without us duplicating content
As an agent, I want to preview a synced article inside the chat product, so that I can confirm it displays correctly before pointing a visitor to it
Error/edge case: As an agent, if an article hasn't synced yet or was saved as a draft, I want it to simply not appear in the chat widget yet, rather than showing broken or partial content
Requirements
Must-Have (P0)
1. Account linking
Administrator can link the chat account to a helpdesk account from Settings, using a shared account email
On successful link, the helpdesk portal name and the linking administrator's name are visible in settings
If no helpdesk account exists for the email, linking fails with a clear message (no silent failure)
If the linking administrator's helpdesk account is later deleted or disabled, the system prompts for re-linking
Administrator can change the linked helpdesk portal, and can disable/re-enable the integration at any time
Acceptance criteria:
Given an admin with matching helpdesk and chat account emails, when they click "Add" on the integration settings, then the accounts link and the portal name displays in settings
Given an admin with no helpdesk account, when they attempt to link, then linking fails with an explanatory error
Given a linked integration where the linking admin's helpdesk account is disabled, when any user views integration settings, then a re-link prompt is shown
2. Chat-to-ticket conversion — automatic
Team lead can configure which chats auto-convert to tickets: All Chats, Attended Chats, Missed Chats, or None
Team lead can configure the conversion trigger: on answering the chat, or on ending the chat
Team lead can configure the default status of auto-created tickets: Open or Closed
Team lead can enable syncing of visitor post-chat feedback into the created ticket
Acceptance criteria:
Given "Missed Chats" is selected, when a chat goes unanswered, then a ticket is automatically created in the helpdesk system
Given "None" is selected, when any chat ends, then no ticket is automatically created
Given the trigger is set to "While Ending Chat," when a chat ends, then the ticket is created at that point, not while still active
3. Chat-to-ticket conversion — manual
Agent can convert any active or ended chat into a ticket via a single control in the chat window
If the visitor's email is missing, agent can manually add visitor name, email, and phone number, then convert
Converted tickets are viewable both in the helpdesk portal and inline in the chat product
Acceptance criteria:
Given an agent is chatting with a visitor with a known email, when the agent clicks "Convert Chat as Ticket" and saves, then a ticket is created and viewable in both systems
Given a visitor has no email on file, when the agent attempts conversion, then conversion is blocked until the agent supplies an email via the visitor-edit control
4. Department mapping
System detects helpdesk departments with names matching chat departments and auto-maps them on integration
Team lead can manually map each chat department to a helpdesk department, or set it to No Integration, Read Only, or Choose on Demand
New chat departments auto-map to a same-named helpdesk department if one exists, otherwise default to Choose on Demand
For "Choose on Demand" departments, agent can select priority (High/Medium/Low), status (Open/On Hold/Escalated/Closed), classification, and destination department at conversion time
"No Integration" departments cannot view or create helpdesk requests; "Read Only" departments can view but not create or edit
Acceptance criteria:
Given a chat department and helpdesk department share the same name, when the integration is first enabled, then they are mapped automatically
Given a department is set to "No Integration," when an agent chats in that department, then no ticket controls or ticket history are visible
Given a department is set to "Choose on Demand," when an agent converts a chat, then they are prompted to set priority, status, classification, and department before the ticket is created
5. In-chat ticket context and actions
Agent sees, in the chat sidebar: account name, SLA name, contract name, contact owner, total ticket count, overdue ticket count
Agent sees the visitor's recent tickets, and can open one to view details and any associated chat transcript
Agent can reopen or close a linked ticket from within the chat window
Agent can associate the current chat with an existing ticket (merge), rather than creating a duplicate
Acceptance criteria:
Given a returning visitor with prior tickets, when an agent opens the chat, then recent tickets and account metadata display in the sidebar
Given an agent viewing an existing request during a chat, when they click "Associate Chat," then the current chat is merged into that existing request rather than creating a new one
Nice-to-Have (P1)
6. In-chat ticket search
Agent can search helpdesk tickets by visitor name, ticket number, email, or subject from the chat sidebar
7. In-chat ticket editing
Agent can open a full ticket edit view inline (status, due date, ticket fields, notes, email replies) without leaving the chat product
Only agents who are also members of the linked helpdesk portal can access ticket editing
8. Scoped ticket views
Agent/team lead can choose whether the sidebar shows tickets from "All Departments" or only "Mapped Departments"
9. Knowledge base sync
Team lead can enable one-directional sync of helpdesk knowledge base articles into the chat widget's article section
Team lead maps helpdesk article categories to chat departments (one category maps to exactly one department)
Team lead selects audience for synced articles (All Users, Registered Users, or Both) and initial status (published or draft)
Team lead sets sync frequency (Daily, Weekly, Monthly) with time and time zone, plus a manual "Sync Now"
Synced articles are tagged to indicate their helpdesk origin and always arrive as drafts requiring publish
Only articles in the supported language set sync; unsupported-language articles are silently excluded
Article display permission must be "All Users" in the helpdesk system for the article to be eligible for sync

Tag changes in either system propagate to the other automatically once enabled

raw_module_items.name: Adding an email provider saves invalid settings and credentials without checking them
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Email Providers saves wrong settings and fake credentials without checking them. The new connection is switched on right away and used for CRM staff email on that domain, so those emails can't be sent.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Email Providers.

  2. Under Browse providers, click Connect on SMTP server.

  3. Enter Host "not a host", Port 70000 and any sending domain, then click Connect.

  4. Click Connect on SendGrid, enter the API key "qa-fake-0929" and a sending domain, then click Connect.

Expected result

An invalid host and a port outside 1–65535 are refused. The credentials are tested before saving, and if the test fails, the admin is told and the connection is not used.

Actual result

Both are saved, switched on, and marked "Staff send from their own address in CRM". The status only shows "Not checked yet".

Additional notes

POST /mail/connections/smtp and /mail/connections/transactional both return 201. On 28 September the same happened with port 0, an http:// host, a bad Amazon SES login and region, and an unreadable Google Workspace key. Typing "abc" as the port only shows "One or more validation errors occurred." without saying which field. The QA connections were removed after the test.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Replace credentials adds a second connection and leaves the old one listed
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Replace credentials says it replaces the current connection, but it creates a new one. The old one stays in the list as "Off", so the same domain shows up more than once.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Email Providers.

  2. On an SMTP connection, click ⋯ and choose Replace credentials.

  3. Change the host and click Replace credentials.

  4. Look at Your providers.

Expected result

The same connection is updated, and only one row stays for that domain.

Actual result

A second row is added for the same domain. The new row is on and the old row is "Off". The count goes from 3 to 4 connections.

Additional notes

The page sends POST /mail/connections/smtp (create) instead of an update. Turning the old row back on silently turns the new one off. Sending isn't doubled, because only one connection per domain is active. The QA connections were removed after the test.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: SendGrid and Amazon SES connections are listed as "Bulk sending service"
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A SendGrid or Amazon SES connection is shown as "Bulk sending service" instead of its real name, so the admin can't tell which service it is. The connection check also talks about an SMTP server, even though SendGrid was connected with only an API key.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Email Providers.

  2. Under Browse providers, connect SendGrid (or Amazon SES).

  3. Look at the new row under Your providers.

  4. Click ⋯ on that row and choose Check now.

Expected result

The row says "SendGrid" (or "Amazon SES"), and the check message is about that service.

Actual result

The row says "Bulk sending service". Check now returns "the SMTP server closed the connection before answering".

Additional notes

Both services are saved with provider "transactional" (the real service is only in settings.service), which is probably why the name is lost. The QA connection was removed after the test.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, admin account.
