raw_module_items.name: Collaboration Integrations
raw_module_items.description_html:
Status: Draft

Model reference: Zoho Desk — Collaboration integrations (Slack, Zoho Cliq, Microsoft Teams, Zoom Meeting, GitHub, Zoho WorkDrive, Egnyte, Zoho Mail, Google Chat, GoToWebinar, Zoho DAP)

Author: Product/Eng

Last updated: 2026-09-19

Epic Description

Zoho Desk's "Collaboration" category isn't one feature — it's a dozen separate third-party apps (team chat, video meetings, file storage, dev issue trackers, and more) that all plug into the same surface: a ticket. Every one of them follows the same underlying pattern — install an extension, authorize it, scope it to departments/profiles, and it either (a) pushes ticket events out to an external tool, or (b) pulls content from an external tool into the ticket as an attachment/comment/link. Rather than building each integration as a one-off, this epic establishes a general integration framework other connectors can plug into, and ships one concrete connector end-to-end to prove it out.

Epic Goals

  • A single, reusable pattern for connecting external collaboration tools to a ticket: install → authorize → scope (department/profile) → configure → enable/disable/uninstall

  • Agents get ticket updates and can act on tickets (reply, comment, change status, assign) from outside the help desk, in the tool they're already working in

  • External artifacts (files, meeting links, dev issues) can be attached to a ticket and stay visible/linked without manual copy-paste

  • Admins retain full control: which departments/profiles can use a connector, which events trigger notifications, and the ability to disable or fully remove a connector without losing historical ticket data

Epic Non-Goals

  • Building all 12 of Zoho's listed integrations in v1 — this epic ships the framework plus one connector; the rest become incremental additions later (see Phasing)

  • Replacing the live chat ↔ ticket integration already spec'd separately — that's a different, deeper integration (chat-to-ticket conversion), not a "collaboration connector"

  • A public marketplace/extension store where third parties can submit their own connectors — this framework is for connectors we build ourselves, not an open ecosystem, for v1

  • Deep two-way sync (e.g., editing a linked GitHub issue's status from Desk and having it reflect back) — v1 is link/attach/notify, not full bidirectional state sync

User Stories

Support Agent

  • As an agent, I want to receive a notification in my team chat tool when a ticket in my department changes status, gets a comment, or is escalated, so I don't have to keep the help desk open to stay aware

  • As an agent, I want to reply to, comment on, or reassign a ticket directly from a chat notification, so I don't have to context-switch to the help desk for quick actions

  • As an agent, I want to look up ticket details from my chat tool using a simple command, so I can answer a colleague's question without leaving the conversation

  • As an agent, I want to schedule or start a video meeting directly from a ticket, with the meeting link and details automatically recorded on the ticket, so I don't lose that context later

  • As an agent, I want to attach a file from our shared drive to a ticket reply without downloading and re-uploading it, so sharing documentation is fast

  • As an agent, I want to link a ticket to an issue in our dev tracker, so support and engineering are working from the same reference instead of duplicate records

Admin

  • As an admin, I want to install a connector and scope it to specific departments and agent profiles, so only the relevant teams have access

  • As an admin, I want to choose which ticket events trigger notifications through a given connector, so we don't create noise for events nobody needs to react to

  • As an admin, I want to map departments to specific external channels/spaces (e.g., department X → chat channel Y), so notifications land with the right team

  • As an admin, I want to disable a connector without deleting its historical data, and separately be able to fully uninstall it, so I have a safe way to pause an integration before committing to removing it

Sub-Item 1: Integration Framework & Connector Management

As an admin, I want a consistent way to install, authorize, configure, and remove any collaboration connector, so adding a new integration in the future doesn't require a bespoke settings experience.

Requirements

  • A connector registry/settings area (e.g., Setup → Integrations) listing available and installed connectors

  • Standard install flow: select connector → review what data it will access → authorize (OAuth or equivalent) → scope to department(s) and profile(s) → save

  • Standard state model per connector instance: Enabled, Disabled (paused, config retained, no new notifications/actions), Uninstalled (data/config removed, but past ticket references to it are preserved as historical record, not deleted)

  • Department-to-external-resource mapping support (e.g., one department → one external channel, or all departments → one shared channel) as a reusable configuration primitive

  • Event-based notification toggles: a defined set of ticket events (created, status changed, comment added, escalated, reassigned, nearing SLA/due time, happiness rating received) that any notification-style connector can subscribe to

  • Re-authorization flow for when an external token expires or needs refreshing, without requiring a full reinstall

  • Audit trail: who installed/configured/disabled/uninstalled a connector and when

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an admin installs a connector, when they scope it to one department, then agents outside that department cannot see or use it

  • Given a connector is disabled, when a ticket event occurs, then no notification is sent, but the connector's configuration remains intact for re-enabling later

  • Given a connector is uninstalled, when an admin views a ticket that previously referenced it (e.g., a linked file or meeting), then that historical reference is still visible, even though new actions via the connector are no longer possible

Open Question: Should the framework support multiple simultaneous instances of the same connector type (e.g., two different chat workspaces), as Zoho's Slack integration does? This affects the data model for connector instances vs. connector types.

Sub-Item 2: Team Chat Notifications & Actions

As an agent, I want ticket notifications and quick actions available in our team chat tool, so I can stay responsive without living in the help desk UI.

Requirements

  • Uses the framework from Sub-Item 1 for install/authorize/scope

  • Department-to-channel mapping: either all departments → one channel, or a one-to-one department-to-channel map

  • Configurable notification events per the shared event list (Sub-Item 1), delivered as channel messages and/or direct messages to the relevant agent (e.g., DM the ticket owner, channel-post for team-wide visibility)

  • Quick actions directly from a notification message: update ticket status, reassign/assign the ticket, send a reply, add a public or private comment — without opening the help desk

  • Command-based ticket lookup from within the chat tool (e.g., a slash-style command to fetch a ticket by ID, by customer email, or list the requesting agent's recent/overdue/due-today tickets)

  • Command responses are private to the requester, not posted to the whole channel, unless explicitly shared

  • First-time use requires the acting agent to authenticate; subsequent uses don't require re-login

  • A daily or configurable-interval summary feed (e.g., tickets opened/closed, satisfaction score, top performers) optionally posted to a channel

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given a department is mapped to a channel and notifications for "status changed" are enabled, when an agent changes a ticket's status, then a message appears in the mapped channel (or DM, per configuration) reflecting the change

  • Given an agent uses a quick action to reply to a ticket from a chat notification, when they submit the reply, then it's recorded on the ticket exactly as if sent from the help desk, including author attribution

  • Given an agent runs a lookup command for a ticket ID, when the command resolves, then only that agent sees the response, not the full channel

Open Question: Which chat platform do we build first — and do we need multi-platform support in v1, or is one sufficient to prove the framework (per the earlier decision to lead with one team-chat connector)?

Sub-Item 3: Video/Meeting Integration

As an agent, I want to schedule or start a video meeting directly from a ticket, so I can resolve issues that need a live conversation without losing the ticket context.

Requirements

  • Uses the framework from Sub-Item 1 for install/authorize/scope; authorization is per-agent (each agent connects their own video account) alongside the admin-level connector setup

  • "Meet now" (start immediately) and "Schedule" (set a future time) actions available from the ticket detail view

  • Meeting creation form pre-fills from ticket context: subject (from ticket subject), contact (from ticket's primary contact, editable), owner (defaults to ticket owner, editable)

  • Support for audio or video meeting type, participant selection (agents, ticket contacts/secondary contacts, or manually entered external emails), and a reminder setting

  • On creation, meeting details (link, ID, access code if applicable, scheduled time/duration) are automatically recorded on the ticket as a comment/thread entry — configurable as public or private, defaulting to a sensible choice (private, since access codes are typically not customer-facing content)

  • Once a meeting concludes, its record updates to reflect completion; a recording link is added if one is generated

  • Meetings can also be initiated from related views (e.g., an activity/calendar view tied to the ticket or contact), not only from the ticket detail page directly

  • Single active connection per agent per video provider (agents don't juggle multiple concurrent authorizations to the same tool)

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent clicks "Meet Now" on a ticket, when the meeting is created, then a comment with the meeting link and details is automatically added to the ticket

  • Given an agent schedules a meeting for a future time with the ticket's contact as a participant, when the scheduled time arrives, then the meeting can be started from the link recorded on the ticket

  • Given the connector is disabled, when an agent tries to schedule a new meeting, then the action is unavailable, but previously recorded meeting links/details on existing tickets remain visible

Sub-Item 4: File Storage Integration

As an agent, I want to attach or link files from our shared file storage directly into a ticket reply, so I don't have to download and re-upload documents that already live elsewhere.

Requirements

  • Uses the framework from Sub-Item 1 for install/authorize/scope

  • A panel accessible from the ticket detail view (e.g., a side panel/tab) that browses the connected storage account's folders and files

  • Two actions per selected file: Attach (embeds the file directly into the reply being composed) or Share Link (inserts a link into the reply, with a choice of access-permission level for that link — e.g., recipients of this email only, anyone in the org, only those with existing storage permissions, or anyone with the link)

  • A consolidated view of all attachments already present in the ticket's incoming conversations (i.e., what the customer has sent in), separate from what the agent is attaching from storage

  • Respects the storage account's own permission model — sharing a file via this integration should not silently override the storage tool's access controls beyond what the agent explicitly selects

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent selects a file from the storage panel and clicks Attach, when they send the reply, then the file is included as an attachment on the outgoing message

  • Given an agent shares a file as a link with "anyone with the link" permission, when the customer clicks it, then they can access the file without needing storage-account credentials

  • Given a customer sends an attachment in their reply, when the agent opens the file panel, then that incoming attachment appears in a distinct "incoming attachments" view, not mixed into the agent's own storage browser

Sub-Item 5: Dev Issue Tracker Integration

As an agent, I want to link a ticket to an issue in our development issue tracker, so support and engineering can reference the same record instead of maintaining duplicate ones.

Requirements

  • Uses the framework from Sub-Item 1 for install/authorize/scope, with an additional per-connector configuration for which external project/organization/repository to connect to

  • From the ticket detail view, an agent can: search existing issues by keyword and link one (or multiple) to the ticket, or create a new issue directly from the ticket (title, description, labels, assignee) which is simultaneously created in the external tracker and linked

  • Linking or creating an issue posts a record of that action to the ticket as a comment (configurable public or private, defaulting to private)

  • Agents can remove a link between a ticket and an issue from the Desk side; this does not delete the issue in the external tracker (one-directional removal)

  • A settings panel controls: whether linking-generated comments are public or private, which sections of tracker data are visible to agents, and which fields display when listing a linked issue

  • Optional: if commit messages in the external tracker follow a defined reference format tying them to a ticket ID, commit/file-change activity for a linked issue is surfaced on the ticket for context

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent searches for an existing issue by keyword and links it to a ticket, when the link completes, then the ticket shows the issue as linked and a comment records the action

  • Given an agent creates a new issue from a ticket, when it's submitted, then the issue exists in the external tracker and is simultaneously linked to the originating ticket

  • Given an agent removes a linked issue from a ticket, when they check the external tracker, then the issue itself still exists there, unaffected

Cross-Cutting Success Metrics

  • Adoption: % of eligible agents actively using at least one collaboration connector within 30 days of it being enabled for their department

  • Deflection: reduction in agents switching to the help desk tab purely to check ticket status, measured via time-in-app or a proxy survey

  • Reliability: notification delivery success rate above a defined threshold (e.g., 99%), and connector authorization failure rate tracked and alerted on

  • Framework reuse: time/effort to add the second connector after the first is shipped, as a proxy for whether the framework is actually general-purpose

Cross-Cutting Open Questions

  • [Product] Confirmed direction from earlier discussion: build the general framework first, with team chat notifications as the proving connector. Does file storage or video meeting integration follow next, or does that depend on which teams request it post-launch?

  • [Engineering] Do all connectors share one OAuth/token-management layer, or does each external provider's auth model (Slack OAuth vs. Zoom OAuth vs. a GitHub personal/org token) require enough divergence that the framework only standardizes the configuration layer, not the auth layer?

  • [Engineering] For quick actions performed via an external tool (e.g., replying to a ticket from a chat notification), how do we attribute and audit that action — same identity model as replies made directly in the help desk?

  • [Security] What data does each connector type need to expose externally (e.g., ticket subject and status in a chat notification vs. full ticket content)? This should be reviewed per-connector, since a video-meeting connector and a file-storage connector have very different data-exposure footprints.

  • [Design] Where does the per-ticket connector state (linked issues, attached-from-storage files, meeting history) live in the ticket detail UI — a shared "Integrations" panel, or connector-specific tabs?

Suggested Phasing

  • Phase 1 (Foundation): Integration Framework & Connector Management, plus Team Chat Notifications & Actions as the proving connector — validates the framework end-to-end with the highest-value use case.

  • Phase 2 (Expansion): File Storage Integration and Video/Meeting Integration — both are largely additive once the framework exists, and address distinct, high-frequency agent workflows (sharing files, hopping on a call).

  • Phase 3 (Specialized): Dev Issue Tracker Integration — valuable but narrower in audience (departments that work closely with engineering), so it's reasonable to sequence after the broader-reach connectors.

Agents get ticket updates and can act on tickets (reply, comment, change status, assign) from outside the help desk, in the tool they're already working in

Building all 12 of Zoho's listed integrations in v1 — this epic ships the framework plus one connector; the rest become incremental additions later (see Phasing)

Deep two-way sync (e.g., editing a linked GitHub issue's status from Desk and having it reflect back) — v1 is link/attach/notify, not full bidirectional state sync

raw_module_items.name: Ticket Replies
raw_module_items.description_html:
Status: Draft

Model reference: Zoho Desk — Ticket Replies

Author: Product/Eng

Last updated: 2026-09-19

Epic Description

Agents need a full toolkit for communicating on a ticket — not just a single reply box. This covers every way an agent (or customer) adds content to a ticket's conversation: formal email replies, internal-only comments, bulk actions across many tickets at once, time-delayed sends, delivery/read confirmation, reusable canned text, and control over who else sees or is looped into the conversation. Today, if our system only supports a single flat "reply" action, agents lack the tools to work efficiently at volume, communicate internally without noise to the customer, or guarantee a message lands at the right time. This epic brings ticket replies up to parity with a modern help desk's conversation layer.

Epic Goals

  • Agents can communicate both externally (replies, public comments) and internally (private comments, private threads) on the same ticket without context-switching

  • Repetitive work (identical replies/comments across many tickets, boilerplate text) is handled in bulk or via reusable snippets instead of manual retyping

  • Time-sensitive communication (replies that must land at a specific time, delivery/read confirmation) is supported natively

  • Every reply/comment action is auditable — who did what, when, and whether it was public or private

Epic Non-Goals

  • Real-time chat/messaging inside a ticket (that's live chat, covered separately) — this epic is about asynchronous, thread-based replies and comments

  • Multi-channel reply composition (SMS, WhatsApp, social) — this epic assumes email as the reply channel; other channels may reuse the same comment/thread model later but aren't in scope here

  • AI-generated reply drafting — out of scope for this epic, though snippets/templates should be built so a future AI-draft feature can plug into the same reply editor

Sub-Item 1: Private & Public Comments

As an agent, I want to add a comment to a ticket that's either private (internal-only) or public (visible to the customer), so I can collaborate with colleagues or give the customer a quick update without sending a full formal reply.

Requirements

  • Comment composer accessible from the ticket detail view (button + keyboard shortcut)

  • Toggle to mark a comment Private (default) or Public before posting

  • Private comments visible only to agents/admins with access to the ticket (including agents from other departments with ticket access)

  • Public comments appear in the customer-facing portal/help center, visible to the primary contact and any CC'd secondary contacts

  • Agents can edit or delete their own comments after posting

  • Comments support the snippet picker (see Sub-Item 5) for inserting reusable text

  • Comments can be pinned, with visibility set to "all agents" or "only me"

  • All comment actions (post, edit, delete, pin) are logged in ticket history with author, type, and timestamp

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent posts a private comment, when a customer views the ticket in the portal, then the comment is not visible to them

  • Given an agent posts a public comment, when the customer views the ticket in the portal, then the comment appears with the agent's name and timestamp

  • Given an agent edits or deletes a comment, when another agent views ticket history, then the edit/delete is logged

Open Question: Should public comments trigger a customer notification (email/push), or only appear passively in the portal? Zoho treats it as portal-visible without necessarily emailing — worth deciding based on our notification model.

Sub-Item 2: Mass Comments

As an agent, I want to add the same comment to multiple selected tickets at once, so I can communicate a shared update (e.g., an outage) without repeating myself ticket by ticket.

Requirements

  • Multi-select tickets from the ticket list view, then trigger "Comment" from a bulk action bar

  • Same private/public toggle as single comments

  • Support attachments, up to a defined cap (e.g., 10 per mass comment, matching Zoho's limit — confirm our own cap)

  • Comment only applies to tickets the acting agent has access to; others in the selection are silently skipped and reported back

  • Mass comments are queued and applied sequentially, not necessarily instantaneous

  • Permission-gated: off by default, enabled per role and per department by an admin

  • Blocked on tickets in a strict workflow/blueprint state that restricts edits outside a defined transition window

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent without permission attempts a mass comment, when they select tickets, then the bulk "Comment" action is unavailable

  • Given an agent selects 20 tickets and adds a mass comment, when the action completes, then all 20 tickets show the comment with correct visibility

  • Given 2 of the 20 tickets are outside the agent's access, when the action completes, then those 2 are skipped and the agent is shown which ones failed and why

Sub-Item 3: Mass Replies

As an agent, I want to send the same email reply to multiple tickets at once, so I can resolve a batch of similar customer queries (e.g., a known outage, a subscription reminder) efficiently.

Requirements

  • Multi-select tickets from list view, trigger "Reply" from bulk action bar, compose once, send to all

  • Only applies to tickets associated with an email address (not community, WhatsApp, Messenger, or similar non-email channels)

  • Respects existing CC on each ticket's last response — CC'd contacts also receive the mass reply

  • Hard cap on number of tickets per mass reply (define our limit; Zoho caps at 50)

  • Supports snippet/template insertion in the composer

  • Not available in an "All Departments" combined view — must be scoped to a single department's ticket list

  • Permission-gated (admin-only by default, extendable per profile) and requires "send email" permission as a prerequisite

  • A Mass Reply Log tracks every batch send, split into "Initiated" (queued, not yet delivered) and "Completed" (sent, with per-recipient delivery success/failure counts)

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent selects 50 tickets with email channel origin, when they send a mass reply, then all 50 receive the message and the action is logged in the Mass Reply Log

  • Given a selected ticket has no associated email address, when mass reply is sent, then that ticket is excluded and flagged

  • Given a mass reply partially fails, when the agent checks the Completed log, then they see how many of the total recipients received it

Sub-Item 4: Scheduled Replies

As an agent, I want to schedule a reply to send at a future date/time (or after a preset delay), so my response reaches the customer during their working hours regardless of time zone or my own availability.

Requirements

  • From the reply composer, agent can choose a preset delay (e.g., 10 min, 1 hr, 4 hr, 12 hr), a custom duration, or a specific date/time (with timezone selection)

  • Maximum scheduling window (define ours; Zoho allows up to 60 days out)

  • Auto-cancel-to-draft behavior: if the ticket is closed by the customer before the scheduled time, or if the customer replies first, the scheduled send is cancelled and saved as a draft instead of sending

  • A centralized "Scheduled Replies" view (per-agent "My Scheduled Replies" and, for leads/admins, "All Scheduled Replies") listing every pending scheduled reply with thread content, scheduled time, status, and ticket ID

  • From that view, agent can: send immediately, reschedule, clear the schedule (saves as draft), or send immediately + close the ticket

  • Mass actions on scheduled replies: select multiple and clear-schedule or send-immediately in bulk (define our cap; Zoho caps at 50)

  • Editing a scheduled reply pauses its countdown until the edit is confirmed

  • Notifications to the agent on scheduled-send success or failure (configurable)

  • Only available for tickets received via the email channel

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent schedules a reply for a specific date/time, when that time arrives and the ticket hasn't been closed or replied to, then the reply sends automatically and the agent is notified

  • Given the customer replies to the ticket before the scheduled time, when the scheduled time arrives, then the reply does NOT send and is instead saved as a draft

  • Given an agent has 3 scheduled replies pending, when they open the Scheduled Replies view, then all 3 are listed with correct scheduled times, soonest-relevant ordering, and status

Open Question: Do we need the "Ticket Peek" jump-to-thread behavior (deep-linking into a specific thread within a long ticket), or is opening the full ticket acceptable for v1?

Sub-Item 5: Snippets (Canned Responses)

As an agent, I want to save and reuse pre-written text blocks with dynamic placeholders (customer name, ticket ID, etc.), so I can respond quickly and consistently instead of retyping common answers.

Requirements

  • Create a snippet from within the reply/comment editor: name + content, with support for placeholders that resolve to live ticket/contact field values

  • Snippet name must be a single unambiguous token (no spaces) so it can be triggered via a text-expansion shortcut (type name + Tab to insert)

  • Define caps: max snippet count per org/user, max characters per snippet (Zoho: 200 snippets, 25,600 characters — confirm our own limits)

  • No image embedding inside snippets (text/placeholder content only) for v1

  • "My Snippets" (creator-owned, editable/deletable only by creator) vs. "Shared Snippets" (visible to others, permission-gated to share)

  • Snippet picker shows recently-used snippets for quick access, plus full search

  • Preview before inserting, showing creator and last-modified time

  • Usable in both replies and comments (public or private)

  • Permission-gated: "Share Snippet" is a distinct permission from basic snippet creation/use

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent types a snippet's exact name and presses Tab in the editor, when the shortcut resolves, then the snippet's content is inserted with placeholders replaced by the current ticket/contact's actual values

  • Given an agent without share permission creates a snippet, when another agent searches snippets, then the unshared snippet does not appear in their list

  • Given a shared snippet is deleted by its creator, when other agents who had access try to use it, then it's no longer available to them either

Sub-Item 6: Read Receipts

As an agent, I want to see whether a customer has read my outgoing reply, so I know whether to follow up or wait.

Requirements

  • Only applies to tickets originating from the email channel

  • Visual indicator (e.g., checkmark states) on each sent reply showing: delivered, read, partially delivered/read (for multi-recipient threads with To/CC/BCC), or bounced/failed

  • A detail panel ("Thread Read Info") showing per-recipient delivery and read status/timestamps

  • Bounce/failure indicator shown at the thread level only when delivery fails for every recipient

  • Feature is opt-in per department, toggled by an admin

  • Graceful degradation: some recipient email clients won't return read-receipt data (e.g., free-tier Outlook accounts) — the UI should reflect "unknown" rather than imply "not read" in these cases

  • Disabling the feature hides read receipts on both new and previously-tracked tickets

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given read receipts are enabled for a department and a reply is sent to a single recipient, when the recipient opens the email, then the reply's status updates from "delivered" to "read"

  • Given a reply is sent to 3 recipients (To + CC) and only 1 has read it, when the agent views the thread, then the status indicator reflects partial read, and the Thread Read Info panel shows exactly which recipient(s) read it

  • Given the recipient's email client doesn't support read receipts, when the agent checks status, then the UI shows an "unknown/unsupported" state rather than falsely indicating "not read"

Sub-Item 7: Secondary Contacts (CC) on Tickets

As an agent or customer, I want to add other people as CC on a ticket conversation, so relevant stakeholders stay informed without needing to be the primary contact or receive forwarded emails manually.

Requirements

  • Agents can add CC recipients from: the reply composer, the ticket detail/info panel, or the ticket form/layout

  • Customers can add CC recipients when submitting a ticket via the help center, or when replying by email

  • Cap on CC recipients per ticket (define ours; Zoho caps at 20)

  • Adding a new email as CC auto-creates a Secondary Contact record if one doesn't already exist

  • CC'd users get notified on: ticket creation, agent replies, public comments, and edits/deletions of public comments — not just inbound email replies

  • CC'd users can view and track the ticket independently via the help center (if help center access is enabled for that department)

  • CC'd users can submit happiness ratings after replies or on ticket closure

  • Feature is department-specific and admin-toggled; the CC field cannot be removed from a department's layout unless CC is disabled entirely for that department

  • Excluded from CC eligibility: deleted contacts, spam contacts, anonymous contacts, the support/from mailbox address, and agent addresses

  • Removing a CC address from a single reply's recipient list does not remove them from the ticket's CC field — that requires an explicit removal from the ticket detail page

  • CC field is preserved during ticket merges (agent chooses which original ticket's CC list carries over)

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given a customer adds a CC recipient while submitting a ticket, when the ticket is created, then that recipient is added as a Secondary Contact and can view the ticket in the help center

  • Given an agent removes a CC email from the reply editor's recipient field only, when they check the ticket's CC field afterward, then the contact is still listed there

  • Given two tickets with different CC lists are merged, when the agent selects which CC list to keep, then only that list carries over to the merged ticket

Sub-Item 8: Email-to-Ticket Conversion (Outbound)

As an agent, I want to send an email to a contact and have it automatically become a trackable ticket, so issues resolved over phone/chat still get logged, and proactive outreach is tracked.

Requirements

  • New "Send as Email" action from the ticket creation flow: select/create contact, enter subject + description, attach files, send

  • Resulting ticket is created with the sent email as its first thread

  • Supports snippets/templates in the outbound composer

  • CC recipients supported (cap TBD, e.g., 20); BCC not supported

  • Department signature auto-appended unless removed by the agent

  • Recipient does not get a separate "ticket created" acknowledgment — the email itself is the only outbound artifact

  • Permission-gated: requires both "Send Email" and "Create Ticket" permissions, enabled per department by an admin

  • Distinct from bulk/marketing sends (newsletters, campaigns) which should NOT create tickets — this flow is for one-to-one, trackable outreach only

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent uses "Send as Email" for an existing contact, when the email is sent, then a new ticket is created with that email as the opening thread and no duplicate customer record is made

  • Given the agent enters an email address with no existing contact match, when they send, then a new Contact record is created alongside the new ticket

  • Given an agent without "Create Ticket" permission attempts this action, when they try, then the action is unavailable

Sub-Item 9: Public & Private Threads

As an agent, I want a reply thread to be automatically or manually marked public or private based on who it's addressed to, so customer-facing communication and internal/external collaboration (e.g., with a consultant) stay properly separated.

Requirements

  • A thread is automatically marked public when its recipients match the ticket's primary contact and/or secondary (CC) contacts

  • A thread is automatically/manually marked private when addressed to someone who is not the primary or secondary contact (e.g., an internal peer or outside consultant)

  • All forwarded threads are private by default, regardless of recipient

  • Configurable setting (department-level, admin-controlled): auto-mark as private any thread not sent to the primary/secondary contact

  • Private threads are excluded from help center visibility and trigger no customer notification

  • Private threads still count toward response-time SLA calculations

  • Workflow automation can be triggered off private-thread events, same as public ones

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given an agent replies to a ticket addressed only to the primary contact, when the reply sends, then the thread is automatically marked public and visible in the help center

  • Given an agent forwards the ticket to an external consultant, when the forward is sent, then the thread is automatically marked private regardless of the recipient

  • Given the "auto-private for non-contact recipients" setting is enabled and an agent replies to someone who isn't the primary/secondary contact, when the reply sends, then it's automatically marked private without the agent needing to toggle it manually

Cross-Cutting Success Metrics

  • Adoption: % of agents using snippets, mass actions, and scheduling at least weekly within 60 days of launch

  • Efficiency: reduction in average handle time for tickets resolved via mass reply/comment vs. one-by-one baseline

  • Reliability: scheduled-reply success rate (sent as scheduled, without failure) above a defined threshold (e.g., 99%)

  • Data integrity: zero cases of a private thread/comment leaking into customer-facing views (tracked via support/bug reports)

Cross-Cutting Open Questions

  • [Engineering] Do comments and threads share one underlying data model (both are "thread entries" with a public/private flag and a comment/reply type), or are they architecturally distinct? This affects how read receipts, history, and mass actions are implemented across both.

  • [Product] Should CC notification behavior (Sub-Item 7) and read receipts (Sub-Item 6) be considered part of this epic's v1, or split into a fast-follow given they're more "visibility/tracking" than core reply composition?

  • [Legal/Compliance] Does our jurisdiction require any disclosure when read receipts are enabled, given they track recipient behavior?

  • [Design] Where do Scheduled Replies and Mass Reply Log live in the navigation — a dedicated section per department, or a global cross-department view for admins?

Suggested Phasing

  • Phase 1 (Core): Private & Public Comments, Public & Private Threads, Secondary Contacts (CC) — the foundational conversation model everything else builds on.

  • Phase 2 (Productivity): Snippets, Email-to-Ticket Conversion — agent-facing efficiency tools with lower technical risk.

  • Phase 3 (Scale & Tracking): Mass Comments, Mass Replies, Scheduled Replies, Read Receipts — higher complexity (queuing, scheduling infra, delivery tracking) and depend on Phase 1's thread/comment model being stable.

Agents can communicate both externally (replies, public comments) and internally (private comments, private threads) on the same ticket without context-switching
Repetitive work (identical replies/comments across many tickets, boilerplate text) is handled in bulk or via reusable snippets instead of manual retyping
Time-sensitive communication (replies that must land at a specific time, delivery/read confirmation) is supported natively
Every reply/comment action is auditable — who did what, when, and whether it was public or private

Real-time chat/messaging inside a ticket (that's live chat, covered separately) — this epic is about asynchronous, thread-based replies and comments
Multi-channel reply composition (SMS, WhatsApp, social) — this epic assumes email as the reply channel; other channels may reuse the same comment/thread model later but aren't in scope here
AI-generated reply drafting — out of scope for this epic, though snippets/templates should be built so a future AI-draft feature can plug into the same reply editor

Comments can be pinned, with visibility set to "all agents" or "only me"

Given an agent posts a private comment, when a customer views the ticket in the portal, then the comment is not visible to them
Given an agent posts a public comment, when the customer views the ticket in the portal, then the comment appears with the agent's name and timestamp
Given an agent edits or deletes a comment, when another agent views ticket history, then the edit/delete is logged

Permission-gated: off by default, enabled per role and per department by an admin

Given an agent selects 20 tickets and adds a mass comment, when the action completes, then all 20 tickets show the comment with correct visibility

Sub-Item 3: Mass Replies

raw_module_items.name: Web form: HTML typed by a visitor in Description is rendered in the agent's ticket view and loads outside images
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The Description field of a web form is plain text for the visitor, but the ticket view shows it to the agent as HTML. A visitor can put bold text, clickable links and images into a ticket, and any image address they choose is loaded by the agent's browser as soon as the ticket is opened. That works as a tracking pixel: it tells an outside server the agent's IP address and when the ticket was read. Script is not executed. The visitor's line breaks are also lost.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Embed any web form (feedback widget or advanced form) on a web page.

  2. As a visitor, type this in Description and send: line 1, a new line, <b>bold</b> <a href="https://example.com/qa">QA link</a> <img src="https://example.com/qa-pixel.png">

  3. As an agent, open the new ticket in Tickets.

Expected result

The description is shown exactly as typed, as text, with the visitor's line breaks. Nothing is loaded from outside addresses.

Actual result

The agent sees "bold" in bold, "QA link" as a working link to example.com and an image element. The agent's browser requested https://example.com/qa-pixel.png when the ticket opened (seen in the network log). "line 1" and the next line run together on one line. Tickets #81 and #84 show this.

Additional notes

The ticket subject is shown correctly as plain text, and the stored description is exactly what the visitor typed; only the display is wrong. Customer email and phone are masked in the screenshot.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Web form: a program file renamed to .png is accepted as an image attachment
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Web form attachments are checked only by their name and declared type, never by their content. A Windows program renamed to qa-photo.png is accepted, attached to the ticket and shown to the agent as a PNG image.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Take a small Windows program file (its first two bytes are "MZ") and rename it qa-photo.png.

  2. Attach it in a feedback widget and send the form.

  3. As an agent, open the ticket and go to the Attachment tab.

Expected result

The file is refused because its content is not a PNG image, as already happens for .exe, .zip, .svg and .html files and for a PNG named .exe.

Actual result

The upload and the submission both return 200. Ticket #91 lists qa-photo.png (202 B). Downloading it from the ticket returns Content-Type image/png with first bytes 4D 5A ("MZ"), and the agent view puts it in an image preview.

Additional notes

The file-type check on name and declared type works (SVG, ZIP, EXE, HTML, HEIC and generic binary are refused), so only the content check is missing. Customer email is masked in the screenshot.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Web form changes are not recorded in the Audit Log
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Creating, editing, turning on or off and deleting web forms leaves nothing in the Audit Log, and Web Form is not one of the entities the Audit Log filter offers. An admin cannot find out who changed or deleted a form that is live on the company website.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings, Channels, Web Forms.

  2. Create a feedback widget, edit it and save, turn it off and on, then delete it.

  3. Go to Settings, Security Control, Audit Log.

  4. Open the All Entities filter and search for "web".

Expected result

Each web form change appears in the Audit Log with who made it and when, and Web Form can be picked in the entity filter.

Actual result

Between 11:40 and 13:05 UTC about 100 web form changes were made (6 created, about 90 saved, 6 turned on or off, 3 deleted). raw_module_items.name: Web form: the "websites the form is on" restriction can be bypassed by claiming an allowed website
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A web form limited to certain websites decides where it is being used only from the website the caller claims. Any site or script that names one of the allowed websites can load the form and create tickets through it, so the restriction does not stop use from other sites.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create an advanced web form whose only website is http://localhost:4640.

  2. Embed it on a page at http://localhost:4641: nothing is shown, which is correct.

  3. From any other origin (for example https://evil.example), send the form's submission request with page_origin set to http://localhost:4640.

Expected result

Requests coming from a website that is not on the list are refused, whatever website they claim.

Actual result

The submission sent with Origin https://evil.example and page_origin http://localhost:4640 returned 200 and created ticket #87 "QA W2 spoofed origin". Loading the form with ?origin=http://localhost:4640 from the same origin returned the form (200).

Additional notes

In the browser the embedded form behaves correctly on listed and unlisted sites; the gap is only in what the server trusts.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium and direct API calls, 29 September 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Feedback widget embed code says it works only on listed websites when the website list is empty
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

For a feedback widget with no websites listed, the embed code dialog tells the admin the form works only on the websites in its settings. The widget settings say an empty list allows any website, and the widget does load on any website. The two messages contradict each other.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open a feedback widget's settings and leave "Only show on these websites" empty (hint: "Leave empty to allow any website").

  2. Save, then open its Embed code.

  3. Read the note "Test it on your website, not from a file".

Expected result

When the list is empty the note does not mention listed websites, or it says the widget works on any website served by a web server.

Actual result

The note says "The form works only on a page served by a web server from one of the websites in its settings", although there are none. The widget loaded on both http://localhost:4640 and http://localhost:4641.

Additional notes

For advanced forms the note is right, because they require at least one website. The embed code is masked in the screenshot.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 29 September 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Web form API returns internal .NET class names for values of the wrong type
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When a web form is saved with a value of the wrong type, the API answers with the server's internal .NET class names, namespaces and byte positions instead of a readable message about the field.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Send POST /api/v1/web-forms with department_id set to "not-a-uuid" (or null, a number or a list).

  2. Send PUT /api/v1/web-forms/{id} with definition.launcher.offset_px set to 2.5, or definition.default_owner_id set to "xyz".

Expected result

A 400 or 422 with a plain message naming the field, as the API already gives for an offset of -1 ("The vertical offset is between 0 and 2000 pixels.").

Actual result

400 with text such as "The JSON value could not be converted to MetadataEngine.Modules.WebForms.Infrastructure.Http.SaveWebFormWire. Path: $.department_id | LineNumber … | BytePositionInLine …", and the same for WebFormLauncherSettings and the definition class.

Additional notes

Same kind of problem as NDC-1407, now on the Web Forms endpoints.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com API, 29 September 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: An agent without the delete permission can still delete tickets through the API
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Non-admin agents do not have the ticket delete permission, and the Desk screens correctly hide Delete from them. But the same agent can delete any ticket they can see by calling the records API directly. The server does not check the permission on this route.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Sign in as a non-admin agent whose profile has no "desk:ticket:delete" permission (checked with GET /iam/me/permissions).

  2. Open a ticket and confirm the More menu has no Delete.

  3. Send DELETE /api/v1/modules/{ticket module}/records/{ticket id} with the agent's own session.

  4. Read the ticket again.

Expected result

403, the same as the mass-delete route returns for this agent. The ticket stays.

Actual result

204 and the ticket is deleted (GET returns 404). Reproduced on two agent accounts, several times.

Additional notes

Right after the delete, GET /desk/tickets/{id} still returned 200 with engine_deleted_at null for a short time. Only QA test tickets were used and they were cleaned up.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 4 October 2026, non-admin agent account.

raw_module_items.name: Ticket attachments can be downloaded by an agent who cannot see the ticket, including private and removed files
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The file download route only checks that the file belongs to the same company. It does not check whether the agent may see the ticket the file is attached to. An agent who gets 404 on a ticket can still download its attachments, including files marked Private and files already removed from the ticket.

Steps to reproduce

  1. As Agent A, attach a file to a ticket that Agent A owns (Agent B, in the same department, cannot open it).

  2. As Agent B, confirm GET /desk/tickets/{id} and GET /desk/tickets/{id}/attachments both return 404.

  3. As Agent B, call POST /files/{file id}/download.

  4. Open the signed link that comes back.

Expected result

403 or 404. File access follows the ticket's access.

Actual result

200 with a signed link, and the link serves the file. Seen for a public PDF, a TXT marked Private and a PNG that had been removed from the ticket. Reproduced several times, also on a Call Center ticket.

Additional notes

The file id has to be known, so the risk depends on ids leaking (links shared in comments, exports, logs). Evidence shows tokens as REDACTED.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 4 October 2026, non-admin agent account.

raw_module_items.name: A non-admin agent can edit and delete another agent's comment on a ticket
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Any agent who can see a ticket can rewrite or delete comments written by other agents. The menu offers "Edit comment" and "Delete comment" on other people's comments, and the server accepts both. The Ticket Replies spec (NDC-1851) says agents edit and delete their own comments.

Steps to reproduce

  1. As Agent A, add a comment on an unassigned ticket in the department.
  2. Sign in as Agent B (non-admin, same department) and open the ticket.
  3. Open the comment's menu: Edit comment and Delete comment are offered.
  4. Edit the text and save, then delete the comment.

Expected result

Only the author (or an admin) can edit or delete a comment.

Actual result

Agent B's edit returns 200, the body is replaced and edited_by becomes Agent B. Agent B's delete returns 204 and the comment is gone for Agent A. Neither change is written to the ticket History.

Additional notes

Both agents hold desk:ticket:manage, so the team may intend this; if so, please confirm and say so in the spec.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 4 October 2026, non-admin agent account.

raw_module_items.name: Images in a customer email load before "Show images" is clicked, so tracking pixels fire
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Ticket conversations show a "Show images" button, which suggests outside images are blocked until the agent allows them. They are not: the browser fetches the outside image as soon as the ticket opens. A sender's tracking pixel therefore learns when an agent read the email.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Have an email arrive as a ticket whose body contains an outside image (the Desk mailbox test message contains a SendGrid open-tracking image).

  2. Open the ticket and watch network requests. Do not click "Show images".

Expected result

No outside image is requested until "Show images" is clicked.

Actual result

About 5 seconds after load, the browser requests the SendGrid tracking image from the message frame, while "Show images" is still offered. Seen on 3 of 3 loads.

Additional notes

Related to NDC-1855 (outside images in web form descriptions), but this is the email conversation view.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 4 October 2026, admin account.

400/422. Status allows only Open, On Hold, Escalated and Closed; Priority only low, medium, high and urgent.

raw_module_items.name: Ticket API stores owner, contact and department ids that do not exist
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When a ticket is created through the records API, the owner, contact, account, product, contract and department fields accept any id, even ids that do not exist. The ticket then shows "Unknown user" as owner, and the department stored on the record differs from the department the Desk view shows.

422 naming the fields whose ids do not exist, the same way POST /desk/tickets/{id}/assign refuses an unknown user.

201. All three ids are stored. The ticket page shows Ticket Owner "Unknown user" and a "Not Found" toast; the Desk view silently shows techSupport as department.

Values like "not-a-uuid" are also stored. The assign route does validate the owner, so only the records route is affected.

Environment

raw_module_items.name: Ticket API lets an agent write system fields such as Created Time and add fields that do not exist
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

An agent can send system fields (created_at, created_by, modified_by, closed_at, merged_into_ticket_id) and made-up field names when saving a ticket through the API. They are stored inside the record and logged in History as changes, although the real system values do not change.

  1. As a non-admin agent, PATCH /api/v1/modules/{ticket module}/records/{id} with created_at = 2020-01-01 and qa_unknown = x (plus the required subject and status).
  2. Read the record back and open the History tab.

Expected result

System fields and unknown fields are refused or ignored, the way approval_status (422) and ticket_number (ignored) already are.

Actual result

200. created_at = 2020-01-01 and qa_unknown = x are stored as data fields, while the record's real created time stays 4 October 2026. History logs "Created Time was updated". Same for created_by, modified_by, closed_at and merged_into_ticket_id.

Additional notes

Reports or integrations that read the record data can be misled by these stored values.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 4 October 2026, non-admin agent account.

raw_module_items.name: Saving a ticket from an older tab silently undoes changes made in another tab
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A ticket save sends the whole record and replaces it, with no check that the record changed in the meantime. When two agents (or two tabs) edit the same ticket, the later save quietly wipes the earlier change.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the same ticket in tab A and tab B.

  2. In tab A set Priority to urgent.

  3. In tab B (still showing the old data) set Channel to phone.

  4. Reload and read the ticket.

Expected result

raw_module_items.name: A due date set on the New Ticket form is saved without a time zone
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The New Ticket form sends the due date as a local time with no time zone. Every agent then sees the same clock time whatever their zone, so the countdown ("Due in …") is wrong by the difference between zones. The ticket-page date picker does it correctly (UTC).

Steps to reproduce

  1. With the browser in Asia/Tokyo, open New Ticket and set Due Date to 1 March 2027 10:30. Save.

  2. Open the ticket in a browser set to America/New_York.

  3. Compare with a due date set from the ticket-page picker.

Expected result

The due date is stored as one moment in time (UTC) and shown in each agent's own zone.

Actual result

The request sends "2027-03-01T10:30" with no zone. Both Tokyo and New York show 01/03/2027 10:30, so the "Due in" countdowns differ by about 14 hours. A due date stored as UTC ("2027-03-01T10:30:00Z") shows 19:30 in Tokyo. The ticket-page picker stores UTC correctly.

Additional notes

Reproduced twice. Agent email masked in the screenshot.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 4 October 2026, agent account.

Closed Time is cleared on reopen.

Status is Open and the Desk view's closed_at is null, but the record field closed_time still holds the close time (e.g. 2026-10-04T09:27:01). Reproduced three times.

Views, filters and reports that use Closed Time will count open tickets as closed.

raw_module_items.name: Time entries are kept in two places that never match, so ticket time totals are wrong
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The Time Entry tab saves entries in the time-entry module, while the Desk ticket API keeps its own separate list of time entries. Neither side sees the other's entries, so the tab total and the ticket's total time disagree.

Steps to reproduce

  1. On a ticket, add a time entry on the Time Entry tab.

  2. Read GET /desk/tickets/{id} (counts.time_entries, total_time_seconds) and GET /desk/tickets/{id}/time-entries.

  3. Add an entry with POST /desk/tickets/{id}/time-entries and look at the tab.

Expected result

One list of time entries and one total everywhere.

Actual result

Fresh ticket: the tab shows 32:00:00 from two entries; the Desk API shows time_entries 0 and total_time_seconds 0. On another ticket the tab showed 7 entries (37:55:15) while the API listed 4 different entries (1,080 seconds). Entries made through the API never appear on the tab. The timer-stop entry appears on the tab but not in the API totals.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 4 October 2026, non-admin agent account.

raw_module_items.name: Custom view criteria cannot use OR, and a view with an OR pattern shows the wrong tickets
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The custom view dialog has no way to combine criteria with OR (its tooltip mentions "Edit Pattern", but no such control exists). A view saved with the pattern "1 OR 2" is stored correctly, but the list ignores the pattern and joins the criteria with AND, so it shows the wrong tickets.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create a custom view with criteria Priority = high and Priority = low and pattern "1 OR 2" (the API accepts and stores it).

  2. Open the view in Desk.

Expected result

The view lists tickets with priority high or low, and the dialog lets the user choose AND or OR.

Actual result

The list shows "(0)". The page sends filters=[priority high, priority low] without the pattern, so they are joined with AND. GET records?view_id=<id> on the server returns the 2 matching tickets for the same view.

Environment

desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 4 October 2026, admin account.

  3. Given two tenants, when a customer of one opens a link or id from the other, then nothing is shown.

  4. Given an agent without the right permission, when they open a setting page or call its API, then they are refused (403).

raw_module_items.name: Help Center (customer portal)
raw_module_items.description_html:
A portal where customers sign in, follow their tickets and read articles. Example: a customer signs in, sees ticket #1042 and reads "Reset password".

Phase 2. Needs first: template engine.

User stories

Written to match Zoho Desk's Help Center. Each story says who needs it, what they need and why, then numbered checks (Given / When / Then) that tell you when the story is done.

Story 1 — Turn on and set up the Help Center

As an admin, I want to turn on a Help Center and choose what it shows, so that customers have one place to get help.

  1. Given I open Setup → Channels → Help Center, when I turn it on, then the Help Center gets its own address that customers can open.

  2. Given I set the name, logo and colours, when I click Publish, then customers see the new look. Before Publish, customers still see the old one.

  3. Given I choose which departments appear, when a customer opens the Help Center, then only those departments are shown.

  4. Given I set the landing page to Home or to the Add Ticket form, when a customer opens the address, then that page opens first.

Story 2 — Sign up, sign in and reset password

As a customer, I want my own Help Center account, so that I can follow my tickets.

  1. Given I click Sign Up, when I enter my name, email and CAPTCHA, then I get an invitation email. The link works for 30 days.

  2. Given I open the invitation link, when I set a password, then my account is active and linked to my contact record (a new contact is made if none exists).

  3. Given I click Sign In, when I enter my email and password, then I am signed in. A wrong password shows a clear message and does not say whether the email exists.

  4. Given I click Forgot password, when I enter my email and CAPTCHA, then I get a reset code (works 15 minutes) and a reset link (works 6 hours).

  5. Given an agent opens a contact, when they click Invite to Help Center, then the contact gets the same invitation email.

  6. Given an admin turns off self sign-up, when a visitor opens the Help Center, then the Sign Up button is gone and only invited contacts can join.

Story 3 — Submit a ticket

As a customer, I want to send a request from the Help Center, so that I don't have to write an email.

  1. Given I open Add Ticket, when I choose a department, then I see that department's ticket form with its required fields.

  2. Given I fill the form and add a file, when I submit, then a ticket is created in that department with channel "Web" and I see its ticket number.

  3. Given I am not signed in, when I submit, then the ticket is created, but I am told to sign up to follow it.

  4. Given I am signed in, when I submit, then the ticket is linked to my contact and shows in My Area.

Story 4 — My Area: follow and reply to my tickets

As a signed-in customer, I want to see all my tickets in one place, so that I know where each request stands.

  1. Given I open My Area, when the page loads, then I can switch between My Tickets, My Open Tickets, My Closed Tickets, My On Hold Tickets and My Overdue Tickets.

  2. Given the list is open, when I search, sort or filter, then the list updates to match.

  3. Given I open a ticket, when the page loads, then I see its number, status, department and the whole public conversation. Private agent comments are never shown.

  4. Given I write a reply with an attachment, when I send it, then it is added to the ticket and the agent is notified.

Story 5 — Who can see which tickets

As an admin, I want to control which tickets a customer can see, so that customers never see someone else's ticket by mistake.

  1. Given default settings, when a customer opens My Area, then they see only tickets they raised.

  2. Given I turn on "Customers can view tickets of other users in their account" in Access Settings, and an agent turns on "Show tickets from other contacts" for a contact, when that contact opens My Area, then they also see tickets from other contacts of the same account. The per-contact switch is off by default.

  3. Given a department is hidden from the Help Center, when "Show tickets from hidden departments" is off, then its tickets do not show in My Area.

  4. Given a customer changes a ticket id in the address bar, when the ticket is not theirs, then they get "not found" and no ticket data.

Story 6 — My profile

As a signed-in customer, I want to manage my profile, so that my details stay correct.

  1. Given I open Profile, when I edit my name or phone and save, then the change is saved on my contact record.

  2. Given I change my password, when I save, then my other sessions are signed out.

  3. Given I click Delete account, when I confirm, then I can no longer sign in. My tickets stay in Desk.

Story 7 — Read articles in the Help Center

As a customer, I want to read help articles, so that I can fix simple problems myself.

  1. Given the Knowledge Base tab is open, when I browse or search, then I see only published articles I am allowed to see.

  2. Given an article is for registered users only, when I am signed out, then it is hidden. After I sign in, I can see it.

  3. Given an admin limits a category to a user group, when I am not in that group, then its articles are hidden from me.

Zoho reference

raw_module_items.name: Knowledge Base advanced: review, translations, feedback, import
raw_module_items.description_html:
The remaining Knowledge Base functions. Example: a disliked article turns the feedback into a ticket.

Phase 4. Needs first: Help Center.

Details — authoring and review

  • Turn on review for a category and choose its reviewers; email to reviewers when an article is sent for review; comments between author and reviewer.

  • In-app notification when an article is sent for review or gets a review comment.

  • Email reminders to the owner before an article expires (7 days, 1 day, on the day).

  • Article templates.

  • Compare any two versions and restore an old version.

  • Download an article as PDF.

Details — organisation

  • Drag-and-drop order of articles in a category or section, and a switch back to the default order.

  • Reorder categories and sections (drag-and-drop or A to Z).

  • More sub-section levels.

  • Share a category with other departments as read-only.

  • Article numbers, a choice of permalink format, and 301 redirects for old addresses.

  • Translations of articles and categories, manual and automatic, with an "outdated translation" flag.

  • Import many articles from a CSV or XLS file, one per row, placed in the named category.

  • Bulk actions on the list: move, change owner, tags or status, delete.

  • Recycle Bin for deleted articles.

  • Filter the list by display permission and by expiry date.

Details — visibility (needs the Help Center)

  • Visibility per section.

  • One switch that shows or hides the whole Knowledge Base in the Help Center.

  • One place per article that shows why it is or is not visible.

  • Like and dislike, with a feedback form on dislike that can become a ticket.

  • Customer comments on articles, with moderation and turning a comment into a ticket.

  • Follow an article or category and get an email when it changes.

  • Related articles (from tags), and popular and recent articles on the Help Center home page.

  • Sitemap for search engines.

Details — agents and insights

  • Suggested articles on the ticket, and insert an article (link or content) into a reply.

  • "Used in tickets" count per article.

  • Article insights: views by customer type and source, who liked or disliked, and article history.

  • Knowledge Base dashboard: views, likes, trending articles and searches, including searches with no result.

  • API for search, tags, bulk update, reorder, import, export, feedback and statistics.

User stories

Written to match Zoho Desk's Knowledge Base. One story per group of details above. Each story says who needs it, what they need and why, then numbered checks (Given / When / Then) that tell you when the story is done.

Story 1 — Review before publishing

As a Knowledge Base manager, I want articles in some categories reviewed before they go live, so that customers only read checked content.

  1. Given I edit a category, when I turn on Review and pick reviewers, then every new or changed article in it must be reviewed.

  2. Given an author clicks Send for Review, then each reviewer gets an email and an in-app notification.

  3. Given a reviewer adds a comment, then the author is notified and can reply on the article.

  4. Given the reviewer approves, then the article is published. If they reject it, it goes back to Draft with the comment.

Story 2 — Expiry reminders

As an article owner, I want reminders before my article expires, so that I update it in time.

  1. Given an article has an expiry date, when it is 7 days away, 1 day away and on the day, then the owner gets an email each time.

  2. Given the date is changed or removed, then the old reminders are not sent.

Story 3 — Templates, versions and PDF

As an author, I want templates and version history, so that I write faster and can undo mistakes.

  1. Given I create an article template, when I start a new article, then I can start from it.

  2. Given an article has several versions, when I pick any two, then I see the differences highlighted.

  3. Given I restore an old version, then it becomes a new latest version. No history is lost.

  4. Given I click Download as PDF, then I get a PDF with the article's title, content and images.

Story 4 — Order and structure

As a Knowledge Base manager, I want to arrange categories, sections and articles, so that customers find things in a sensible order.

  1. Given a category, when I drag articles into a new order, then the Help Center shows that order. "Reset to default order" puts it back.

  2. Given the category list, when I drag or choose A to Z, then categories and sections are reordered.

  3. Given a section, when I add a sub-section inside a sub-section, then deeper levels are allowed.

  4. Given I share a category with another department, then that department's agents can read it but not edit it.

Story 5 — Article addresses

As a Knowledge Base manager, I want stable article addresses, so that old links never break.

  1. Given articles are created, then each gets an article number.

  2. Given Settings, when I choose the permalink format (for example title or number), then new addresses follow it.

  3. Given an article's address changes, when someone opens the old address, then they are sent to the new one (301 redirect).

Story 6 — Translations

As a Knowledge Base manager, I want articles and categories in several languages, so that every customer reads in their own language.

  1. Given an article, when I add a translation by hand or click auto-translate, then a translated version is saved for that language.

  2. Given the main article changes after translation, then the translation is marked "Outdated".

  3. Given a customer views the Help Center in a language, then they see the translation if there is one, otherwise the main language.

Story 7 — Import, bulk actions and Recycle Bin

As a Knowledge Base manager, I want to handle many articles at once, so that big changes don't take hours.

  1. Given a CSV or XLS file with one article per row, when I import it, then each row becomes an article in the category named in that row. Bad rows are listed with the reason and the good rows still import.

  2. Given I select many articles, when I choose move, change owner, change tags, change status or delete, then all selected articles change.

  3. Given I delete an article, then it goes to the Recycle Bin and I can restore it.

  4. Given the article list, when I filter by display permission or expiry date, then only matching articles are shown.

Story 8 — Who can see what in the Help Center

As a Knowledge Base manager, I want clear visibility control, so that private articles never reach the wrong people.

  1. Given a section, when I set its visibility (everyone, registered users, a user group or agents only), then the Help Center follows it.

  2. Given I turn off the Knowledge Base for the Help Center, then the whole tab is hidden from customers.

  3. Given an article, when I open its visibility panel, then I see in one place why it is or is not visible (status, category, section and the global switch).

Story 9 — Customer feedback on articles

As a customer, I want to say whether an article helped, so that the company improves it.

  1. Given I read an article, when I click Like or Dislike, then my vote is counted once.

  2. Given I click Dislike, then a short form asks why. If I submit it, a ticket can be created from it.

  3. Given comments are on, when I post a comment, then it waits for moderation. An agent can approve it, delete it or turn it into a ticket.

  4. Given I follow an article or category, when it changes, then I get an email.

Story 10 — Help customers find articles

As a customer, I want to see related and popular articles, so that I find answers faster.

  1. Given an article has tags, when I read it, then related articles with the same tags are listed.

  2. Given the Help Center home page, then popular and recent articles are shown.

  3. Given search engines visit, then a sitemap lists every public article.

Story 11 — Articles inside tickets

As an agent, I want suggested articles on the ticket, so that I can answer with an existing article.

  1. Given I open a ticket, then articles that match its subject are suggested.

  2. Given I click insert, then I can add the article as a link or as its full text in my reply.

  3. Given an article is used in a reply, then its "Used in tickets" count goes up by one.

Story 12 — Insights, dashboard and API

As a support manager, I want numbers about our articles, so that I know what to fix or write next.

  1. Given I open an article's insights, then I see views by customer type and source, who liked or disliked it, and its history.

  2. Given I open the Knowledge Base dashboard, then I see views, likes, trending articles, top searches and searches with no result.

  3. Given the public API, then search, tags, bulk update, reorder, import, export, feedback and statistics work and respect permissions.

raw_module_items.name: Web form extras: position, analytics, languages
raw_module_items.description_html:
The remaining feedback widget and web form functions. Example: the widget remembers its position on the page.

Phase 4. Needs first: Help Center.

Details

  • Widget position.

  • Form analytics.

  • Display languages.

  • More advanced forms (number limit).

  • Plain HTML embed for the advanced form.

Moved out on 2026-10-13: "Knowledge Base inside the widget" now belongs to NDC-1995 (help widget), which owns all articles in the widget. Community inside the widget is out, because Desk has no community module.

User stories

Written to match Zoho Desk's Feedback Widget and Advanced Web Form. Each story says who needs it, what they need and why, then numbered checks (Given / When / Then) that tell you when the story is done.

Story 1 — Place and style the widget tab

As an admin, I want to choose where the feedback tab sits and how it looks, so that it fits our website.

  1. Given I edit a feedback widget, when I open its settings, then I can put the tab on the left or the right of the page.

  2. Given I enter an offset in pixels, when I save, then the tab moves up or down by that amount.

  3. Given I set the tab title, background colour and text colour, when I save, then the preview shows them right away.

  4. Given the widget is already on a website, when I save a change, then the website shows the change on the next page load.

Story 2 — Choose the widget language

As an admin, I want to choose the language of each widget, so that customers see it in their own language.

  1. Given I edit a widget, when I open the General tab, then I can pick one display language (English and Arabic at least).

  2. Given I pick Arabic, when a customer opens the widget, then all labels, buttons and messages are in Arabic and the layout is right-to-left.

  3. Given I renamed a field label myself, when the language changes, then my own label is kept.

Story 3 — More advanced web forms

As an admin, I want more than one advanced web form, so that each product or service can have its own form.

  1. Given I am under the limit, when I click New Advanced Form, then a new form is created. Zoho's limit depends on the plan: 1 (Free, Express), 5 (Standard), 10 (Professional), 50 (Enterprise).

  2. Given I reach the limit, when I look at the page, then the create button is turned off and a message says the limit has been reached.

  3. Given the limit is reached, when someone calls the API to create one more, then it is refused with a clear message.

Story 4 — Plain HTML embed for the advanced form

As an admin, I want plain HTML code for an advanced form, so that our web developer can place it inside our own page.

  1. Given I open a form's Embed Code, when I choose HTML, then I can copy the code.

  2. Given the code is on a website, when a customer fills it in and submits, then a ticket is created in the form's department with every field filled correctly.

  3. Given the form uses CAPTCHA, when the CAPTCHA is wrong, then no ticket is created and the customer sees an error.

  4. Given the form is deleted or turned off, when someone submits the old HTML, then no ticket is created.

Story 5 — Form analytics

As a support manager, I want to see how people use each form, so that I can fix the fields where they give up.

  1. Given I open a form's Analytics, when I choose a date range, then I see views, forms started and forms submitted.

  2. Given the same page, when I look at each field, then I see where people stopped (drop-off).

  3. Given a form had no visits, when I open Analytics, then I see zeros, not an error.

Zoho reference

Creating the feedback widget and advanced web form · FAQs: advanced web form and form analytics. Zoho tracks form analytics through PageSense. We build it inside Desk.
