raw_module_items.name: Guided conversations (self-service flows)
raw_module_items.description_html:
Step-by-step flows that answer common requests without an agent. Example: "Track my order" answers without an agent.

Phase 4. Needs first: Help Center.

User stories

Written to match Zoho Desk's Guided Conversations. Each story says who needs it, what they need and why, then numbered checks (Given / When / Then) that tell you when the story is done.

Story 1 — Create a flow

As an admin, I want to create a guided flow for a department, so that common requests get answered without an agent.

  1. Given I open Setup → Guided Conversations and pick a department, when I click Create Flow, then I can start from a blank flow or from a template.

  2. Given a blank flow, when I enter a name, target audience, channels, default language and description, then the flow is saved as a draft.

  3. Given flows exist, when I open the page, then I see them in three lists: Published, Draft and Trash.

Story 2 — Build the flow with blocks

As an admin, I want to build a flow from blocks, so that I can design the conversation without code.

  1. Given the builder is open, when I add a message block, then I can show text or an info card (fixed, or filled from data).

  2. Given I add a question block (text, email, phone, number, date or file), when the customer answers, then the answer is saved in a variable. A wrong format, such as a bad email, is asked again.

  3. Given I add a choice block, when I set buttons or choice cards, then each choice leads to its own next block.

  4. Given I add an action block, when I pick Jump, Fork, Operations, Combine or Webhook, then the flow can go to another flow, branch on a condition, set or calculate values, or call an outside URL and use its reply.

  5. Given I use variables, when I add one, then it can be global, local or session, and I can use it in later message text.

  6. Given a block is not supported on a chosen channel (for example, info cards on WhatsApp), when I add it, then I am warned.

Story 3 — End with a ticket or an agent

As a customer, I want to reach a person when the flow can't help, so that I am never stuck.

  1. Given the flow reaches a "Create ticket" step, when it runs, then a ticket is created in the flow's department with the customer's answers in its fields. The customer sees the ticket number.

  2. Given the flow reaches a "Talk to an agent" step, when an agent is available, then a live chat starts with the conversation so far attached.

  3. Given no agent is available, when that step runs, then the customer is offered a ticket instead.

Story 4 — Preview, publish and edit

As an admin, I want to test a flow before customers see it, so that mistakes never reach customers.

  1. Given a draft, when I click Preview, then a chat window opens and runs the flow without creating real tickets.

  2. Given I click Save Draft part way, when I come back, then my work is still there.

  3. Given I click Publish, when the flow is placed in a widget, then customers can use it.

  4. Given I edit a published flow, when I save without publishing again, then customers keep getting the old version until I publish.

Story 5 — Put the flow where customers are

As an admin, I want to place a published flow on our channels, so that customers can find it.

  1. Given a published flow, when I open the help widget settings (NDC-1995), then I can add the flow to the widget.

  2. Given a published flow, when I open Share, then I can copy an embed snippet, an iFrame code or a public link.

  3. Given the flow is set to "agents only", when I open Share, then embedding is not offered.

Story 6 — Languages

As an admin, I want a flow in more than one language, so that each customer reads it in their own language.

  1. Given a flow, when I add a language, then I can translate every block. The default language is the base.

  2. Given a customer picks a language in the widget, when the flow runs, then it uses that translation.

  3. Given a Jump block, when I choose the target flow, then only flows fully published in this language are listed.

Story 7 — Sessions, delete and restore

As an admin, I want clear rules for open sessions and deleted flows, so that nothing is lost by mistake.

  1. Given I set an idle timeout (up to 23 hours 59 minutes), when a customer is idle that long, then the session ends with a message.

  2. Given a session is older than 24 hours, when the customer comes back, then a new session starts.

  3. Given I delete a flow, when I open Trash, then I can restore it with all its languages.

Zoho reference

Guided Conversations — a self-service platform · Building the flow · FAQs

raw_module_items.name: Help widget for websites
raw_module_items.description_html:
An embeddable help widget. Example: a site widget shows articles, a ticket form and chat.

Phase 4. Needs first: Help Center.

Details

  • Knowledge Base inside the widget: search, browse and read articles under the Help Center's visibility rule. Moved here from NDC-1993 on 2026-10-13.

  • JWT remote sign-in: the host site signs its visitor in, for the widget and the Help Center alike.

User stories

Written to match Zoho Desk's ASAP help widget. Each story says who needs it, what they need and why, then numbered checks (Given / When / Then) that tell you when the story is done.

Story 1 — Create the widget

As an admin, I want to create a help widget for our website, so that customers get help without leaving the page.

  1. Given I am an administrator and open Setup → Self Service → ASAP, when I click Create New Widget, then I can enter a display name and map it to All Departments or a Specific Department.

  2. Given the form, when I choose modules, then I can turn on Knowledge Base, Community, Chat and Ticket one by one.

  3. Given I click Generate, then the widget is created, I see a preview in the bottom-right corner and I get a snippet to paste into our website. The Launcher toggle shows or hides the widget on the site.

  4. Given I open the widget's "Customize your widget's appearance" tab, when I set the theme colour, pattern, header logo, window size (small or big) and the launcher icon, shape and position, and click Update, then the preview shows them.

  5. Given JWT sign-in is on, when I enter up to 5 allowed domains in the "Secure your help widget" tab, then the widget appears only on those domains.

Story 2 — Articles inside the widget

As a website visitor, I want to search and read articles in the widget, so that I can solve the problem myself.

  1. Given the widget is open, when I type in search, then matching articles appear as I type.

  2. Given I browse categories, when I open an article, then it opens inside the widget.

  3. Given an article is hidden from me in the Help Center (registered users only or a user group), when I open the widget, then it is hidden there too.

Story 3 — Submit a ticket from the widget

As a website visitor, I want to send a request from the widget, so that I don't need to open another page.

  1. Given I open Submit Ticket, when I choose a department, then I see that department's form.

  2. Given I submit with an attachment, then a ticket is created and I see its number.

  3. Given I am anonymous, when I submit, then the ticket is created, but I cannot see my ticket history in the widget.

Story 4 — Sign visitors in with JWT

As an admin, I want our website to sign its users into the widget, so that they see their own tickets without a second login.

  1. Given I open the widget's "Secure your help widget" tab, when I choose JWT, then I can enter our site's JWT endpoint, copy a secret key and enter up to 5 allowed domains.

  2. Given the website passes a valid token, when the widget loads, then the visitor is signed in, sees My Tickets and can reply. Opening the Help Center signs them in too.

  3. Given a token is older than 10 minutes, wrongly signed or for another domain, when the widget loads, then sign-in is refused, the visitor stays anonymous and the reason is logged for the admin.

  4. Given the email in the token has no contact yet, when sign-in succeeds, then a contact is created.

Story 5 — Chat in the widget

As a website visitor, I want to chat from the same widget, so that I can talk to someone when articles don't help.

  1. Given Chat is on, when I start a chat, then a conversation opens in Omnichannel for an operator.

  2. Given a module is turned off, when I open the widget, then its tab is not shown.

User stories
Written to match Zoho Desk's ASAP help widget. Each story says who needs it, what they need and why, then numbered checks (Given / When / Then) that tell you when the story is done.
Story 1 — Create the widget
As an admin, I want to create a help widget for our website, so that customers get help without leaving the page.
Given I am an administrator and open Setup → Self Service → ASAP, when I click Create New Widget, then I can enter a display name and map it to All Departments or a Specific Department.
Given the form, when I choose modules, then I can turn on Knowledge Base, Community, Chat and Ticket one by one.
Given I click Generate, then the widget is created, I see a preview in the bottom-right corner and I get a snippet to paste into our website. The Launcher toggle shows or hides the widget on the site.
Given I open the widget's "Customize your widget's appearance" tab, when I set the theme colour, pattern, header logo, window size (small or big) and the launcher icon, shape and position, and click Update, then the preview shows them.
Given JWT sign-in is on, when I enter up to 5 allowed domains in the "Secure your help widget" tab, then the widget appears only on those domains.
Story 2 — Articles inside the widget
As a website visitor, I want to search and read articles in the widget, so that I can solve the problem myself.
Given the widget is open, when I type in search, then matching articles appear as I type.
Given I browse categories, when I open an article, then it opens inside the widget.
Given an article is hidden from me in the Help Center (registered users only or a user group), when I open the widget, then it is hidden there too.
Story 3 — Submit a ticket from the widget
As a website visitor, I want to send a request from the widget, so that I don't need to open another page.
Given I open Submit Ticket, when I choose a department, then I see that department's form.
Given I submit with an attachment, then a ticket is created and I see its number.
Given I am anonymous, when I submit, then the ticket is created, but I cannot see my ticket history in the widget.
Story 4 — Sign visitors in with JWT
As an admin, I want our website to sign its users into the widget, so that they see their own tickets without a second login.
Given I open the widget's "Secure your help widget" tab, when I choose JWT, then I can enter our site's JWT endpoint, copy a secret key and enter up to 5 allowed domains.
Given the website passes a valid token, when the widget loads, then the visitor is signed in, sees My Tickets and can reply. Opening the Help Center signs them in too.
Given a token is older than 10 minutes, wrongly signed or for another domain, when the widget loads, then sign-in is refused, the visitor stays anonymous and the reason is logged for the admin.
Given the email in the token has no contact yet, when sign-in succeeds, then a contact is created.
Story 5 — Chat in the widget
As a website visitor, I want to chat from the same widget, so that I can talk to someone when articles don't help.
Given Chat is on, when I start a chat, then a conversation opens in Omnichannel for an operator.
Given a module is turned off, when I open the widget, then its tab is not shown.

raw_module_items.name: Customer Happiness automation and reports
raw_module_items.description_html:
Act on ratings and report on them. Example: a Bad rating reopens the ticket and alerts the supervisor.

Phase 4. Needs first: workflow triggers, basic reports.

Details — automation

  • Reopen the ticket when a rating comes in (bad only, or all).

  • Notify the ticket owner about a rating (bad only, or all), and chosen supervisors about bad ratings.

  • Workflow rule that runs when a rating comes in; rating as a condition in workflows, time-based rules, assignment rules and SLAs; Blueprint step that moves on when a rating comes in.

Details — rating page and links

  • Customise each rating option: icon (or uploaded image), label and thank-you messages.

  • "End users" access option.

  • Rating page in other languages.

  • Rating link inside the "Ticket Closed" email template, with an option to move it; a rating placeholder for any email template or workflow email.

  • Ratings at the end of a chat, on WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram and other messaging channels, and for phone tickets.

Details — where ratings show

  • Rating and comment on the ticket; the customer's overall score next to their name.

  • "Happiness Rating" field for list filters and views.

  • Happiness tab on contacts and accounts; score on the agent profile compared with the team average.

  • Help Center widget with the overall rating percentages.

  • Happiness dashboards and reports by agent, customer and period.

  • API to list and count ratings with filters, and rating percentages on contacts and accounts.

User stories

Written to match Zoho Desk's Customer Happiness (Setup → General → Customer Happiness). Each story says who needs it, what they need and why, then numbered checks (Given / When / Then) that tell you when the story is done.

Story 1 — Reopen the ticket on a rating

As a support manager, I want an unhappy rating to reopen the ticket, so that the customer's problem is looked at again.

  1. Given Customer Happiness settings, when I open Reopen Ticket, then I can choose: don't reopen, reopen on bad ratings only, or reopen on all ratings.

  2. Given "bad only" is chosen, when a closed email or web ticket gets a Bad rating, then it reopens. A Good or Okay rating leaves it closed.

  3. Given "don't reopen" is chosen, when a closed email or web ticket gets any rating, then it stays closed.

  4. Given a chat or messaging ticket (WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram) is closed, when the customer rates it, then it reopens whatever the Reopen Ticket setting says. This is how Zoho works: the reopen setting does not apply to messaging tickets.

Story 2 — Tell the right people about a rating

As a support manager, I want owners and supervisors told about ratings, so that a bad experience gets a quick follow-up.

  1. Given I choose "notify the ticket owner" for bad ratings only or for all ratings, when a matching rating comes in, then the owner gets an email and an in-app notification.

  2. Given I pick supervisors for bad ratings, when a Bad rating comes in, then each of them is notified with the ticket link and the customer's comment.

Story 3 — Ratings in automation

As an admin, I want rules to react to ratings, so that follow-up happens without manual work.

  1. Given I create a workflow rule, when I choose the trigger "rating received", then the rule runs each time a rating comes in.

  2. Given workflows, time-based rules, assignment rules and SLAs, when I add a condition, then "Happiness Rating" (Good, Okay, Bad) is in the list.

  3. Given a Blueprint, when I add a step that waits for a rating, then the ticket moves on once the rating comes in.

Story 4 — Customise the rating page

As an admin, I want to change how the rating options look, so that they match our brand and our customers' language.

  1. Given the rating options Good, Okay and Bad, when I edit one, then I can change its label, icon (or upload an image) and thank-you message.

  2. Given I turn off Okay, then customers only see Good and Bad.

  3. Given I choose who can rate, then "End users" is one of the options.

  4. Given the customer's language is Arabic, when they open the rating page, then it shows in Arabic and right-to-left.

Story 5 — Rating links in emails

As an admin, I want the rating link in our emails, so that customers can rate with one click.

  1. Given the "Ticket Closed" email template, when I open it, then the rating link is already there and I can move it.

  2. Given any email template or workflow email, when I add the rating placeholder, then the sent email has working rating links for that ticket.

  3. Given I add the link to every reply, when a customer rates from any reply, then the rating is saved on that ticket.

Story 6 — Ratings on chat, messaging and phone

As a support manager, I want ratings from every channel, so that happiness covers all our support, not only email.

  1. Given a chat ends, then the customer is asked to rate inside the chat.

  2. Given a WhatsApp, Messenger or Instagram ticket is closed, then the customer gets a rating message in that channel.

  3. Given a phone ticket is closed, then the customer gets a rating link.

  4. Given any of these ratings, then it is saved on the ticket the same way as an email rating.

Story 7 — See ratings across Desk

As an agent, I want to see ratings where I work, so that I know how a customer feels before I reply.

  1. Given a rated ticket, when I open it, then I see the rating and the customer's comment.

  2. Given a customer, then their overall score is shown next to their name.

  3. Given the ticket list, when I filter or build a view, then "Happiness Rating" can be used.

  4. Given a contact or account, then a Happiness tab lists their ratings. My profile shows my score compared with the team average.

Story 8 — Happiness reports, Help Center widget and API

As a support manager, I want reports on ratings, so that I can track happiness over time.

  1. Given the Happiness dashboard, when I choose a period, then I see ratings by agent, by customer and over time.

  2. Given the Help Center, when the happiness widget is on, then it shows the overall Good, Okay and Bad percentages.

  3. Given the API, then I can list and count ratings with filters and get the rating percentages for a contact or account.

Zoho reference

Using Happiness Ratings · Viewing the happiness rating score · Happiness in instant messaging (source for Story 1, check 4: "a closed IM ticket is reopened when a rating is submitted, even if Don't reopen is selected").

raw_module_items.name: User Story: Tavi Desk → Tavi Analytics integration
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Send Tavi Desk data (tickets, agents, customers, time, happiness) into Tavi Analytics automatically, so managers can build reports and dashboards without exporting files. Same idea as the Zoho Desk + Zoho Analytics integration. Today the Analytics tab inside Desk shows "In development". Tavi Analytics already has some Desk dashboard templates (for example "Desk SLA"), so part of the pipe exists; this story makes it a complete, admin-controlled feature. Related: NDC-1996 (Desk basic reports and dashboards).

Full document with screenshots: Tavi Desk → Tavi Analytics Integration: User Stories

How Zoho does it

  • Only a Desk admin can set it up. One connection per organization.

  • Start from Desk (Settings → Integrations) or from Analytics (Import data → Desk).

  • Admin ticks the modules to send. Each module becomes a read-only table in Analytics.

  • Sync every 1, 3, 6, 12 hours or daily, plus "Sync now" up to 5 times a day.

  • 75+ ready-made reports and dashboards are created.

  • Only the admin sees the data at first; they share it, with per-user filters.

  • On sync failure the admin gets an email and in-app message with the reason.

Source: Zoho Analytics help: Zoho Desk connector

User stories (must-have, P0)

  1. Connect Desk to Analytics. As a Desk admin, I want to connect Desk to an Analytics workspace in a few clicks, so managers can report without exports. Connect button in Desk Settings → Integrations and "Tavi Desk" listed in Analytics Import data. Pick or create a workspace. A second connection is blocked with a clear message. Non-admins do not see the button and the API returns 403.

  2. Choose what data to send. As a Desk admin, I want to tick which modules are sent. Tickets is always on. Unticked modules create no dataset. Adding a module later fills it on the next sync without breaking reports.

  3. Keep data fresh. As a Desk admin, I want to set the sync schedule (1, 3, 6, 12 hours or daily at a chosen time, in the org time zone). Only changes since the last sync are sent: new, edited and deleted records. A deleted ticket stops counting after the next sync.

  4. Sync now. As a Desk admin, I want a "Sync now" button. Up to 5 per day, then disabled with "Daily limit reached (5/5)". Disabled while a sync is running.

  5. Ready-made reports. As a support manager, I want default Desk reports and dashboards on day one: tickets by status, channel and agent, first response time, resolution time, SLA breaches, happiness rating, open ticket age. Re-running setup never makes duplicates. Workspace admins can edit; others use "Save as".

  6. Permissions. As a Desk admin, I want Analytics to respect who can see what. Only the connecting admin sees data until it is shared. Per-user filters on shared reports. Users without Analytics access get 403 from every reporting API. Export only with export permission.

  7. Sync status and errors. As a Desk admin, I want to see last sync result and time, next sync, schedule, time zone and syncs done today. Failures send an in-app and email message in plain words with what to do. A sync history lists start, end, records added/updated/deleted and result. A deleted Desk field shows "field removed" in the report instead of crashing.

  8. Edit or disconnect. As a Desk admin, I want "Edit setup" (modules, schedule) and "Remove data source" with a confirm and a keep/delete choice for copied data. Every connect, edit, sync now and remove goes to the Audit Log.

Data to send (one read-only dataset each)

Tickets (always), ticket threads, agents, departments, teams, contacts, accounts are ticked by default. Products, activities (tasks, calls, events), time entries and Knowledge Base articles are optional. Happiness ratings and SLA metrics are added when those Desk modules ship. Times in UTC, shown in the org time zone. Links between datasets (ticket → agent, ticket → contact) are set automatically. Field names use Desk display names. Ready-made formulas on Tickets: ticket age, first reply time, resolution time, resolved %, SLA breached count.

Later (P1/P2)

P1: Desk custom fields in Analytics; auto-join with CRM data; pick fields inside modules; open reports from the Desk Analytics tab; scheduled email of reports. P2: one connection per department; near real-time sync; ask questions in plain words.

Not in version 1

Editing Desk data from Analytics; second-by-second sync; per-department connections; data flowing back from Analytics to Desk.

Open questions for the tech team

  • Reuse the existing Desk data-access layer (behind the Desk SLA dashboard) or build a new sync job?

  • Is one connection per tenant enough?

  • Smallest sync interval our servers can handle for a tenant with 100,000 tickets?

  • Should deleted tickets leave Analytics at once, or when they leave the Desk Recycle Bin?

  • Copy Desk's "who sees which tickets" rules, or per-user filters like Zoho?

Success measures

Admin connects in under 5 minutes; Analytics equals Desk ticket counts per status and agent after each sync; 99% of scheduled syncs succeed in month one; 50% of Desk tenants turn it on within 60 days.

raw_module_items.name: Merge Tickets: features Zoho Desk has that Desk is missing
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

We compared Desk's new Merge Tickets feature with Zoho Desk. Bulk merge from the ticket list works like Zoho (2 to 5 tickets, same department, pick the master and the value of each field). This ticket lists only what Desk has not built yet; the user stories are in NDC-2094. The feature item is NDC-1963 ("Merge, in bulk and from the ticket page").

Missing — where agents start a merge

  1. Merge from the ticket page. Zoho lets an agent open a ticket, see the same customer's other tickets (Timeline), tick the duplicates and press Merge. Desk has no Merge action on the ticket page; its menu has Move, Clone, Share, Print, Archive and Delete only. NDC-1963 asks for this.

Missing — undo a wrong merge

  1. Restore a ticket that was merged by mistake. In Zoho the merged tickets go to the Recycle Bin for 60 days and can be restored. In Desk they are closed with "This cannot be undone", and there is no restore or unmerge (POST /desk/tickets/{id}/unmerge returns 404). Not in NDC-1963.

Could not be checked

We did not merge any tickets during this check, so we have not yet seen what the master's History tab shows, whether the customer gets an email, or where a customer's reply to a merged ticket's old email goes. These are in the test spec and will be checked in the test run. Zoho also shows merged threads to the customer in the Help Center; Desk has no Help Center yet, so this cannot be tested.

Additional notes

Not gaps: merging tickets of different departments (Zoho blocks it too), merging more than 5 tickets at once (Zoho limit is also 5), unmerge (Zoho has none either), a workflow or webhook event for merges (Zoho has none). Desk does better than Zoho in two places: time entries move to the master (Zoho drops them), and merged tickets stay as closed tickets that link to the master (in Zoho their links break).

Test spec: Desk Specs/spec-desk-merge-tickets.md in the QA repository. Nothing was changed on the tenant.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 6 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Merge Tickets: user stories for the functions not built yet
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary
User stories for the 2 functions in NDC-2093 that are not built yet, plus 1 story to confirm. Feature item: NDC-1963.

Story 1 — Merge from the ticket page (NDC-2093 item 1, NDC-1963)


As an agent, I want to merge duplicates while I am reading a ticket, so that I don't have to go back to the list and find them.

  1. Given I open a ticket and have the Merge permission, then I see a Merge action on the ticket page.

  2. Given I press Merge, then I see the same customer's other open tickets in the same department, and I can tick up to 4 of them.

  3. Given I tick at least one and continue, then the same Merge Tickets page opens with the current ticket and the ticked ones.

  4. Given the customer has no other tickets in this department, then I am told so and nothing can be merged.

  5. Given I do not have the Merge permission, or the ticket is already merged, then there is no Merge action.

Story 2 — Restore a ticket merged by mistake (NDC-2093 item 2, not in NDC-1963)


As a support lead, I want to undo a wrong merge, so that a customer's separate request is not lost inside another ticket.

  1. Given a ticket was merged, then for 60 days a user with the restore permission can restore it.

  2. Given I restore it, then it opens again as its own ticket with its own number, and its own conversations, comments, attachments and time entries move back from the master.

  3. Given I restore it, then the master no longer shows those items, and both tickets' History tabs say who restored it and when.

  4. Given the 60 days have passed, then restore is no longer offered.

Story 3 — What the merge leaves behind (to confirm, NDC-1963)

As an agent, I want the master ticket to record the merge, so that anyone can see later which tickets were joined and by whom.

  1. Given tickets were merged, then the master's History tab shows who merged which ticket numbers and when.

  2. Given a customer replies to an email of a merged ticket, then the reply lands on the master, not on a new ticket.

  3. Given a merge happens, then the customer does not get a "ticket closed" email for the merged tickets.

To confirm: this needs a real merge on staging. Please confirm we may merge two "QA" test tickets on the techSupport department (merges cannot be undone) so we can test this.

Environment
staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 6 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: A merged ticket can still be reopened and worked on, and that work never reaches the master ticket
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

After two tickets are merged, the ticket that was merged away (the secondary) is closed and shows "This ticket was merged into another ticket." But it can still be reopened, commented on, timed, and given new CC addresses. Everything added this way stays on the secondary and never appears on the master ticket, so agents can end up working on a ticket that no longer counts. Only Move and editing fields are refused.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Sign in to Desk as an admin and create two tickets, "QA MRG S1 A" and "QA MRG S1 B".

  2. In All Tickets tick both, press Merge, keep A as master and press Merge, then Yes, Merge.

  3. Open ticket B. It shows the merged banner and Closed.

  4. Change its status to Open (or press Reopen), then add a private comment, start the timer and add a CC address.

  5. Open ticket A.

Expected result

A merged ticket is read-only. Reopen, comment, reply, timer, time entry, CC and pick-up are refused with "This ticket was merged into #A. Work on that ticket instead.", the same message Move already gives. The ticket page hides those actions and offers only "Open that ticket".

Actual result

On ticket #123 (merged into #122) the API accepted reopen (200), a private comment (201), a time entry (201), a CC address (201), start timer (200) and pick-up (200). The ticket page shows Open, Reply All, Start timer and Close Ticket next to the merged banner. The comment "QA after merge" is only on #123; #122 still has 2 comments. Move returned 422 "The ticket has been merged into …" and a field edit returned 422, so the guard exists but is not applied to the other actions.

Additional notes

Found while running the Merge Tickets spec (NDC-2093, Desk Specs/spec-desk-merge-tickets.md). Email addresses in the screenshot are masked. The timer started on #123 was reset afterwards.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 6 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Tickets closed by a merge have no Closed Time
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When tickets are merged, the merged-away tickets get status Closed but their Closed Time stays empty. A ticket closed with Close Ticket gets a Closed Time. Reports and views that use Closed Time will miss every merged ticket.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create two tickets in Desk.

  2. In All Tickets tick both and merge them (Merge, then Yes, Merge).

  3. Read the merged-away ticket with GET /api/v1/modules/{tickets module}/records/{id}, or look for Closed Time on it.

Expected result

Closed Time is set to the time of the merge, as it is when a ticket is closed normally.

Actual result

Tickets #144 (merged in the UI), #125 and #123 (merged by API) have status Closed and no closed_time. A ticket that was closed with Close Ticket before being merged kept its closed_time (2026-10-06 13:57:29 UTC).

Additional notes

Similar to NDC-1899 (a ticket created as Closed has no closed time), but this one happens through merge. Found while running the Merge Tickets spec (NDC-2093).

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 6 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Merge page lets you pick an already merged ticket, then shows its internal id in the error
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Merged tickets stay in the ticket list, so an agent can select one and open the merge page. The page gives no warning and even makes it the default master. Only after "Yes, Merge" does an error appear, and it names the ticket by its internal id (a 36-character code) instead of its ticket number.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Merge ticket #127 into #126.

  2. In All Tickets tick #127 and another open ticket, #128, and press Merge.

  3. Press Merge, then Yes, Merge.

Expected result

The merge page warns straight away that #127 was already merged into #126 and does not allow merging it, the way it already warns about tickets from different departments. Any error message uses ticket numbers.

Actual result

#127 is shown as the default master with no warning. After Yes, Merge the page shows "#127: Ticket bd9860a1-… has itself been merged, so nothing can be merged into it. Merge into the ticket that now holds the conversation instead." The other duplicate-merge path gives "Ticket <id> has already been merged into <id>." with two internal ids.

Additional notes

Found while running the Merge Tickets spec (NDC-2093).

Environment

raw_module_items.name: Merge API returns wrong error messages for unknown tickets and fields
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

POST /api/v1/desk/tickets/merge refuses bad requests correctly, and nothing gets merged, but several of its messages describe the wrong problem or show internal .NET class names.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Call POST /api/v1/desk/tickets/merge as an admin with each body below.

  2. Read the error message.

Expected result

A ticket id that does not exist gives "Ticket not found". A wrong type gives a plain message such as "master_ticket_id must be a ticket id". An unknown field gives "Unknown field".

Actual result

  1. master_ticket_id that does not exist: 400 "Choose the master ticket.", though a master was given.

  2. source_ticket_ids with an id that does not exist: 400 "Each ticket can be merged once.", though there is no duplicate.

  3. master_ticket_id null, "not-a-uuid" or 123: 400 with "could not be converted to Anyware.Desk.Contracts.Tickets.MergeTicketsRequest …", which exposes the internal class name.

  4. field_sources with a field that does not exist: 400 "'no_such_field' always keeps the master ticket's value."

Additional notes

Reading the tickets back showed that none of these calls merged anything. Found while running the Merge Tickets spec (NDC-2093).

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, API, 6 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Customer Happiness rating page is blank for every valid rating link, so customers cannot rate
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When a customer clicks a rating link (one of the smileys) in a Desk email, the rating page opens completely empty. No question, no options, no message. The rating link itself is valid and the server answers correctly, but the page never shows anything, so customers cannot rate through the page at all.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Turn on Customer Happiness (Settings → Customer Happiness → Collect customer ratings).

  2. Reply to a customer on a ticket so the customer receives an email with the rating smileys.

  3. As the customer, click any smiley (or open the rating link) in that email.

  4. Wait 15 seconds.

Expected result

The rating page shows the agent's name, the question, the Bad / Okay / Good options, the optional comment box and the Submit button.

Actual result

The page stays blank — there is no visible text at all. The server responds to the page's request with status 200 and the full rating details (status "open", question, options), but the page does not display them. raw_module_items.name: Ticket Closed rating link is refused for the ticket's own requester in "Requesters and cc'd users" mode
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When "Rating link accessible to" is set to "Requesters and cc'd users", the rating link sent in the Ticket Closed email can never be used by the customer who opened the ticket. Every attempt is refused with "This rating can only be submitted by someone the message was sent to." Rating links sent with ordinary replies work for the same customer, so only the close-time link is affected.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Customer Happiness.

  2. Set "Rating link accessible to" to "Requesters and cc'd users", keep "Send the Ticket Closed email" on, and save.

  3. Close a ticket so the customer receives "Your ticket #N has been closed" with the rating smileys (either with "When to ask" = when the ticket is closed, or with "Also ask on close when no agent replied" on).

  4. As the customer, open the rating link, pick a rating and enter the email address the message was sent to (the ticket's requester address).

  5. Submit.

Expected result

The rating is accepted, because the person rating is the ticket's requester and the email was sent to them.

Actual result

The rating is refused with status 403 and the message "This rating can only be submitted by someone the message was sent to." It happens with the address typed exactly and in upper case. Reproduced on ticket #152 and ticket #158 on 6 October, and again on #158 on 7 October (the requester field on the ticket matches the inbox that received the email). The same customer can rate links sent with normal replies. Switching access to "Anyone on internet" makes the same close-time link work.

Additional notes

Customers can therefore never rate a closed ticket while this access mode is selected. Because the rating page itself is currently blank (separate ticket), this was tested by sending the rating directly to the rating service, the way the page does.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, rating service called directly, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Saving Customer Happiness settings without the newer fields silently resets them
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

If the Customer Happiness settings are saved with only the original ten fields (question, trigger, access, expiry, departments and so on), the save succeeds and every newer setting that was left out is wiped. Reopen on rating and Notify owner go back to Off, the people notified about bad ratings are removed, custom option icons return to defaults and the reminder goes back to Never. Any older client or integration that does not know the new fields will erase the configuration without anyone noticing.

Steps to reproduce

  1. In Settings → Customer Happiness, set "Reopen the ticket" to All ratings, "Notify the ticket owner" to All ratings, add one person under "Also notify about bad ratings", and pick a custom icon for Good. Save.

  2. Send a settings save to the server containing only the ten original fields (is_enabled, question, okay_enabled, trigger, show_smileys_inline, show_agent_photo, access_mode, expiry_days, department_scope_enabled, department_ids) plus the current row_version.

  3. Reload the Customer Happiness page.

Expected result

Fields that were not sent stay as they were, or the save is refused with a clear message (as already happens when the question or trigger is left out).

Actual result

The save returns 200. Reopen changes from All to Off, Notify owner from All to Off, the notified people from 1 to 0, and the Good icon from 💔 back to 🙂. The reset of the notified people is not recorded in the Audit Log either. Reproduced on 7 October; settings were restored afterwards.

Additional notes

Leaving out question or trigger is correctly refused with 400, so the server already checks some missing fields — just not the newer ones.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, settings API and Chromium, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: An empty rating link access value is saved as "Anyone on internet"
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Saving the Customer Happiness settings with the access value left empty (null) is accepted and quietly stores the most open option, "Anyone on internet". A tenant that had restricted rating links to requesters and cc'd users can lose that restriction without any error or warning.

Steps to reproduce

  1. In Settings → Customer Happiness, set "Rating link accessible to" to "Requesters and cc'd users" and save.

  2. Send a full settings save to the server with access_mode set to null (all other fields unchanged).

  3. Reload the Customer Happiness page.

Expected result

The save is refused with a message, the same way an empty string or an unknown value such as "everyone" is refused.

Actual result

The save returns 200 and the setting becomes "Anyone on internet". The page now shows that option selected. Reproduced on 7 October; settings were restored afterwards.

Additional notes

Empty string, "everyone" and the number 2 are all refused with 400, so only null slips through.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, settings API and Chromium, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Changes to who is notified about bad ratings are not recorded in the Audit Log
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Adding or removing people under "Also notify about bad ratings" leaves no trace in the Audit Log. Other Customer Happiness changes made in the same minutes (access, reopen, notify owner, reminder, options) are logged, so an admin can see those but cannot find out who changed the list of people notified. Department scope entries are also logged without naming the department.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Customer Happiness → When a rating comes in.

  2. Remove the person listed under "Also notify about bad ratings" and save.

  3. Add the same person back and save.

  4. Open Settings → Audit Log and look at the entries for those two saves.

Expected result

Each save has an entry saying who changed the list and which people were added or removed.

Actual result

The two saves only produce "UpdatedAt from … to …" entries. Of the 11 Customer Happiness entries written on 7 October, none mentions the notified people. Department scope entries read "added a audit.entity.happiness_department_scope" without saying which department.

Additional notes

Related to the general Audit Log coverage issue NDC-1343, but this one is specific to the new Customer Happiness setting.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, settings and audit API, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Rating page shows "check your connection" instead of the real reason a rating was refused
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When the rating service refuses a rating with a clear reason — for example "This rating can only be submitted by someone the message was sent to." — the rating page ignores that reason and tells the customer "Something went wrong. Please check your connection and try again." The customer is sent looking for a network problem that does not exist.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Set "Rating link accessible to" to "Requesters and cc'd users".

  2. Open a rating link from a reply email.

  3. Pick a rating and enter an email address the message was not sent to.

  4. Submit.

Expected result

The page shows the service's message: "This rating can only be submitted by someone the message was sent to."

Actual result

The service answers 403 with that message, but the page shows "Something went wrong. Please check your connection and try again." The page looks for the message in a different place than where the service puts it, so every refusal (403, 409, 422) falls back to the network text.

Additional notes

The rating page is currently blank for valid links (separate ticket), so this was observed on the page with the response unwrapped by the test, and confirmed in the live page code on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, customer side (no login).

raw_module_items.name: Rating links in customer emails go through SendGrid click tracking, exposing the rating link to a third party
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Every rating smiley in customer emails points to a SendGrid tracking address (ct.sendgrid.net) instead of directly to the rating page. The private rating link is handed to SendGrid and every click is logged there. Email security scanners that open tracked links in advance also pass through it.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Turn on Customer Happiness.

  2. Reply to a customer so they receive an email with the rating smileys.

  3. In the received email, inspect where each smiley link points.

Expected result

The smileys link directly to the rating page on the Desk public address, and the rating link does not reach any third party.

Actual result

All smiley links in all 13 received rating emails (replies and Ticket Closed emails) point to u114932968.ct.sendgrid.net/ls/click…, which then redirects to the rating page. Checked on 6 and 7 October.

Additional notes

Turning off click tracking for the rating block (or for these emails) would avoid it. Link values are not shown in the evidence.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, emails received in a QA inbox, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Customers see the raw text {{happiness.link}} in the quoted history of later emails
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When an agent inserts the rating link placeholder into a reply, the reply itself is sent correctly with the rating smileys. But every later email on the same ticket quotes the earlier reply with the placeholder text {{happiness.link}} written out literally, so the customer sees template code in their email.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Turn on Customer Happiness.

  2. On a ticket, reply to the customer and insert the "Rating link" placeholder in the text (for example "Link here: {{happiness.link}}"). Send.

  3. Send a second reply on the same ticket.

  4. Open the second email in the customer's mailbox and look at the quoted earlier message.

Expected result

The quoted earlier message shows the rating link (or nothing) in place of the placeholder — never the raw placeholder text.

Actual result

The quoted part reads "> QA E-A default. Link here: {{happiness.link}}". Found in 2 of the 13 received emails on ticket #149 (6 October), confirmed in the mailbox on 7 October.

Additional notes

The first reply itself is correct: the placeholder is replaced by one rating block, and the agent's copy shows "[Customer Happiness rating link]". Only the quoted history is wrong.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, email received in a QA inbox, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Rating links of a deleted ticket stay open and still accept ratings, and the stats count them
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

After a ticket is deleted, the rating links already sent for it keep working. A customer can still open them and submit a rating, and that rating is counted in the happiness statistics even though the ticket no longer exists.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Turn on Customer Happiness with "When to ask" = every response.

  2. Reply to a customer on a QA ticket so a rating link is sent, and do not rate it.

  3. Delete the ticket (it goes to the Recycle Bin).

  4. Open the rating link from the email.

  5. Submit a rating.

  6. Check the happiness statistics.

Expected result

The link shows "This rating link is not valid." and the rating is refused while the ticket is deleted.

Actual result

On 6 October, after ticket #159 was deleted (opening the ticket gives "not found"), its pending link still showed status "open". A Good rating was accepted (200), and the statistics went from 8 to 9 ratings. On 7 October the links of deleted tickets #160 and #166 still show "open". The statistics total of 16 includes ratings on tickets that have since been deleted.

Additional notes

After the ticket was restored from the Recycle Bin, its ratings showed on it again.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, rating service and API, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Merging tickets leaves the merged ticket's ratings behind instead of moving them to the master ticket
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When a ticket that already has ratings is merged into another ticket, its replies move to the master ticket but its ratings do not. The ratings stay on the merged ticket, under a conversation that no longer holds the replies they belong to, and the master ticket shows none of them.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create two QA tickets, A and B, in the same department.

  2. Reply on both so rating links are sent, and rate one of B's replies Bad.

  3. Merge B into A (A is the master).

  4. Open A and B and look at the ratings in each conversation.

Expected result

The rating follows its reply to the master ticket A, so A's conversation shows it next to the reply that was rated.

Actual result

Merging #162 into #161 succeeded and moved 2 replies to #161. #161 still lists only its own pending request, and the Bad rating stays on #162, whose conversation now holds only the description. Confirmed on 7 October: #161 has 1 pending request; #162 is merged into #161 and holds both ratings.

Additional notes

Related to the Merge Tickets feature (NDC-1963).

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium and API, 7 October 2026, owner account. QA inbox address masked.

raw_module_items.name: After a "someone else changed these settings" conflict, the Customer Happiness page throws away the admin's edit
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When two admins edit Customer Happiness at the same time, the second save correctly gets the message "Someone else changed these settings after you opened them. Reload to see their changes, then save again." But the page immediately replaces the second admin's form with the saved values, so their edit is lost before they can compare or re-apply it.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open Settings → Customer Happiness in two browser tabs.

  2. In tab 1, change the rating question and save.

  3. In tab 2, change "Link expires after (days)" from 30 to 45 and save.

Expected result

Tab 2 shows the conflict message and keeps 45 on screen, so the admin can reload and re-apply their change.

Actual result

Tab 2 shows the conflict message, and within a second the field is back to 30 and the question shows tab 1's text. The value 45 the admin typed is gone. Reproduced on 7 October.

Additional notes

The conflict detection itself works correctly.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Double-clicking Save on Customer Happiness sends two saves and can show a false conflict message
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Double-clicking the Save button on the Customer Happiness page sends the save twice. The second save is rejected as a conflict, and on a slow connection the message left on screen can be "Someone else changed these settings after you opened them…" even though the admin's own save succeeded.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open Settings → Customer Happiness and change the rating question.

  2. Double-click Save (easiest to see on a slow connection).

Expected result

One save is sent and "Customer Happiness settings saved." is shown.

Actual result

Two saves are sent: the first succeeds and the second is rejected as a conflict. On 6 October, with the save delayed by 4 seconds, the message left on screen was the conflict message. On 7 October two saves were sent again, and that time the success message was shown. A triple-click sends three.

Additional notes

The Save button only becomes disabled after the first click has been processed.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, owner account.

Typing a decimal such as 2.5 into "Link expires after (days)" and saving shows only "One or more validation errors occurred." The admin is not told which field is wrong or why. Out-of-range whole numbers (0, 91, -1) get a clear message, so only decimals and other wrong types are affected.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open Settings → Customer Happiness.

  2. Enter 2.5 in "Link expires after (days)".

  3. Save.

Expected result

A message naming the field and the rule, like the existing "The link lifetime must be between 1 and 90 days." (for example "Enter a whole number of days between 1 and 90.")

Actual result

The save is refused with 400 and the toast only says "One or more validation errors occurred." The error details in the response also expose internal type names and byte positions from the server. Reproduced on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium and settings API, 7 October 2026, owner account.

The same problem was reported for Omnichannel Global Settings in NDC-1738.

Environment

raw_module_items.name: Invalid Customer Happiness settings values are accepted and silently replaced instead of refused
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Several invalid values sent when saving Customer Happiness settings are accepted with 200 and quietly turned into something else, instead of being refused with a message. What gets stored is not what was sent, and nobody is told.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Save the Customer Happiness settings (full body) with each of the values below, one at a time.

  2. Read the settings back after each save.

Expected result

Each invalid value is refused with a 400 that names the field, as already happens for other bad values (for example "bad" for Reopen, or an icon outside the set).

Actual result

  • Reopen the ticket = empty, and Notify the ticket owner = null → 200, both stored as "off".

  • Ticket Closed email subject = empty → 200, the default subject is stored.

  • Rating options with Okay missing and Good/Bad in reverse order → 200, Okay is added back with defaults and the order is put back.

  • Notify list containing an all-zero user id → 200, the id is silently dropped (6 October).

  • Rating options with an unknown key ("great") or a duplicate key → 200, the entry is dropped and that option is reset to its defaults, losing its custom icon (6 October).

Reproduced on 7 October; settings were restored after each case.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, settings API, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Audit Log entries for Customer Happiness show a raw key and internal field names
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Audit Log entries written when Customer Happiness settings are saved are hard to read. They show an untranslated key instead of "Customer Happiness settings", internal field names instead of the labels on the page, and an extra "UpdatedAt" entry for every save.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Change any Customer Happiness setting and save.

  2. Open Settings → Audit Log.

Expected result

Readable entries such as "Eslam Ahmed updated Customer Happiness settings: Reopen the ticket from Off to All ratings."

Actual result

  • Entries read "Eslam Ahmed updated audit.entity.happiness_settings' IsEnabled from no to yes", including a stray apostrophe.

  • Field names are internal, such as UpdatedAt, OptionsJson, CloseFallbackEnabled, NotifyOwnerOnRating and AccessMode (with values like "RequesterAndCc").

  • Every save adds a separate "UpdatedAt from … to …" entry.

  • Option changes show the whole stored option list instead of what changed.

Confirmed in the audit data on 7 October.

Additional notes

The raw stored-document part is similar to NDC-1643 (CRM blueprints and layouts). This ticket covers the Customer Happiness entries.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium and audit API, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: My Profile happiness score differs from the agent's happiness score elsewhere
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The "Customer happiness" tiles on My Profile give a different score and different counts than the agent profile and the happiness statistics for the same agent and period. An agent sees one number for themselves and their manager sees another.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Make sure an agent has ratings this month.

  2. Sign in as that agent and open My Profile → Customer happiness.

  3. Open Settings → Agents → the same agent → Happiness Rating.

  4. Compare the scores and counts.

Expected result

Both views show the same score and the same Good / Okay / Bad counts.

Actual result

On 7 October My Profile shows Good 2, Neutral 3, Bad 2 and Happiness 28.6%. The agent profile and the statistics show 16 ratings — Good 8, Okay 3, Bad 5 — and 50%. On 6 October it was 40% against 50%. My Profile appears to leave out some ratings, for example chat ratings and ratings on close.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: If the connection drops while submitting a rating, the whole form and the customer's choice are lost
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

If the network drops at the moment the customer submits a rating, the rating page replaces everything — question, chosen option, email and comment — with the line "Something went wrong. Please check your connection and try again." There is nothing left to retry with, so the customer has to start again or gives up.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open a rating link.

  2. Pick a rating, type a comment (and the email, if asked).

  3. Lose the connection and press Submit.

Expected result

The error is shown above the form, and the chosen option, email and comment stay so the customer can press Submit again.

Actual result

The whole form disappears and only the error line remains. The live page code clears the form on any network failure (confirmed 7 October).

Additional notes

The rating page is currently blank for valid links (separate ticket), so this was observed with the response unwrapped by the test and confirmed in the page code.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, customer side (no login).

raw_module_items.name: "Send the Ticket Closed email" is on, but closing a ticket does not always send it
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

With "Send the Ticket Closed email" switched on, customers only get the "Your ticket has been closed" email when a rating link is issued on that close. With "When to ask" set to every response, or when a ticket is closed a second time, no closed email is sent at all. This needs a product decision: if the email is meant to go out on every close, this is a defect.

Steps to reproduce

  1. In Settings → Customer Happiness, keep "Send the Ticket Closed email" on and set "When to ask" to every response.
  2. Reply to a customer on a ticket, then close the ticket.
  3. Check the customer's mailbox.

Expected result

The customer receives "Your ticket #N has been closed", as the setting name suggests.

Actual result

No closed email arrives for ticket #155 (every response, agent replied) or #157 (every response, no reply). Ticket #152 got a closed email on its first close but none when it was closed again after a rating reopened it. Closed emails did arrive for #152 (first close), #153 and #158, where a rating link was issued on close.

Additional notes

The settings hint says the email "carries the rating link when ratings are sent on close", which may mean this is intended — please confirm.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, emails received in a QA inbox, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: The customer's rating comment is silently changed when it is saved
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Text in angle brackets that a customer types into the rating comment is removed when the rating is saved, and "&" is stored as "&". No script runs, so this is safe, but agents see a different comment from the one the customer wrote, and nobody is told.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open a rating link and pick a rating.
  2. Type a comment containing text in angle brackets and an ampersand, for example "<b>bold</b> & thanks".
  3. Submit, then look at the rating on the ticket.

Expected result

The comment is stored and shown exactly as typed, displayed as plain text.

Actual result

The comment sent on ticket #149 contained an image tag, a script tag, "<b>bold</b>" and "&". It is stored as "QA R1 bad alert(2) bold & مرحبا بالعالم ${7*7} {{7*7}} 😀👍🏽". The tags were removed and "&" became "&". The save returned 200 with no notice. Re-checked on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, rating service and API, 7 October 2026, owner account.

  1. Open Setup → Customer Happiness.

  2. Click in "Link expires after (days)" and press Tab repeatedly into Rating options.

  3. Inside an Icon picker, press the Right arrow key.

Expected result

Each picker is one Tab stop, and the arrow keys move between icons and select them, as for any group of choices.

Actual result

Each picker has 14 Tab stops (3 pickers = 42), and the Right arrow neither moves focus nor changes the selection. Re-checked on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, owner account.

Summary

In Customer Happiness → Languages, the "Add a language…" menu has no label, so a screen reader only reads the first option text. The download buttons next to English and Arabic are both read as "Download translation file", so a screen reader user cannot tell which language each one downloads.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open Setup → Customer Happiness → Languages with a screen reader (or inspect the accessibility tree).

  2. Move to the "Add a language…" menu and to the download buttons.

Expected result

The menu has a label (for example "Add a language"), and each button names its language (for example "Download English translation file").

Actual result

The menu has no label of any kind. Both per-language buttons are named "Download translation file". Re-checked on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Malformed rating links show a raw server error page with the server version
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Opening a rating link whose code contains certain encoded characters shows the web server's own "400 Bad Request" page, including the server software and version ("nginx/1.18.0 (Ubuntu)"), instead of the app's "This rating link is not valid." The rating service returns the same HTML page instead of its normal error.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open https://staging-desk.taviportal.com/happiness/%00 (also /happiness/..%2F..%2Fsettings).

Expected result

The app's page "This rating link is not valid.", or at least a plain 400 without the server name and version.

Actual result

HTTP 400 with an nginx page reading "400 Bad Request — nginx/1.18.0 (Ubuntu)". The rating service address /api/v1/desk/public/happiness/%00 returns the same HTML page. Re-checked on 7 October.

Additional notes

Showing the server version helps attackers pick known weaknesses. Hiding it (for example with nginx server_tokens off) affects the whole site, not only this page.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, no login.

raw_module_items.name: The public rating page has no enforced Content Security Policy
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The rating page that customers open from their email is protected only by a report-only Content Security Policy, which blocks nothing. The policy also has no reporting address (so nothing is ever reported) and allows inline scripts. The same headers are used across the Desk app.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Request https://staging-desk.taviportal.com/happiness/<any code> and look at the response headers.

Expected result

An enforced Content-Security-Policy header on the customer-facing page, without 'unsafe-inline' for scripts.

Actual result

There is no Content-Security-Policy header. Only Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only is sent; it allows 'unsafe-inline' scripts and has no report-to or report-uri. Safari/WebKit warns that the policy "will have no effect". Re-checked on 7 October.

Additional notes

This is defence in depth: no script injection was found in Customer Happiness. The fix is app-wide, not only for this page.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, response headers, 7 October 2026, no login.

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields Missings
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

We compared TAVI Desk's Modules and Fields (modules, tabs, layouts and fields) with Zoho Desk. This ticket lists what Zoho Desk has and TAVI Desk does not have yet. Time Entry was not checked. Six items are already filed in NDC-1879 and one in NDC-1866; they are listed at the end and not repeated. Each item has an attached image: TAVI on the left, Zoho Desk on the right, with numbered boxes and a short comparison table.

Missing — tabs and modules

  1. Tab bar set by the admin for everyone. In Zoho a hidden module is hidden for every user, and at least one module must stay. Today TAVI's Organize Tabs changes only your own tab bar ("Changes apply to you only"). Image 01.

  2. Rename any tab. Zoho has a Rename Tabs page with 19 names, including Knowledge Base, Customers, Activities, Analytics, Reports, Dashboards, Community, Social, Chat and IM. Today TAVI can rename only record modules. Image 02.

Missing — fields

  1. Protect the standard fields. In Zoho, core fields are "Non-removable", system-mandatory fields cannot be made optional, other standard fields can only go to Unused Fields, and only custom fields are marked as custom. Today every seeded field is marked "Custom Field"; Subject on Calls, Events and Tasks, Product Name and Contract Name can be deleted; Ticket Subject and Status can be made optional and removed; Contact, Department, Email, Description, Due Date, Priority, Channel, Ticket Owner and Resolution can be removed from the ticket layout (API flags isCustomField, canMarkRequired, canRemoveFromLayout). Image 04.

  2. Layouts per department and the Department field. In Zoho, Tickets, Tasks, Calls, Events and Contracts have one layout per department; Department cannot be removed there and is mandatory on Tasks, Calls, Events and Contracts; Products has a mandatory multi-select Department. Today TAVI layouts are assigned to profiles only, and Department is optional and not on the Tasks, Calls or Events layouts. Image 05.

  3. Missing or different standard fields: Tickets Category and Sub Category (with a dependency); Accounts Annual Revenue and separate Street, City, State and Code; Products Department, and Manufacturer as a pick list; Tasks Remind At; Calls and Events Remind me; Contact Name mandatory on Calls and Events; Call Status mandatory on Calls; Contracts Account Name, Start Date and Support Plan mandatory, plus SLA Name. Image 06.

  4. Picklist tools: Add Values in Bulk (predefined lists, typed values or a file), Sort A–Z, clear all values, and Replace Values at any time, which updates existing records. Today values are added, moved and removed one at a time, and replacement is offered only when removing a used option. Image 07.

  5. Rounding for Decimal and Currency fields (Normal, Round off, Round down, Round up). Today only precision and scale. Zoho side from the help docs. Image 08.

  6. Lookup options: filter which records can be picked (up to 5 criteria), search by up to 6 fields, show up to 6 fields in the pop-up, sort, and fill up to 5 fields from the chosen record. Today only target module, display field, related list title and multi-module. Zoho side from the help docs. Image 09.

Missing — layouts and setup pages

  1. Help Center settings on a layout: Display in Help Center (a column on the Tickets layouts list), Display Name in Help Center, Description, and Allow non-department agents. Today a new layout has a name only. Image 10.

  2. Ticket Status page, per department: add statuses and give each one a type (Open, On Hold, Closed), so that On Hold pauses the SLA clock. Today Status is a plain pick list. Image 11.

  3. Agents as a customisable module. In Zoho, Agents has its own layout, 15 field types and 240 custom fields. TAVI has no Agents module in Modules and Fields (check NDC-1878 for overlap). Image 12.

Missing — found in functional testing (added 13 Oct 2026)

  1. Default value for a field. In Zoho a text, pick list or checkbox field can have a default value, which is filled in on new records only (the Priority value list shows a "Default" tag). Today TAVI's Field Properties (General, Validation, Permissions, Advanced) have no default-value setting, and a defaultValue saved into the layout through the API is ignored: the create form opens empty and a record created through the API with no values is saved empty. Spec rows I19 and I24. Image 13.

Already filed (still missing, seen live in Zoho on 5 Oct 2026)

  • NDC-1879 item 1: Layout Rules page.

  • NDC-1879 item 2: Validation Rules page.

  • NDC-1879 item 3: picklist values per layout.

  • NDC-1879 item 4: Help Center access per field ("Hide from Help Center", "Editable for End Users").

  • NDC-1879 item 5: nested and colour-coded picklists.

  • NDC-1879 item 6: field encryption.

  • NDC-1866 item 16: ticket number format (Zoho Ticket Id is an Autonumber; TAVI Ticket Number is a read-only single line).

Could not be checked

  • No Light Agent or Reviewer test account is available. Please give us one account for each of these profiles so we can test field permissions and Light Agent limits for them.

  • Some standard fields are already soft-deleted on the tenant (Contacts Mailing Address and Description; Accounts Industry, Fax, Address and Description; last changed 14 Sep 2026). Please confirm whether this was done on purpose, so we know whether to restore them before checking item 6.

  • Zoho's new-field dialogs are drag-only and we did not drag anything in the Zoho org, so items 8 and 9 come from Zoho's help docs. Please confirm if a live check in Zoho is needed.

Additional notes

  • Not gaps: department access for custom modules (locked to "All Departments" in live Zoho), Products tab (Zoho has none in the bar either), the IM tab (part of the IM channel), Zoho field limits, and import/export of custom module records (Zoho does not support it either).

  • Different values, not gaps: Ticket Priority and Ticket Channel values differ from Zoho, but both are editable lists.

  • Possible bug to check separately: Tickets layout builder, gear → Rename Module crashes the page ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')"). See image 02, box 3.

  • Possible bug to check separately: seeded standard fields are flagged as custom and can be permanently deleted.

  • Possible bug to check separately: the layout preview shows stored option keys (low, email) instead of labels.

  • Possible bug to check separately: every module has a required "Name" field that is on no layout (for example Tickets).

  • Possible bug to check separately: Desk shows CRM wording ("Set up your CRM", "inside the CRM").

  • Possible bug to check separately: Last Modified shows "UN" for every seeded module.

  • Possible bug to check separately: the Create module dialog has no Arabic name ("Registers a new module (English label)").

  • Test spec and full missing list: docs/desk-modules-fields/ in the QA repository (spec-desk-modules-fields.md, desk-modules-fields-missing-list.md, evidence/).

  • The comparison was read-only. Nothing was changed on the TAVI tenant or in the Zoho org.

  • Item 13 was found in functional test run 2 (6–7 Oct 2026) on a QA test module, which was deleted afterwards. Nothing was changed in the Zoho org.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium (TAVI) and Edge (Zoho Desk), 5 October 2026, admin accounts. Item 13: functional run 2, 6–7 October 2026.

raw_module_items.name: Scheduling a reply for a date and time fails with "Unknown time zone." for every real time zone
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

In the Schedule this reply dialog, the "Date and time" option never works. Whatever date, time and time zone the agent picks, the dialog shows "Unknown time zone." and the reply is not scheduled. The time zone list offers real zones such as Africa/Cairo (and defaults to the agent's own), but the server only accepts the value "UTC". The quick picks (In 10 minutes, In 1 hour…) and "After" work.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open any email ticket and click Reply.

  2. Type a message.

  3. Click the arrow next to Send and choose Schedule.

  4. Choose "Date and time", pick tomorrow at 10:00, and leave the time zone as shown (here Africa/Cairo, the browser's zone).

  5. Click Schedule.

Expected result

The reply is scheduled for 10:00 in the chosen time zone. The dialog's own preview already says "Sends Oct 9, 2026, 10:00 AM GMT+3", and a "Reply scheduled for …" message appears.

Actual result

The dialog stays open with the error "Unknown time zone." and nothing is scheduled. The server refuses the request with status 400 (time zone invalid). Sending the same request with other zones — Europe/London, America/New_York, Asia/Dubai, Etc/UTC — is refused the same way. Only the literal value "UTC" is accepted. Rescheduling an existing scheduled reply to a date and time fails for the same reason.

Additional notes

So the "Date and time" option is unusable for anyone who doesn't pick UTC. The time zone list comes from the browser and uses standard zone names, which the server does not recognise. Found in the Scheduled Replies smoke test (feature NDC-2017). QA inbox address masked in the screenshot.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium (browser time zone Africa/Cairo), 7 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Scheduled Replies: features Zoho Desk has that Desk is missing
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

We compared Desk's new Scheduled Replies feature with Zoho Desk. Scheduling from the reply box, the Scheduled Replies list (My / All, filters, row and bulk actions) and the automatic send work like Zoho. This ticket lists only what Desk has not built yet; the user stories are in NDC-2178. The feature spec is NDC-1851 (Sub-Item 4, Scheduled Replies); the delivery item is NDC-2017.

Missing — settings

  1. Turn scheduled replies on or off per department (Zoho: Setup → General Settings → Schedule Replies → Configure). Today scheduling is always on for every ticket.

  2. Per department, choose whether a customer reply cancels the schedule, and whether the customer closing the ticket from the help center cancels it. Today both are fixed and cannot be changed.

  3. Turn the agent notifications "scheduled reply sent" and "scheduled reply not sent" on or off. Today they are always sent. NDC-1851 asks for them to be configurable.

Missing — on the ticket

  1. A "Scheduled" label on the reply inside the ticket conversation, with the send time on hover. Today the ticket shows nothing until the reply is sent.

  2. Edit, reschedule, send now, clear or discard the scheduled reply from the ticket itself. Today these actions exist only on the Scheduled Replies page.

  3. "Schedule and close ticket" (and "Reschedule and close"). The reply box never offers it, although the API already has close_after_send.

Missing — Scheduled Replies list

  1. Discard a scheduled reply (cancel it and delete the text, with no draft kept). Today only "Clear schedule" exists, and it always saves a draft.

  2. Jump straight to the reply inside the ticket ("Ticket peek"). Today the row opens a small detail panel or the ticket from the top. NDC-1851 lists this as an open question.

  3. Choose the list columns (for example Subject, Time zone, Thread owner). Today the columns are fixed.

Could not be checked

Cancelling a scheduled reply when the customer replies first. Email sent to the hosted address (help.taviportal.com) does not create tickets or replies on the new staging, so we cannot make a customer reply. Please fix inbound email routing on staging so we can test this.

Additional notes

Not gaps: Desk allows several pending scheduled replies on one ticket (Zoho allows one and keeps a second as a draft — please decide which we want); Desk has a public API for scheduled replies (Zoho has none); Zoho's Blueprint strict-mode rules (Desk has no Blueprint yet); scheduling from Zoho's mobile apps (Desk has no mobile app).

Bugs found while testing are filed separately with the "Scheduled Replies" label (NDC-2175 and the 7 Oct spec run).

Test spec: Desk Specs/spec-desk-scheduled-replies.md in the QA repository (Group Z = the items above).

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account.

Per department, choose whether a customer reply cancels the schedule, and whether the customer closing the ticket from the help center cancels it. Today both are fixed and cannot be changed.
Turn the agent notifications "scheduled reply sent" and "scheduled reply not sent" on or off. Today they are always sent. NDC-1851 asks for them to be configurable.

"Schedule and close ticket" (and "Reschedule and close"). The reply box never offers it, although the API already has close_after_send.
