raw_module_items.name: Scheduled Replies: user stories for the functions not built yet
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary
User stories for the 9 functions in NDC-2177 that are not built yet, plus 1 story to confirm. Feature spec: NDC-1851 (Sub-Item 4); delivery item: NDC-2017.

Story 1 — Turn scheduling on or off per department (NDC-2177 item 1)

As an admin, I want to choose which departments can schedule replies, so that only teams that need it use it.

  1. Given I open Settings, then I can switch Scheduled Replies on or off for each department.

  2. Given it is off for a department, then agents on its tickets do not see "Schedule", and the API refuses to schedule there.

  3. Given I switch it off while replies are pending, then I am told how many are pending and what will happen to them.

Story 2 — Choose what cancels a scheduled reply (item 2)

As an admin, I want to decide whether a customer reply or a customer closing the ticket cancels a scheduled reply, so that we don't send answers the customer no longer needs.

  1. Given "Cancel when the customer replies" is on, when the customer replies before the send time, then the reply is not sent and is saved as a draft.

  2. Given that option is off, then the reply is still sent at its time.

  3. Given "Cancel when the customer closes the ticket from the help center" is on, then the same happens when the customer closes it.

Story 3 — Choose my scheduled-reply notifications (item 3)

As an agent, I want to turn the "sent" and "not sent" notifications on or off, so that I only get the alerts I care about.

  1. Given I turn "sent" off, then I get no notification when my scheduled reply is sent.

  2. Given "not sent" is on, then I am told when a reply is not sent, with the ticket number and the reason.

Story 4 — See a scheduled reply on the ticket (item 4)

As an agent, I want to see on the ticket that a reply is waiting to go out, so that I don't answer the customer twice.

  1. Given a ticket has a pending scheduled reply, then the conversation shows it with a "Scheduled" label and its send time.

  2. Given it is sent, cleared or cancelled, then the label disappears or changes to match.

Story 5 — Manage the scheduled reply from the ticket (item 5)

As an agent, I want to edit, reschedule, send now, clear or discard a scheduled reply from the ticket, so that I don't have to go to the Scheduled Replies page.

  1. Given I open the scheduled reply's menu on the ticket, then I see Edit, Reschedule, Send now, Clear schedule and Discard.

  2. Given I use any of them, then the result is the same as from the Scheduled Replies page.

Story 6 — Schedule and close (item 6)

As an agent, I want to schedule a reply and close the ticket in one step, so that I can finish my work now and the customer still gets the answer later.

  1. Given I choose "Schedule and close ticket", then the reply is scheduled and the ticket is closed.

  2. Given the ticket is closed this way, then the scheduled reply is still sent at its time (it is not cancelled by the close).

  3. Given I reschedule, then I can also choose "Reschedule and close".

Story 7 — Discard a scheduled reply (item 7)

As an agent, I want to throw away a scheduled reply completely, so that no draft is left behind.

  1. Given I choose Discard and confirm, then the reply is deleted, nothing is sent and no draft is saved.

  2. Given I choose Clear schedule instead, then the text is still saved as my draft.

Story 8 — Jump to the reply in the ticket (item 8)

As an agent, I want to open the ticket right at the scheduled reply, so that I can read it in context.

  1. Given I click the row's open action, then the ticket opens scrolled to that reply.

Story 9 — Choose list columns (item 9)

As a team lead, I want to add columns such as Subject, Time zone and Thread owner, so that I can review my team's scheduled replies faster.

  1. Given I open the column chooser, then I can add or remove columns, and my choice is kept next time.

Story 10 — Customer replies first (to confirm, NDC-1851 acceptance criterion)

As an agent, I want my scheduled reply cancelled when the customer writes first, so that I don't send an answer that is out of date.

  1. Given the customer replies before the send time, then the reply is not sent, it is saved as my draft, and I am told why.

To confirm: this needs a real customer email to reach the ticket. Please fix inbound email routing on staging (help.taviportal.com) so we can test this.

Environment
staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: After "Clear schedule" the reply is saved as a draft, but the draft never appears in the ticket's reply box
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Clearing a scheduled reply says "Schedule cleared. The reply is saved as your draft on the ticket." The draft is really saved, but when the agent opens the ticket and clicks Reply, the reply box is empty — the draft is never shown. Worse, that hidden draft then blocks clearing any other scheduled reply on the same ticket ("You already have a draft on this ticket"), and the agent has no way in the screen to find or discard it.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Schedule a reply on an email ticket.

  2. Open Scheduled Replies, open the row menu and choose Clear schedule.

  3. Open the ticket and click Reply All.

Expected result

The reply box opens with the cleared reply's recipients, subject and text, ready to edit or send.

Actual result

The reply box shows only the quoted history. The page does load the draft from the server (status 200, one draft by this agent with the original text), but does not show it. Clearing a second scheduled reply on the same ticket is then refused with "The author already has a draft on this ticket. Send or discard that draft first." Reproduced on 7 October.

Additional notes

The only way out today is deleting the draft through the API. QA inbox addresses are masked in the screenshot.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Replies can be scheduled on phone, web and chat tickets, although scheduling is for email tickets only
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Scheduled replies are meant only for tickets that came in by email (NDC-1851; the app even has the message "Only replies on email tickets can be scheduled."). But on a phone, web or chat ticket the reply box still offers Schedule, and the reply is scheduled without any warning.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open a ticket whose channel is Phone (or Web, or Chat).

  2. Click Reply, type a message, open the arrow next to Send and choose Schedule.

  3. Pick "In 12 hours" and confirm.

Expected result

Schedule is not offered on non-email tickets, or it is refused with "Only replies on email tickets can be scheduled."

Actual result

Schedule is offered and the message "Reply scheduled for …" appears. The server accepts scheduling on phone, web and chat tickets (status 201), even a phone ticket with no contact email. Reproduced on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: A private reply, or one with an attachment from another ticket, is accepted for scheduling but then silently fails at the send time
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Some replies are accepted when they are scheduled, then refused when the time comes to send them. The reply ends as "Not sent — Refused by the mail service", no draft is kept, and the agent's text is lost. This happens for a private reply, and for a reply with an attachment uploaded on another ticket.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Schedule a reply marked private (not public), due in 1 minute.
  2. Separately, schedule a reply with an attachment that was uploaded on a different ticket, due in 1 minute.
  3. Wait until after the due time and check both on the Scheduled Replies page (Not sent filter).

Expected result

A reply that cannot be sent is refused when it is scheduled, the same way sending it immediately is refused (a private reply sent now is refused with "REPLY_PRIVATE_TO_CUSTOMER"). An attachment that is allowed when sending now should also be allowed when scheduled.

Actual result

Both are accepted (status 201). At the due time both end "Not sent", reason "rejected", with no reply and no draft. Sending the same attachment immediately works. Reproduced on 7 October (private case).

Additional notes

The list label "Refused by the mail service" is misleading — the mail service was never reached.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium and API, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Reply emails are not cleaned: script tags, onerror attributes and javascript: links reach the customer
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Unsafe HTML in a reply's text is stored and emailed to the customer unchanged. Script tags, image onerror attributes, javascript: links and iframes all arrive in the customer's email. Desk's own screens show the text safely, but the email is not cleaned. This affects replies sent immediately as well as scheduled ones.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Schedule (or send) a reply whose text contains <script>alert(1)</script>, <img src=x onerror=alert(2)> and <a href="javascript:alert(3)">x</a>.
  2. Open the received email's source.

Expected result

Scripts, event attributes, javascript: links and iframes are removed before the reply is stored and sent.

Actual result

The received email contains all of them unchanged. Reproduced on 7 October.

Additional notes

Most email clients block scripts, but customers using clients or viewers that render the HTML could be exposed, and it could be used by someone with agent access.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, API and QA inbox, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: The author is not told when someone else sends their scheduled reply with "Send now"
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When a team lead sends another agent's scheduled reply with "Send now" (one row or in bulk), the agent who wrote it gets no notification. A manual "Send now" never creates the "scheduled reply sent" notification at all — only automatic sends do.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Agent A schedules a reply on a ticket.
  2. The team lead opens Scheduled Replies → All Scheduled Replies and uses Send now on that row (or selects it and uses the bulk Send now).
  3. Agent A checks their notifications.

Expected result

Agent A is told their reply was sent (and by whom), as happens for an automatic send.

Actual result

Agent A receives nothing. The reply is sent and shows Agent A as the sender, but there is no notification for either the author or the person who pressed Send now. Reproduced on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium and API, 7 October 2026, admin account and agent account.

raw_module_items.name: A scheduled reply to an address that does not exist is reported as "Sent"
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A scheduled reply addressed to an email that cannot exist is shown as "Sent", and the agent gets "Your scheduled reply was sent". It is never marked "Not sent", and no "not sent" notification arrives, even 20 minutes later.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Schedule a reply due in 1–2 minutes with To = an address on a domain that cannot exist (for example …@something.invalid).

  2. Wait 20 minutes.

  3. Check the reply on Scheduled Replies and the agent's notifications.

Expected result

Status "Not sent" with reason "Not delivered" or "Refused by the mail service", and a "not sent" notification to the agent.

Actual result

Status Sent, no reason, the ticket reply shows "sent" with no bounce, and the agent is told it was sent. Reproduced on 7 October.

Additional notes

This may come from the general email sending setup (no bounce feedback reaching Desk on staging) rather than from scheduling itself.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium and API, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Scheduled-reply notifications do not say which ticket or why a reply was not sent
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Every scheduled-reply notification looks the same: "Your scheduled reply was sent" or "Your scheduled reply could not be sent", with no ticket number, subject or reason. In the bell list the title is also cut to "Your scheduled …", so the agent has to open each one to know what it is about.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Let a few scheduled replies send, and let one be cancelled because its ticket was merged or marked as spam.

  2. Open the notification bell.

Expected result

Each notification names the ticket (number or subject) and, when not sent, the reason ("The ticket was merged", "The ticket was marked as spam", "Refused by the mail service").

Actual result

All titles are generic and the body is empty. The reason is stored in the notification data but not shown (only the "ticket closed" case writes it in the title). Reproduced on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: "Scheduled for" on the Scheduled Replies list has no time zone and uses a different zone from the schedule picker
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The schedule picker and its confirmation say the time with a zone ("Reply scheduled for Oct 9, 2026, 10:00 AM UTC"). The Scheduled Replies list then shows the same reply as "09/10/2026 13:00" with no zone, because the list uses the account's time-zone setting while the picker uses the browser's. The detail panel shows a third format ("Oct 9, 2026, 1:00 PM"), also without a zone.

Steps to reproduce

  1. With the browser in UTC (account time zone Cairo), schedule a reply for a date at 10:00 UTC. Note the confirmation message.

  2. Open Scheduled Replies and read "Scheduled for".

  3. Click the row and read "Scheduled for" in the panel.

Expected result

The list and panel show the same time as the confirmation, in the same zone, with the zone named.

Actual result

The list shows 13:00 with no zone (3 hours different from the message the agent just saw); the panel uses a different date format. The times themselves are correct for the account's zone. Reproduced on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account. QA inbox masked.

raw_module_items.name: Saving a reply that was paused past its time says "scheduled again" but sends it at once
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

If an agent edits a scheduled reply and its send time passes while it is paused, pressing "Save and resume" sends it immediately — which is what the editor's note promises. But the confirmation says "Changes saved. The reply is scheduled again.", so the agent believes it is still waiting.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Schedule a reply for 1 minute from now.
  2. Open Edit on it (it pauses), wait until the time has passed.
  3. Press "Save and resume".

Expected result

A message saying the reply was sent (for example "Reply sent.").

Actual result

The message says "Changes saved. The reply is scheduled again." and the reply is sent within seconds. Reproduced on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account.

The scheduling service refuses an empty reply ("Reply body is required.") only when the text is literally empty. A reply whose text is just an empty paragraph — what an emptied rich-text box produces — is accepted and would be emailed blank.

Accepted (status 201) and scheduled. The reply box in the app blocks this case, so it affects other clients and integrations. Reproduced on 7 October.

raw_module_items.name: Repeating a schedule request with the same key but different content silently returns the old reply
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Each schedule request carries a one-time key so a retried request does not create a duplicate. The key is not tied to what is being scheduled: sending the same key with a different text, a different time, or even a different ticket returns the first scheduled reply and silently ignores the new request.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Schedule a reply with key K, text "first body", in 12 hours.

  2. Schedule again with key K, text "DIFFERENT body", in 4 hours (or on another ticket).

Expected result

A reused key with different content is refused (for example 409 "This key was already used for a different request").

Actual result

Status 200 with the first reply ("first body", 12 hours); the new content is dropped without notice. A key longer than about 255 characters is reported as "The request needs an Idempotency-Key." Reproduced on 7 October.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, API, 7 October 2026, admin account.

Messages such as "The JSON value could not be converted to Anyware.Desk.Contracts.Tickets.ScheduleTimeRequest. Path: $.schedule.delay_minutes | LineNumber: 0 | BytePositionInLine: 295" and "…could not be converted to System.Guid…". Reproduced on 7 October.

Environment

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium and audit API, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: A department-scoped agent can read another department's ticket and its comments through the ticket detail API
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A Desk agent who belongs to one department only can open any ticket from another department by its id. The ticket list and the records API refuse the request, but the ticket detail route and the comments route return the full ticket, including private comments. Department scoping is therefore only half applied.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Sign in to Desk as an agent who is a member of the Call Center department only and has no "all departments" permission (on staging: the QA Desk Agent B account).

  2. Take the id of any ticket that belongs to techSupport (for example a ticket created from an Omnichannel chat in the Support department).

  3. Call GET /api/v1/desk/tickets/{id} and GET /api/v1/desk/tickets/{id}/comments with that agent's token.

  4. For comparison call GET /api/v1/modules/e8e5e302-3873-4e32-b945-c9cd25c7659d/records/{id} and the records list with q= the ticket subject.

Expected result

All four calls refuse the request with 403 (or 404 without revealing that the ticket exists), the same way the records API does.

Actual result

The ticket detail call returns 200 with status, department and the rest of the ticket, and the comments call returns 200 with the comments. Only the records API and the list return 403. Verified on 7 October with ticket #292 (techSupport) read by an agent scoped to Call Center.

Additional notes

Found while running the Omnichannel ↔ Desk integration spec; the scoped agent could also act on tickets in its own department normally (close, comment), which is correct. Full run report: Omnichannel Specs/run-omnichannel-desk-integration-2026-10-07.md (addendum).

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, API, 7 October 2026, QA Desk Agent B account, tenant …0002.

raw_module_items.name: Tickets, Contacts and Tasks module dashboards show 0 or far too few records
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

In Desk Analytics, the Tickets Module, Contacts Module and Tasks Module dashboards show 0 or far too few records. Total Tickets shows 0 for this year although there are 88 tickets that are not spam, and Total Contacts shows 4 although there are 66 contacts. Tasks Module shows 0 everywhere. Each widget adds a "spam is false" condition to its query, and records whose spam flag is empty are dropped, which is almost every record. This is the same problem as NDC-2039 in the Analytics app, now seen in Desk.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Log in to Desk as an admin.

  2. Choose All departments in the department selector.

  3. Open Analytics, then Dashboards, then Module Dashboards, then Tickets Module, with the period This year.

  4. Look at Total Tickets and the charts below it.

  5. Open Contacts Module and Tasks Module the same way.

Expected result

Total Tickets shows the number of tickets created this year that are not spam (88), Total Contacts shows 66, Tasks Module counts the existing task, and the charts show the breakdowns.

Actual result

Total Tickets shows 0 and all 8 ticket charts say "No records match". Total Contacts shows 4. Tasks Module shows 0 on every widget. The same widget query sent again without the spam condition returns the right rows (61 tickets in the department tested, 66 contacts).

Additional notes

All 22 queries on Tickets Module, all 16 on Tasks Module and all 16 on Contacts Module carry the spam condition. The other 11 standard dashboards (Overview, Ticket Status, Happiness and so on) count correctly. The dashboard numbers were checked against the ticket and contact lists.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Double-clicking Save creates two dashboards in Desk Analytics
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

In Desk Analytics, double-clicking Save on a new dashboard creates two identical dashboards instead of one. This is the same problem as NDC-2043 in the Analytics app, now seen in Desk.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Log in to Desk as an admin.

  2. Open Analytics, then Dashboards, then Add Dashboard.

  3. Type a name, for example "QA test".

  4. Double-click Save.

  5. Go back to the dashboards list.

Expected result

One dashboard is created. The second click is ignored while the first save is in progress.

Actual result

Two dashboards with the same name are created. The page sends two create requests about 25 milliseconds apart and both succeed. It happened every time (4 of 4 attempts).

Additional notes

The test dashboards were deleted afterwards.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Saving a dashboard that was changed in another tab fails without any message
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

In Desk Analytics, if a dashboard was saved in another tab (or by another person) while you were editing it, clicking Save does nothing visible. The server refuses the save because the dashboard has changed, but no message is shown, so the user believes the work is saved when it is not. This is the same problem as NDC-2044 in the Analytics app, now seen in Desk.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Log in to Desk as an admin and create a dashboard.

  2. Open the same dashboard in the builder in two browser tabs.

  3. In the second tab, change the name and click Save.

  4. In the first tab, change the name to something else and click Save.

Expected result

The first tab shows a clear message that the dashboard was changed elsewhere, with a way to reload or keep your changes.

Actual result

Nothing is shown. The save request is refused by the server with a "revision conflict" error, the changes are not saved, and the Save button looks ready again. Reproduced every time (3 of 3).

Additional notes

The test dashboards were deleted afterwards.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 7 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: DESK Workflow Missings
raw_module_items.description_html:
Running list of Desk workflow-rule gaps vs Zoho Desk. Tick an item when it ships; add new gaps under the right heading as they are found.

Env: staging-desk.taviportal.com/settings/automation/workflow-rules/new · Tickets module · All layouts. Reference: desk.zoho.com.
Evidence: NDC-workflow-missings-1-triggers.png, NDC-workflow-missings-2-actions.png, NDC-workflow-missings-3-field-update-trigger.png, NDC-workflow-missings-4-department.png, NDC-workflow-missings-5-active-inactive-tabs.png, Items 10–13 (conditions) evidence board, Item 28 (ticket history) evidence board.

Trigger events — 5 missing

  • Customer Reply — needed to reopen a closed ticket on reply

  • Agent Response — first-response SLA stamping

  • Comment

  • Private Thread (incoming / outgoing) ⇒ you can choose to execute the rule for incoming or outgoing email responses or both.

  • Happiness Rating (any / good / okay / bad) — Anyware sends the rating email but cannot react to the rating ⇒ specify the rating from the drop-down lists. You can choose to execute the rule for All Ratings or a particular rating.

Present: Create, Edit, Create or Edit, Field Changed, Delete, date-time trigger.

Note: The rule triggers like Customer Reply, Agent Response, Private Thread, Happiness Ratings and Delete are available only for the Tickets module.

Rule actions — 14 missing

  • Add Comment (public / private)

  • Send Email Reply to the customer

  • Reply via Instant Messaging

  • Notify via Instant Messaging

  • Add Followers

  • Mark Ticket as spam

  • Share Ticket

  • Change Layout

  • Custom Functions

  • Send Cliq Notification (external action)

  • Add Skills — blocked: no Skills feature in Anyware Desk

  • Remove Skills — blocked: same

  • Recalculate Skills — blocked: same

  • Reassign ticket based on Skills — blocked: same

Present: Field Update, Add Tags, Remove Tags, Task, plus Anyware-only Webhook, Create Record, Send happiness email, Scheduled actions.

Partial — present but reduced

  • Assign Tickets — “Owner Assignment” sets one owner only; no team, round-robin or load balancing

  • Alerts — “Email” is a plain platform email; no alert template, no users / teams / contact recipient picker

  • Field Changed trigger — watch up to 3 fields in one rule (Anyware's Watch Field takes only one, so watching three fields needs three separate rules)

  • Field Changed trigger — All / Any option, so the rule fires when all or any of the watched fields are updated

Conditions — criteria builder

  • Contact and Account fields in conditions — Zoho's field list is grouped into Tickets / Contacts / Accounts; Anyware offers ticket fields only, and searching "Contact" finds only the ticket's own Contact lookup

  • Business hours / holiday condition — Zoho's "Execution Time": during / outside business hours of, on / not a holiday of; not offered

  • Missing ticket fields — the picker offers 21 fields and leaves out 20: Name, Ticket Number, Team, Created Time, Created By, Modified Time, Modified By, Closed Time, Response Due Date, First Response Time, Happiness Rating, Happiness Link Status, Spam, Customer Responded, Pending Review, Archived, Shared Departments, SLA Name, SLA Violated, SLA Escalated. Zoho also offers Recent Comment, Recent Comment Type, Is Escalated, Is Overdue and Number of Threads / Comments

  • Operator "doesn't contain" for text fields — missing from the picker (the engine already supports it)

  • Date operators "between" / "not between" — missing from the picker (the engine already supports Between)

  • "Current Time" as a value in date conditions — missing

Other gaps

Add newly found workflow gaps here.

  • “Or use a saved action” offers no route to the missing actions — the saved-action library is built from the same 9 action types, and Custom Functions is itself missing

  • Department-scoped rules — Zoho creates each rule inside a department (picker in the rule header); Anyware has no department picker, so a Tickets rule runs on every department

  • Active / Inactive tabs on the Workflow Rules list — Anyware shows status per row but has no tabs or status filter, so active and inactive rules are mixed in one list

  • Ticket history doesn't name the workflow rule — entries read "Tags changed … by System", with no rule name, action, status or failure reason. Zoho records Rule Name, Action Name, Status and Reason (per its docs; not seen live). Today a rule's run can only be traced on Setup › Execution History by pasting the ticket's record ID

raw_module_items.name: Workflow Rules | Owner Assignment › Roles lists CRM profiles instead of Desk's roles
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When setting up a Desk workflow rule with an Owner Assignment action, the Roles list doesn't show Desk's roles. It shows the profiles defined in CRM, and new CRM profiles appear there too. An admin can end up assigning Desk records round-robin to the members of a CRM profile without realising it.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. In Desk, go to Settings › Automation › Workflow Rules and click New Rule.

  2. Choose the Accounts module, leave All layouts, enter a rule name, click Next, then Create.

  3. Under Instant actions, click Add action and choose Owner Assignment.

  4. Under Assign owner to, click Roles and open the Select… list. The list shows CRM Admin, Manager, Supervisor, test, User.

  5. Open Desk Settings › Roles. Desk's roles are CEO and Manager.

raw_module_items.name: Workflow Rules | On Edit and On Field Changed rules fire on newly created tickets
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A ticket that has just been created, and that nobody has touched since, is treated as if it had been edited. The On Edit and On Field Changed workflow rules run on it straight away, alongside the On Create rule. Any action meant to happen only when a ticket is changed later (tags, alerts, assignments) also happens on every new ticket.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. In Desk, go to Settings › Automation › Workflow Rules and make sure these three rules are active on Tickets (Standard layout). Each has the condition Priority is one of High, Urgent:

    • On Create: adds the tag "Newly Created" and updates Description to "Workflow Completed".

    • On Edit: adds the tag "Recently Edited".

    • On Field Changed, watching Subject: adds the tag "Field Changed".

  2. Submit a new ticket through the Desk web form with Priority High (any subject, name and email).

  3. In Desk, open Tickets and open the new ticket.

  4. Look at the tags under the ticket title.

Expected Result

  • When the ticket is created, only the On Create rule runs. The ticket gets the Newly Created tag and its description is updated to "Workflow Completed".

  • The On Edit rule runs only when someone edits and saves the ticket after it was created.

  • The On Field Changed rule runs only when the watched field (Subject) is changed on the ticket after it was created. Filling in the Subject when the ticket is created doesn't count as a change.

  • Changes made by a workflow's own actions, such as the On Create rule's Field Update, don't count as an edit and don't trigger the On Edit rule.

  • The new ticket ends up with Newly Created as its only tag.

Actual Result

  • The ticket has three tags: Newly Created, Field Changed and Recently Edited.

  • The On Edit and On Field Changed rules ran even though the ticket was only just created and nobody edited it.

  • The description reads "Workflow Completed", so the On Create rule also ran as expected.

Environment

raw_module_items.name: Workflow Rules | Rules that run on a Date-Time field can't be saved — "An unexpected error occurred"
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A workflow rule set to run on a Date-Time field (for example, 1 day before a ticket's Due Date) can't be saved. Clicking Save & Activate shows "An unexpected error occurred" every time, and the rule is lost when the user leaves the page. Rules that run on a record action (such as Create) save normally.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. In Desk, go to Settings › Automation › Workflow Rules and click New Rule.

  2. Choose Tickets, layout Standard, enter a rule name and click Create.

  3. Under Execute based on, choose A Date-Time field.

  4. Set Date Field to Due Date, Run to 1 Days before and Counting to Elapsed time. Leave Rule mode on Recurring and click Done.

  5. Add the condition Priority = Urgent.

  6. Under Instant actions, add Add Tags and choose a tag (e.g. "Top Priority").

  7. Click Save & Activate.

  8. For comparison, create another rule the same way but choose A Record Action › Create in step 3, then click Save & Activate.

Expected Result

  • The Date-Time rule saves and is activated: a "Workflow rule saved successfully" message appears, and the rule shows in the Workflow Rules list.

  • Rules that run on a Date-Time field save the same way as rules that run on a record action.

  • If any part of the rule can't be accepted, the message says which setting to change.

Actual Result

  • The message "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again." appears, and the rule is not saved.

  • Clicking Save & Activate again shows the same error.

  • Leaving the page asks to discard changes, and the rule is lost.

  • The comparison rule (step 8) saves successfully.

Environment

  • App: Anyware Desk (staging) — staging-desk.taviportal.com/settings/automation/workflow-rules/new?moduleId=88e8ea44-1658-4df3-9930-d0902b91073d

raw_module_items.name: Merging tickets does not move time entries to the master ticket
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When two tickets are merged, conversations, comments and attachments move to the master ticket, but time entries do not. The merged ticket keeps its time and the master shows none, although the merge page says every time entry moves to the master. Because nothing moved, unmerging cannot bring the time back either.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create two open tickets in techSupport for the same contact.

  2. On the second ticket, add a 15-minute time entry.

  3. Open the first ticket, choose More ticket actions, then Merge, tick the second ticket, press Continue, then Merge and Yes, Merge.

  4. Open the Time Entry tab of both tickets.

Expected result

The 15-minute entry is on the master ticket, as the merge page promises ("Every conversation, comment, attachment and time entry moves to the master"), and comes back to the ticket if it is unmerged.

Actual result

The merge returns success but reports 0 time entries moved. The master shows "0 TIME ENTRY" and the merged ticket still holds its 15-minute (900 s) entry. The same happens with a bulk merge from the ticket list and with the merge API. Unmerge also reports 0 time entries. Reproduced on staging and twice on desk.anyware.software on 11 October.

Additional notes

Found while retesting the Merge Tickets items (NDC-1963, NDC-2093, NDC-2094). Email addresses in the screenshot are masked.

Environment

desk.anyware.software, Chromium, 11 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: A ticket shared with a department cannot be opened by that department's agents
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Sharing a ticket with another department is saved, but the agents of that department still cannot open the ticket. The share dialog says "Agents of these departments can open this ticket", yet for them the ticket does not exist.

Steps to reproduce

  1. As an admin, create an open ticket in the Call Center department.

  2. Share it with techSupport, read-only. The share saves and the ticket's share list shows techSupport.

  3. Sign in as an agent who belongs to techSupport only (QA_DESK_Agent_A_User) and open the ticket by its link.

Expected result

The agent can open the ticket read-only.

Actual result

The agent gets "This ticket is not available"; the request for the ticket returns 404 "Ticket … was not found". It stays 404 when checked again after 30 seconds, 90 seconds and 5 minutes. The same agent can open techSupport tickets normally. Reproduced on staging (sharing a techSupport ticket with Call Center) and on desk.anyware.software (sharing a Call Center ticket with techSupport) on 11 October.

Additional notes

On desk.anyware.software there is also no Shared Tickets view where such a ticket could be found (separate ticket). Ticket Access is set to hierarchy visibility on this tenant, which may be overriding the share.

Environment

desk.anyware.software, API and Chromium, 11 October 2026, admin account sharing, non-admin techSupport agent viewing.

raw_module_items.name: Spam and Shared Tickets views are missing on desk.anyware.software
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The Spam view and the Shared Tickets view do not exist on desk.anyware.software, although both work on staging. Tickets marked as spam stay in All Tickets with a SPAM badge, and there is nowhere to see tickets shared with your department.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Sign in as admin and open Tickets → Views.

  2. Look for Spam and Shared Tickets in the views list.

  3. Mark a ticket as spam, then open /views/spam and /views/shared directly.

Expected result

Spam Tickets and Shared Tickets appear in the views list. Spam tickets move to the Spam view and leave All Tickets.

Actual result

Neither view is listed, for the admin or for an agent. /views/spam and /views/shared fall back to All Tickets. The ticket marked as spam is still in All Tickets with a SPAM badge. The ticket module on this host has 27 fields and does not have the is_spam and shared_departments fields that these views depend on; on staging both views work.

Additional notes

Marking and unmarking spam, and the 30-day spam auto-delete setting, do work. Feature item NDC-1963.

Environment

desk.anyware.software, Chromium, 11 October 2026, admin account.

Google Drive is installed and enabled as a collaboration connector, but no agent can connect their Drive account. Google blocks the sign-in with "Access blocked: This app's request is invalid", so attaching or sharing Drive files from a ticket cannot be used.

raw_module_items.name: The enable/disable switch on the Web Forms list is invisible
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Web forms can be disabled and re-enabled, but the switch for it cannot be seen. Each row on the Web Forms page has the switch in its code, yet it is drawn with no size, so an admin cannot pause a form and cannot tell which forms are disabled.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Channels → Web Forms.

  2. Look at any feedback widget or advanced form row, and open its ⋮ menu.

Expected result

Each row shows a visible on/off switch (or a Disable / Enable menu entry) and shows when a form is disabled.

Actual result

Each row only shows "Embed code" and the ⋮ menu. The switches named "Disable E2E feedback widget", "Disable test" and "Disable E2E advanced form" are 0 × 0 pixels. The ⋮ menu only offers Edit settings and Delete permanently, even though the delete dialog says "To pause it instead, disable it." A form disabled through the system looks exactly like an active one in this list.

Additional notes

Disabling and enabling work through the system itself, so only the control is missing. Feature item NDC-1666.

Environment

desk.anyware.software, Chromium, 11 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: A support plan can't be removed from a contract, and stays "in use" forever after its contract is deleted
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Once a support plan is attached to a contract, it can't be removed from that contract. After the contract is deleted, the plan is still counted as in use, so neither the plan nor its SLA policy can ever be deleted.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create a support plan with an SLA policy.
  2. Attach the plan to a contract.
  3. Try to remove the plan from the contract (DELETE /desk/sla/contracts/{id}/plan, which is what the UI's clear action sends), or set it to none (PUT the same path with plan_id null).
  4. Delete the contract, which is the only one using the plan.
  5. Delete the plan, then delete its SLA policy.

Expected result

The plan can be removed from a contract. Once no contract uses the plan, the plan and its SLA policy can be deleted.

Actual result

Removing the plan returns 405, and setting plan_id to null returns 400. After the contract is deleted (204), deleting the plan returns 409 SUPPORT_PLAN_IN_USE, and deleting its SLA policy returns 409 SLA_POLICY_IN_USE_BY_PLAN. The only option left is to discontinue the plan and set the policy inactive.

Additional notes

Reproduced twice: on 11 October with plan "QA IF2 Gold" and policy "QA IF2 SLA NY hours", and on 12 October with "QA JG3 Gold Plan" and "QA JG3 SLA Gold". Those four QA records remain in the tenant (discontinued or inactive) because of this bug. Found while retesting NDC-1972.

Environment

desk.anyware.software (build index-DO94wOp8), Chromium + API, 12 October 2026, admin account, tenant …0002.

raw_module_items.name: A business-hours set used by an SLA target can be deleted without warning, and the SLA keeps using the deleted set
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A business-hours set can be deleted while an SLA target still uses it. There is no warning. The SLA target keeps pointing at the deleted set, and the editor shows "Default" instead.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create a business-hours set, for example 09:00–10:00 UTC.
  2. Create an SLA policy with a target whose Operational Hours is that set.
  3. Go to Settings → Business Hours and delete the set.
  4. Open the SLA target again, and create a ticket that matches the target.

Expected result

Deleting is blocked or warns that the set is used by an SLA. If it is allowed, the target moves to a valid set that the editor shows.

Actual result

The delete returns 204 with no warning. The target editor shows Operational Hours "Default (default)", but the API still returns business_hours_id = the deleted set. A ticket created at 07:07 UTC got a first-response due time of 09:30 UTC, so it was still calculated on the deleted set.

Additional notes

Found while retesting NDC-1971. The QA business-hours set, policy and tickets were removed afterwards, except for the policy that is blocked by the support-plan bug filed alongside this one.

Environment

desk.anyware.software (build index-DO94wOp8), Chromium, 12 October 2026, admin account, tenant …0002.

raw_module_items.name: Company currency and primary contact can't be cleared once set
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Once the company currency or primary contact is set in Organization → Company, it can't be set back to empty.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Settings → Organization → Company → Company Details.

  2. Set Currency to Euro and save.

  3. Clear Currency with the × (Not set) and save.

  4. Reload the page. Do the same for Primary contact.

Expected result

The currency (and the primary contact) is cleared and stays empty after reload.

Actual result

Save succeeds, but Currency still shows Euro. PUT /iam/tenant/company-profile with currency null returns 200, and the profile still has EUR. The primary contact also can't be cleared; it stays stored as an explicit choice.

Additional notes

Found while retesting NDC-1969. Because of this bug, the test tenant's currency is now EUR and could not be reverted.

Environment

desk.anyware.software (build index-DO94wOp8), Chromium, 12 October 2026, admin account, tenant …0002.

raw_module_items.name: Tickets | Ticket Owner filter lists CRM users alongside Desk agents
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

In Desk's ticket list, the Ticket Owner filter offers people who exist only in the CRM, not just Desk agents. Agents can pick a name that can never own a ticket. Because one CRM user has almost the same name as a Desk agent, it's also easy to filter by the wrong person.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. In Desk, open Tickets › All Tickets and click the Filter icon.

  2. Expand Ticket Owner and scroll through the list of names.

  3. Open Desk Settings › User Management › Agents and compare the two lists.

Expected Result

  • The Ticket Owner filter lists only Desk agents, the 10 shown on the Agents page.

  • Agents who exist Desk are the only users that can be listed within Desk Application

Actual Result

  • The filter also lists ZZ Sweep Tavi Delegate, ZZ Sweep Tavi Probe, test user 1 and test user 2. None of them is a Desk agent; all four are CRM users only.

  • Test User 1 (a Desk agent) and test user 1 (a CRM user) appear one under the other, so it's easy to choose the wrong one.

Environment

  • App: Anyware Desk (staging) — staging-desk.taviportal.com/views/all

  • Compared against: Desk Settings › Agents, and CRM (staging-crm.taviportal.com) Settings › Users

  • Browser: Microsoft Edge, Windows

  • Reporter: Moaz Adly

  • Captured: 12 Oct 2026

Attachment

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields | A CRM Admin profile gives module and field administration inside Desk
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A user who has the Desk Agent profile in Desk and the CRM Admin profile in CRM gets CRM Admin's metadata permissions inside Desk, so an agent can open and change Setup → Modules and Fields.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Give a user the Desk Agent profile (Desk) and the CRM Admin profile (CRM).

  2. Sign in to Desk as that user.

  3. Open Setup → Modules and Fields.

  4. Call GET /api/v1/iam/me/permissions with header x-app-key: desk.

Expected result

Only Desk Agent permissions apply in Desk (metadata.records.access, metadata.records.manage). Modules and Fields says "You don't have permission to view this page".

Actual result

The page opens with the full module table and "Create New Module". The permissions response contains CRM Admin's metadata permissions.

Request

GET /api/v1/iam/me/permissions  (x-app-key: desk)

Response

200 — includes metadata.modules.manage, metadata.fields.manage_permissions, metadata.capabilities.manage, metadata.views.manage, metadata.integrations.manage, metadata.records.convert. GET /api/v1/iam/profiles/{desk_agent_id}/effective lists only metadata.records.access and metadata.records.manage.

Evidence

Attached: the annotated image (TAVI vs Zoho, numbered boxes and an expected-vs-actual table) and the original screenshot.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com (tenant NDC-Staging), TAVI Desk web app, headless Chromium, 5–6 Oct 2026; Gmail test user with Desk Agent + CRM Admin.

Additional notes

  • Severity: Critical. Spec row SEC-1 in docs/desk-modules-fields/spec-desk-modules-fields.md (QA repository), functional run 1.

  • MF-11 (Access Control picker lists CRM users) is the same family: Desk reads CRM data.

  • Full bug report: docs/desk-modules-fields/desk-modules-fields-bug-report.md (MF-01).

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields | Profiles chosen in the Create Module dialog are not applied
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When a module is created with "Module Permission" limited to some profiles, the limit is silently lost: the request that saves it returns 404 and the module stays open to everyone.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Setup → Modules and Fields → Create New Module.

  2. Name "QA MF Closed", Module Permission: tick only Desk Administrator → Create.

  3. Sign in as a Desk Agent.

  4. Open the "+" create menu and the module page; create a record.

Expected result

The agent does not see the module and cannot read or create its records. If saving the permission fails, the dialog shows an error.

Actual result

No error is shown. The agent sees the module (sidebar and "+" menu), lists its records and creates a record. Access Control on the module still shows "All Users".

Request

PUT /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/permissions
{"profileIds":["44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444401"]}

Response

404 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"The requested resource was not found."}}. As the agent afterwards: GET /modules/{module_id}/records → 200; POST /modules/{module_id}/records → 201.

Evidence

Attached: the annotated image (TAVI vs Zoho, numbered boxes and an expected-vs-actual table) and the original screenshot.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com (tenant NDC-Staging), TAVI Desk web app, headless Chromium, 6–7 Oct 2026; tenant owner creates the module; Desk Agent account (mahmoud.mohamed1, profile lowered for the test) checks access.

Additional notes

  • Severity: Critical. Spec row H10 in docs/desk-modules-fields/spec-desk-modules-fields.md (QA repository), functional run 2.

  • Full bug report: docs/desk-modules-fields/desk-modules-fields-bug-report.md (MF-02).

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields | Records can be saved without the required Name field
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The record API accepts a record with no Name although Name is required on the layout.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Use a custom module whose default layout has the required Name field.

  2. Send the request below with no "name" value.

400/422 — Name is required (as for other required fields, see I4).

201 Created; the record has no name.

POST /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/records
{"data":[],"layout_id":"{default_layout_id}"}

201 Created (also 201 without layout_id).

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields | A saved field's data type can be changed
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

An existing field can be switched to another data type through the API; existing values are left unconverted.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create a single-line field and save a record with text in it.

  2. Send the request below to change its type to number.

  3. Read the field and the record.

Expected result

Refused (Zoho: "the field type cannot be changed").

Actual result

200; the field is now a number field and the old text value stays as text.

Request

PUT /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/fields/{field_id}
{"fieldName":"qa_sl","labels":{"en":"QA MF sl"},"datatypeKey":"number","required":false,"unique":false,"uniquePeerModuleIds":[]}

Response

200 OK — datatypeKey "number".

Evidence

API only — see the request and response above.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com (tenant NDC-Staging), TAVI Desk web app, headless Chromium, 5–6 Oct 2026; admin account (Desk Administrator).

Additional notes

  • Severity: High. Spec row I13 in docs/desk-modules-fields/spec-desk-modules-fields.md (QA repository), functional run 1.

raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Email, phone and URL fields accept invalid values; a javascript: URL is a stored-XSS risk wherever URLs become links.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create email, phone and URL fields on the default layout.

  2. Send a record with the values below.

Expected result

400/422 for each invalid value; javascript: URLs always refused.

Actual result

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields | A required field can be set to "Don't Show"
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Field Permissions lets an admin hide a required field from a profile; that profile can then no longer create any record.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Module → Fields → Field Permissions → profile Desk Agent.

  2. Set Name (required) to "Don't Show" → Save.

  3. As a Desk Agent, create a record (form or API).

Expected result

"Don't Show" disabled for required fields, or Save refused with a message.

Actual result

Saved ("3 field permissions updated"). Every agent create then fails with 422 "One or more fields in the payload are not writable for your profile."

Request

POST /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/field-permissions
{"fieldId":"{name_field_id}","profileId":"44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444402","permission":"hidden"}
then as the agent: POST /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/records {"data":[{"field":"name","value":{"kind":"string","value":"QA MF agent rec"}}]}

Response

field-permissions → 200/201. Agent record → 422 "One or more fields in the payload are not writable for your profile."

Evidence

Attached: the annotated image (TAVI vs Zoho, numbered boxes and an expected-vs-actual table) and the original screenshot.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com (tenant NDC-Staging), TAVI Desk web app, headless Chromium, 6–7 Oct 2026; tenant owner; Desk Agent account (mahmoud.mohamed1, profile lowered for the test).

Additional notes

  • Severity: High. Spec row H4 in docs/desk-modules-fields/spec-desk-modules-fields.md (QA repository), functional run 2.

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields | Access Control picker lists CRM users and profiles instead of Desk ones
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The "Select principals" picker used by module Access Control and Layout Permissions loads CRM users and profiles, so a layout or module cannot be limited to a Desk profile or a Desk agent.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open a layout → Layout settings → Layout Permissions (or a module → Access Control).

  2. Choose Selected Users → Select principals.

  3. Switch the kind to Profiles; then search Users for a Desk agent.

Expected result

Desk profiles (Desk Administrator, Supervisor, Agent, Light Agent, Reviewer) and Desk agents.

Actual result

Profiles: CRM Admin, Manager, Supervisor, test, User. The Desk agent mahmoud.mohamed1@taviportal.com is not found.

Request

GET /api/v1/iam/users?app_key=crm  (sent by the picker; also GET /iam/profiles, /iam/org-units)

Response

200 — CRM users only. Note: a limit set through the API with the Desk Agent profile id is enforced correctly (G10 passed).

Evidence

Attached: the annotated image (TAVI vs Zoho, numbered boxes and an expected-vs-actual table) and the original screenshot.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com (tenant NDC-Staging), TAVI Desk web app, headless Chromium, 6–7 Oct 2026; tenant owner.

Additional notes

  • Severity: High. Spec row G10, H9 in docs/desk-modules-fields/spec-desk-modules-fields.md (QA repository), functional run 2.

  • Same root cause as the CRM users/profiles shown in other Desk pickers: NDC-2204, NDC-1915.

  • Full bug report: docs/desk-modules-fields/desk-modules-fields-bug-report.md (MF-11).

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields | Field dependency rules (SHOW / REQUIRE) are saved but not applied
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Field Dependency rules are stored and listed, but neither the record form nor the record API applies them.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Layout QA MF L-Agent: add rules "When QA MF e2e_kind = Hardware → Show QA MF e2e_serial" and "→ Require QA MF e2e_serial".

  2. As a Desk Agent: "+" → QA MF Open1 → choose layout QA MF L-Agent.

  3. Look at QA MF e2e_serial before choosing a kind; choose Hardware; leave serial empty; Save.

Expected result

Serial hidden until Hardware is chosen; then required; Save blocked. The API refuses the same record.

Actual result

Serial is visible before Hardware; the record saves with serial empty ("Record saved successfully"); the API returns 201. Same on module QA MF Deps (SHOW qa_b / REQUIRE qa_c when ctrl = Z).

Request

PUT /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/layouts/{layout_id}  (…"dependencies":[{"id":"{uuid}","parentFieldId":"{kind_id}","parentValues":["Hardware"],"action":"SHOW","childFieldIds":["{serial_id}"]},{"id":"{uuid}","parentFieldId":"{kind_id}","parentValues":["Hardware"],"action":"REQUIRE","childFieldIds":["{serial_id}"]}])
then as the agent: POST /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/records {"data":[{"field":"name","value":{"kind":"string","value":"QA MF E2E hw no serial"}},{"field":"qa_e2e_kind","value":{"kind":"string","value":"Hardware"}}],"layout_id":"{layout_id}"}

Response

Layout PUT → 200 (2 rules stored). Record → 201 Created.

Evidence

Attached: the annotated image (TAVI vs Zoho, numbered boxes and an expected-vs-actual table) and the original screenshot.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com (tenant NDC-Staging), TAVI Desk web app, headless Chromium, 6–7 Oct 2026; tenant owner sets the rules; Desk Agent account (mahmoud.mohamed1, profile lowered for the test) creates the record.

  • Full bug report: docs/desk-modules-fields/desk-modules-fields-bug-report.md (MF-33).

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields | Department storage has no effect on records
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A module created with Module Data Storage = Department stores records without a department, and every user sees every record.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create New Module "QA MF DeptMod" with Module Data Storage = Department.

  2. Create records: plain, with header x-department-id, and with department_id in the body.

  3. List the records as an agent who belongs only to "QA MF Dept", and as an admin.

Expected result

Each record belongs to a department; users see only their departments' records.

Actual result

All creates return 201; records carry no department field; the agent and the admin see the same 4 records; the list is the same with or without a department header.

Request

POST /api/v1/teamspaces/{teamspace_id}/modules {"moduleKey":"qa_mf_deptmod","labels":{"en":"QA MF DeptMod"},"pluralForm":"QA MF DeptMod","singularForm":"QA MF DeptMod1","storageScope":"department"}
POST /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/records {"data":[{"field":"name","value":{"kind":"string","value":"QA MF dept rec hdr"}}]}  (header x-department-id: {department_id})
POST /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/records {"data":[…],"department_id":"{department_id}"}

Module 201 (storageScope "department"). Records 201 ×3, no department in the stored record. GET records → same 3–4 records for every user and header.

A File Upload field limited to PDF and 1 MB accepts other file types and larger files, on the form and through the API, with no message.

  1. Create File Upload field "QA MF file" with allowed extensions [pdf], max 1 MB, and Image Upload "QA MF img" with [png], 1 MB.

raw_module_items.description_html:

Two saves of a module with the same rowVersion both succeed; the stale one silently overwrites the other.

  1. GET /api/v1/modules/{module_id} and note rowVersion.

  3. Send PUT with description "tab two (stale)" and the same rowVersion.

Second PUT → 409 Conflict.

Both 200; description is "tab two (stale)".

Request

PUT /api/v1/modules/{module_id}
{"pluralForm":"QA MF Devices","singularForm":"QA MF Device","description":"tab two (stale)","rowVersion":{same_n}}

Response

200 OK (twice).

Evidence

API only — see the request and response above.

raw_module_items.name: Modules and Fields | Record API stores values for fields that do not exist
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The record API accepts and keeps values for field names that do not exist on the module; they later collide with real fields.

Steps to reproduce

  1. On a module without field qa_uq, send the request below.

  2. Later create qa_uq as a unique field.

  3. Create a new record with qa_uq = "QA-UQ-1".

Expected result

Unknown field refused (400).

Actual result

First record 201 and the value is kept; after qa_uq is created, the new record is refused as a duplicate (422 "already in use").

Request

POST /api/v1/modules/{module_id}/records
{"data":[{"field":"name","value":{"kind":"string","value":"QA MF uq 1"}},{"field":"qa_uq","value":{"kind":"string","value":"QA-UQ-1"}}],"layout_id":"{default_layout_id}"}

Response

201 Created; later 422 RECORD_FIELD_INVALID "QA MF uq is already in use by another record."

Evidence

API only — see the request and response above.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com (tenant NDC-Staging), TAVI Desk web app, headless Chromium, 6–7 Oct 2026; tenant owner.

Additional notes

  • Severity: Medium. Spec row I7 (setup) in docs/desk-modules-fields/spec-desk-modules-fields.md (QA repository), functional run 2.

  • Full bug report: docs/desk-modules-fields/desk-modules-fields-bug-report.md (MF-40).

raw_module_items.name: SLA and Escalation: features Zoho Desk has that Desk is missing
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

We compared Desk's new SLA and Escalation feature with Zoho Desk. This ticket lists only what Desk has not built yet; the user-story check is in NDC-2267. The feature spec is NDC-1971 (SLA policies and escalations); it has no list of requirements, so each item below says which related item covers it, where one exists.

Missing — escalation

  1. Escalate to roles and to the customer's contacts. Zoho lets a level notify roles, the ticket owner, contacts and chosen users. Today Desk offers agents, teams, ticket owner, owner's manager and department agents only. Tested: saving a level with a role or contact recipient is rejected as an unknown recipient type.
  2. Choose the notification email for each escalation level. Zoho picks an escalation email template per level. Today every level uses one built-in default escalation email, and the screen says "Email templates are not available yet". Desk's email templates exist but none is for SLA escalation.

Missing — where agents see results

  1. Countdown view in the ticket list: columns of tickets grouped by time left to the due time, up to 7 columns, with an On Hold column. Today there is no countdown view anywhere in the app.

Could not be checked

Not tested in this run: (a) Overdue and Response Overdue tickets leave the overdue views when put On Hold; (b) "Is overdue" and "Is response overdue" can be used as criteria in custom views, reports and automation; (c) a ticket counts as resolved for the SLA only when its status is Closed; (d) the Desk SLA dashboard has no "violations by hour of day" widget (Zoho has one) — to confirm by opening the dashboard.

Additional notes

Not gaps, and tested on staging on 14 October 2026: SLA applied within seconds of ticket creation with exact due times; violation flag; two response and four resolution escalation levels (same as Zoho), each firing once and setting the priority; closed tickets never escalate; an On Hold ticket stops the clock and the due times come back correctly when it is reopened; contract, account and general policy order; conditions; targets up to 50 per policy and 25 conditions per target (Zoho allows 10 targets). Also built: 7 triggers, account and contract SLAs, support plans with allowance, several business-hours sets with two holiday lists, impact check and reapply, and the "Desk SLA" dashboard in Analytics. Zoho has no SLA or escalation history log and no SLA API we could find. Already covered by other items: time-based (supervise) rules by NDC-1973; the Overdue, Response Overdue and SLA Violated views by NDC-1964.

Two bugs already filed and not repeated here: NDC-2215 and NDC-2216. A possible bug to check separately: the Analytics library lists two "Desk SLA" dashboards (v1 and v2).

Test spec: Desk Specs/spec-desk-sla-escalation.md; run report Desk Specs/run-desk-sla-escalation-2026-10-14.md in the QA repository.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, API, 14 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: SLA and Escalation: user stories for the functions not built yet
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

One user story for each function listed in NDC-2266 (SLA and Escalation: features Zoho Desk has that Desk is missing). Only what is not built is covered. The On Hold and criteria checks in NDC-2266 have not been confirmed yet, so they are not written as stories.

Story 1 — Escalate to roles and customer contacts

As a support manager, I want an escalation level to notify roles and the customer's contacts, so that the right people hear about a late ticket without picking each person.

  1. Given I edit an escalation level, when I open "Whom to Escalate", then I can add a role.

  2. Given I edit an escalation level, when I open "Whom to Escalate", then I can add the ticket's contact.

  3. Given a level has a role, when the ticket is late, then every active member of that role gets the notification.

  4. Given a level has the contact, when the ticket is late, then the contact gets the email.

Story 2 — Choose the escalation email

As a support manager, I want to pick an email template for each escalation level, so that the message matches how urgent the level is.

  1. Given I edit an escalation level, when I open "Agent Notification Template", then I can choose any escalation email template, not only the default.

  2. Given I choose a template, when the level fires, then the email uses that template's subject and text with the ticket details filled in.

  3. Given the chosen template is later deleted, when I open the level, then I see a clear message and the default email is used.

Story 3 — Countdown view

As a support agent, I want to see my tickets in columns by time left to the due time, so that I work on the ones about to be late first.

  1. Given I open the ticket list, when I switch to the countdown view, then I see columns such as overdue, due in 1 hour, due today.

  2. Given the view is open, when a ticket gets close to its due time, then it moves to the next column without a page reload.

  3. Given a ticket is On Hold, when I look at the view, then it appears only in the On Hold column.

  4. Given I choose columns, when I add more than 7, then I am stopped with a clear message.

Additional notes

Gap list: NDC-2266. Spec: Desk Specs/spec-desk-sla-escalation.md. Nothing was changed on the tenant.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 14 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Desk new Requirements
raw_module_items.description_html:
Client Requirements – Ticket Management & Notifications

  1. Multiple Tickets per Client

    • The system should allow creating multiple tickets for the same client.

  2. Automatic Ticket Creation from Omnichannel to Desk

    • Integrate Omnichannel with Desk to automatically create and transfer a ticket whenever negative feedback is received.

  3. Comment Notifications via Email

    • When a comment is added to a ticket, the system should send it to the client as a new email notification.

    • The email should use a customizable email template.

    • The email must be sent as a new email, not added to the existing email thread.

raw_module_items.name: A deactivated holiday list still counts as a holiday in SLA due times
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

After a holiday list is deactivated, SLA due times still skip its holidays. The screen says "Holiday list deactivated. Its holidays were kept." and the list shows as inactive, but tickets still get due times that jump over the holiday.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create a business-hours set that is open 09:00–10:00 every day.

  2. Create a holiday list attached to that set with one holiday tomorrow.

  3. Create an SLA policy with a target that uses that business-hours set and responds within 30 minutes.

  4. Create a ticket outside the open hours. Its response due time skips tomorrow (the day after tomorrow, 09:30).

  5. Deactivate the holiday list. Check that it shows as inactive.

  6. Wait 35 seconds and create another ticket.

Expected result

The inactive list no longer affects due times. The second ticket is due tomorrow at 09:30.

Actual result

The second ticket gets exactly the same due time as the first (day after tomorrow, 09:30, shown as 2026-10-16 06:30 UTC). The holiday is still skipped. The list was confirmed inactive in the response.

Additional notes

Found while testing the SLA and Escalation feature (NDC-2266). Annotated evidence is attached. The QA business-hours set, holiday list, policy and tickets were removed afterwards.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, API, 14 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: An SLA escalation can be saved with any text as the new priority
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

An escalation level can be saved with a priority that does not exist, for example "bogus". The server accepts it and stores it. Every other invalid field in the SLA policy is rejected.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Send a request to create an SLA policy with one target and one response escalation level.

  2. Set the level's action "set priority" to the text bogus.

  3. Read the policy back.

Expected result

The request is rejected as invalid. Only low, medium, high and urgent are allowed, the same as in the editor.

Actual result

The server answers 201 Created and the policy is stored with set_priority = bogus. A valid value such as urgent is also accepted, so the check is missing, not wrong.

Additional notes

Found while testing the SLA and Escalation feature (NDC-2266). Annotated evidence is attached. When the escalation fires, the ticket would be set to a priority that does not exist; this was not tested. The QA policy was removed.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, API, 14 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The SLA editor stops a description longer than 500 characters ("The description is too long."), but the server saves one with 501 characters. The two do not agree.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Send a request to create an SLA policy with a description of exactly 500 characters. It is saved.

  2. Send the same request with 501 characters.

  3. Read the policy back.

Expected result

The 501-character description is rejected with the same limit as the editor.

Actual result

The server answers 201 Created and stores all 501 characters.

Additional notes

Found while testing the SLA and Escalation feature (NDC-2266). Annotated evidence is attached. Policy name and other fields are checked correctly by the server (for example name 121 characters is rejected). The QA policy was removed.

Environment

raw_module_items.name: Reapplying an inactive SLA policy to open tickets returns success from the server, but the screen blocks it
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

On the SLA policies list, "Reapply to open tickets" is blocked for an inactive policy with the message "Activate the policy before reapplying it." The server does not enforce this: the same request on an inactive policy answers success.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create an SLA policy that is inactive.

  2. Send the reapply-open request for that policy.

Expected result

The request is rejected with an error, the same as the screen rule.

Actual result

The server answers 200 with queued = 0. A script or integration cannot tell that nothing was reapplied.

Additional notes

Found while testing the SLA and Escalation feature (NDC-2266). Annotated evidence is attached. The QA policy was removed.

Environment

raw_module_items.name: A department still counts deleted tickets, so it cannot be deleted without moving "tickets" that no longer exist
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

After every ticket of a department is deleted and then purged from the Recycle Bin, the department still shows a ticket count and refuses to be deleted. It says "This department still has 11 tickets. Choose an active department to transfer them to." although no ticket is left.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Create a department.

  2. Create 11 tickets in it, then delete them.

  3. Open the Recycle Bin and permanently delete those tickets.

  4. Check that no ticket of this department exists in the ticket list.

  5. Delete the department.

Expected result

The ticket count only counts existing tickets, and an empty department is deleted without asking for a transfer.

Actual result

The department keeps ticket_count = 11. Deleting it answers 422 with the message above. Passing the other department as a query value gives the same 422; passing it in the request body works (200).

Additional notes

Found while testing the SLA and Escalation feature (NDC-2266). Annotated evidence is attached. A full scan of 98 tickets found none in this department. The QA department was removed with the body form of the request.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, API, 14 October 2026, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: A deleted department cannot be permanently deleted from the Recycle Bin
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A department that was deleted appears in the Recycle Bin, but "delete permanently" fails for it. Tickets, accounts and other records in the same bin can be removed.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Delete a department. It appears in the Recycle Bin (type Department).
  2. Select it and delete it permanently.

Expected result

The department is removed for good, like other records.

Actual result

The request answers 200, but the item is reported as failed with the reason recyclebin.error.unsupported_app. The item stays in the bin until it expires (2026-12-13 for this one).

Additional notes

Found while testing the SLA and Escalation feature (NDC-2266). Annotated evidence is attached. This leaves one QA test department ("QA SLA Dept") in the Recycle Bin that cannot be removed.

Environment
