raw_module_items.name: Import | Records are imported with an empty required field or a value longer than the field allows
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The Import wizard does not apply the field rules that the rest of Desk applies. A product with an empty Product Name (a required field) and a product with a 306-character name were both imported, and the import reported no errors. Creating the same products in the app or through the API is refused.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Prepare a CSV for Products with three rows: a normal row, a row with an empty Product Name, and a row whose Product Name is about 300 characters long.

  2. Go to Setup, then Data Administration, then Import. Choose Products and click Start import.

  3. Upload the file, choose Add new records, keep the automatic mapping and go to Review.

  4. Submit the import and open the new products.

Expected result

Review lists the two bad rows as errors ("Product Name is required" and "text too long"), and only the valid row is imported, the same rules the app and the API use when a product is created.

Actual result

Review shows no errors and the result is "3 added, 0 errors". One product has no Product Name at all, and another has a 306-character name. Creating either of these directly is refused with HTTP 422: "Product Name is required." and TEXT_TOO_LONG.

Additional notes

Found while running the Data Administration test spec (Desk Specs/spec-desk-data-administration.md, group C). Reproduced twice. The test products were deleted and purged afterwards. Related gap list: NDC-2494.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Import | Imported tickets are not linked to their contact — the email is saved as text
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

When tickets are imported with a Contact column, the ticket is not linked to the contact. The import saves the typed email as plain text in the ticket's contact field instead of the contact's ID, so the ticket shows "No contact on this ticket". An email that matches no contact is accepted in the same way.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Prepare a CSV for Tickets with the columns Subject, Contact and Status. In one row put the email of an existing contact; in another row put an email that belongs to no contact.
  2. Go to Setup, then Data Administration, then Import. Choose Tickets and click Start import.
  3. Upload the file, choose Add new records, and map the Contact column to the Contact field.
  4. Go to Review and submit, then open the imported tickets.

Expected result

The ticket is linked to the existing contact with that email, and appears on that contact. A row whose email matches no contact is reported at Review (or handled as the wizard explains), not stored as text.

Actual result

Review says "All 2 rows passed validation" and the result is "2 added, 0 errors". Both tickets show "No contact on this ticket". The ticket record stores the text "test@example.com" in contact_id, while a ticket created from an email stores the contact's ID there. This breaks the NDC-1662 acceptance criterion "Importing Tickets that reference a contact by email links to the existing contact rather than creating a duplicate."

Additional notes

Found while running the Data Administration test spec (group C). Reproduced twice. The test tickets were deleted and purged afterwards.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Sandboxes | Creating a sandbox never finishes and stays on "Creating · Finishing"
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A new sandbox never becomes ready. It copies the setup in about a minute, then stays on "Creating · Finishing" for good, and the page shows no error. The sandbox log stops at "Finishing — waiting: IAM is not ready for apply-grants yet (INTERNAL_ERROR)". While it is stuck, the Audit Log receives two new entries every 30 seconds.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Setup, then Data Administration, then Sandboxes.

  2. Click New sandbox, enter a name and click Create sandbox.

  3. Wait, refreshing the list from time to time, then open the sandbox's actions and choose View log.

Expected result

The sandbox becomes ready within a few minutes, as the dialog says ("This takes a few minutes"), and can be opened. If a step fails, the page shows the failure.

Actual result

The first sandbox was created at 8:38 PM and was still "Creating · Finishing" (step 6 of 7) 25 minutes later. A second sandbox created at 9:10 PM stopped at the same step with the same message. The page never shows an error. Every 30 seconds the Audit Log records "Sandboxes updated … LastRefreshedAt" and "… UpdatedAt" with raw field names and timestamps (46 entries in the first 22 minutes). The owner's login also starts asking "Choose an organization" and lists the unfinished sandbox.

Additional notes

Found while running the Data Administration test spec (group I). Both test sandboxes were deleted afterwards (deleting worked and took about 2 minutes). Because of this, the sandbox contents and "Restore into a sandbox" could not be tested.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Import | Review says all rows will import, then every row with an existing unique value fails
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The Review step of the Import wizard does not check unique fields. A file whose rows repeat values that already exist in a unique field is shown as fully valid, and then every row fails when the import runs.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Prepare a CSV for Products with three rows whose Product Name already exists (Product Name is a unique field).

  2. Go to Setup, then Data Administration, then Import. Choose Products and click Start import.

  3. Upload the file, choose Add new records without "Skip duplicate records", and go to Review.

  4. Submit the import.

Expected result

Review reports the three rows as errors ("Product Name is already in use") before anything runs, so the user can fix the file or turn on Skip duplicate records.

Actual result

Review says "All 3 rows passed validation and will be imported" with "Rows with errors 0". After Submit the result is 0 added and 3 errors, each "Product Name is already in use by another record."

Additional notes

Found while running the Data Administration test spec (group C). Reproduced twice (9 rows, then 3 rows). Nothing was created. The empty "All errors" table on the Review step is a separate ticket, NDC-2385.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Recycle Bin | Deleted products and contracts are listed as "(no name)"
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Every deleted Product and Contract appears in the Recycle Bin as "(no name)", so the user cannot tell which item to restore. Deleted tickets, tasks, contacts and accounts show their names correctly.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open a product, for example one named "QA DA D1 normal", and delete it.
  2. Go to Setup, then Data Administration, then Recycle Bin.
  3. Filter the Module list by Desk Products (or Desk Contracts).

Expected result

The deleted product is listed under its Product Name (and a contract under its Contract Name), like other modules.

Actual result

The row shows "(no name)". The Recycle Bin API returns record_label null for every desk_products and desk_contracts item. This happens both for a product deleted by hand and for products removed by "Undo import". The name search ("Starts with…") cannot find these items either.

Additional notes

Found while running the Data Administration test spec (group E). The test product was purged afterwards.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Recycle Bin | Empty Bin deletes everything after one confirmation
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

Empty Bin permanently deletes every item in the Recycle Bin after a single confirmation dialog. The Recycle Bin specification (NDC-1665) asks for an explicit second confirmation step for this action.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Go to Setup, then Data Administration, then Recycle Bin.
  2. Click Empty Bin.

Expected result

Emptying the bin needs a second, explicit confirmation (for example typing a word or a second dialog), as NDC-1665 requires: "Empty Recycle Bin with an explicit second confirmation step."

Actual result

One dialog appears, "Empty the Recycle Bin? Permanently delete ALL items you can see. This can't be undone.", with Cancel and Empty Bin. Clicking Empty Bin there is the only step. The bin on this tenant holds 1000+ items from several apps.

Additional notes

Found while running the Data Administration test spec (group E). The dialog was cancelled; nothing was deleted.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Chromium, 24 October 2026, owner account.

raw_module_items.name: Activity Life Cycle: features Zoho Desk has that Desk is missing
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

We compared Desk's Activity Life Cycle (tasks, calls and events) with Zoho Desk Activities. This ticket lists what Zoho has and Desk does not have yet. There is no single PRD for activities; this is item "Activity Life Cycle" of NDC-1865. Earlier activity gaps are in NDC-1782 (only SMS reminders left) and NDC-2008 (Phase 3), and are not repeated here.

Already done in Desk

  • Tasks, calls and events can be added from the Activities page, from a ticket's ACTIVITY tab (ticket pre-filled) and from contacts and accounts.

  • Task statuses match Zoho. Mark as Complete fills Completed Time; Reopen Task goes back to Not Started.

  • Calls: Start Call, End Call with outcome (notes go to the ticket as a private comment), Mark as missed, Cancel Call, Reopen Call, Reschedule. A completed call is locked on its page.

  • Events: Mark as Completed, Cancel, Reopen Event. An event does not close by itself when its time passes, same as Zoho.

  • Overdue badge on open activities whose time has passed.

  • 18 task views (Open, Overdue, Today's, Tomorrow's, Today + Overdue, Next 7 Days + Overdue, My …, Spam and more) showing the right records, plus custom views.

  • Classic, Compact and Table layouts, sort, search, filter, Export and bulk Update.

  • Reminders: up to 5 per activity, pop-up and email, with clear messages for every wrong value. The pop-up arrived 5 seconds after the due time.

  • Comments (with @mention, edit, delete), attachments, time entry and timer on activities.

  • Desk also has a Calendar, event invitees with RSVP and a timer, which Zoho Desk does not have.

Missing — settings

  1. Department on every activity. In Zoho it is required, it limits the owner list to that department, and an activity is only seen inside its department. Desk forms have no Department, and an admin outside Customer Support can open and edit the activities of Customer Support tickets that are 404 for them.

Missing — list and page actions

  1. Delete on the task, call or event page (Zoho: Delete, goes to the Recycle Bin). Desk can only delete through the API.

  2. Delete in the bulk bar (Zoho mass actions: Update, Delete, Assign To). Desk's bulk bar has Update only.

Missing — where activities show

  1. Activity count on the ticket (Zoho returns taskCount). Desk ticket counts are replies, comments, attachments and time entries only.

Missing — API

  1. A ticket-activities endpoint and ready-made filters (Zoho: GET /tickets/{id}/activities, dueDate=Overdue / Today / Tomorrow, /tasks/count). Desk only has the generic records API; /desk/activities, /desk/activities/stats and /desk/activities/reports return 404.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Edge, 26 October 2026, Desk Agent and Desk Admin accounts.

raw_module_items.name: Ticket Replies: features Zoho Desk has that Desk is missing
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

We compared Desk's ticket replies with Zoho Desk. This ticket lists what Zoho has and Desk does not have yet. The feature spec is NDC-1851; each item says which part of NDC-1851 it belongs to, where it is mentioned there. Scheduled replies have their own gap item, NDC-2177.

Already done in Desk

  • Reply, Reply All and Forward from the ticket header and from each message; the composer can switch between them.

  • From is the department mailbox, To is the contact, Cc and Bcc, subject "Re: …", and the answered message is quoted.

  • Send stays disabled while the body is empty. Empty bodies, bad addresses, more than 20 recipients and bodies over 65,535 characters are refused with clear messages.

  • Script, event handlers and javascript: links are removed from the sent HTML (NDC-2182 fixed).

  • Send and Close, Send as private, Schedule, Schedule and close ticket.

  • Forward is always private; Reply All after a forward does not leak it (NDC-1838 fixed).

  • Templates, placeholders, rating link, snippets (Mine / Shared, single-word names up to 50 characters, 25,600 characters, placeholders resolved) and attachments.

  • Comments: private by default, public on request, edit, delete, pin and @mention; all logged in the ticket activity feed.

  • Send for review, withdraw, approve / reject; pin a reply; show original headers; split only incoming messages (same as Zoho).

  • Copied addresses on the ticket. Reply All shows them ("Also copied on this ticket") with "Leave … off this reply" (NDC-1851 item 7).

  • Suggested articles panel in the composer (added in the 26 Oct redeploy).

  • An agent outside the ticket's department gets 404 on the ticket, its replies and its comments.

Missing — composer

  1. Send and set a status (Zoho: a status drop-down in the Send menu, on by default, for example "Waiting for customer"). Desk offers only Send and Close.

  2. Ticket number in the email subject (Zoho adds it by default and lets each department hide it). Desk sends "Re: <subject>" only.

  3. Editor tools: inline image, strikethrough, font family, spell check and attach from cloud, all in Zoho's toolbar. Desk has bold, italic, underline, size, colour, align, lists, link and placeholder.

Missing — drafts

  1. Draft auto-save every 2 minutes and an "Edit Draft" menu (Send / Edit / Discard) on the ticket. Desk saves nothing until "Save draft" is pressed (see the separate bug about where drafts are kept).

Missing — tracking

  1. Read receipts and per-recipient delivery status. NDC-1851 item 6 (Phase 3). Desk shows only "Sent"; the mail platform page reports 40 sent and 0 delivered in 7 days, so delivery events are not coming back.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com, Edge, 26 October 2026, Desk Agent account.

raw_module_items.name: Activities | Rescheduling a call with "log a missed call" fails: "One or more fields in the payload are read-only."
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

On a scheduled call, Reschedule with "The call went unanswered — log a missed call" ticked does nothing except show the error "One or more fields in the payload are read-only." The missed-call record the dialog tries to create copies read-only fields of the call (approval_status, created_at), so the server refuses it, and the call is not moved. Without the tick the same reschedule works.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Sign in as a Desk Agent (Customer Support).

  2. Add a Call with Call Status = scheduled and a start time later today.

  3. Open the call and click Reschedule.

  4. Pick tomorrow 10:00, tick The call went unanswered — log a missed call, click Reschedule.

Expected Result

  • A missed-call entry is logged for this attempt and the call moves to the new time, as the dialog itself says (and as Zoho Desk does for unanswered calls).

Actual Result

  • Error toast "One or more fields in the payload are read-only."

  • POST /api/v1/modules/{Calls}/records answers 422 FIELD_PERMISSION_DENIED, detail data.approval_status "Field 'approval_status' is read-only and cannot be changed." The body also carries created_at.

  • The call keeps its old start time; no missed call is created.

Environment

  • Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-desk.taviportal.com, builds index-PA6o3K2s.js and index-7qe5X0Gd.js (both fail)

  • Account: Desk Agent fedelav803 (Customer Support)

  • Observed: 26 Oct 2026, Activity Life Cycle run (case ACT-E6)

  • Reference: Zoho Desk Calls help article (reschedule an unanswered call, missed call logged). Our Zoho org has no calls, so it was not tried live.

  • Automation: automation/…/deskactivities/ActivityUiTest#rescheduleWithMissedLog

  • Gap list: NDC-2635

  • Evidence: annotated image attached (dialog, captured request, Zoho Add Call).

raw_module_items.name: Activities | A task saved without a status has no status and never shows in Open, My Open or Overdue
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

The Add Task form has no default status, and saving without picking one stores a task with no status at all. Such a task is missing from every working view (Open, My Open, Overdue, Today + Overdue …), even when it is overdue; it can only be found in All Tasks. The same happens for tasks created through the API without a status.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Sign in as a Desk Agent. Open Activities › Add Activity › Task.

  2. Type a subject, set a due date in the past, leave Status as "Select", click Save.

  3. Open Tasks › Open (and Overdue), search for the subject.

  4. Open Tasks › All Tasks, same search.

Expected Result

  • A new task starts as "Not Started" (Zoho Desk's Add Task form defaults Status to Not Started).

  • An open task with a past due date is listed in Open and Overdue.

Actual Result

  • The task is saved with no status (API read: status = null).

  • Open and Overdue do not list it (Open shows only other tasks); All Tasks does.

  • Agents who do not pick a status lose track of their tasks.

Environment

  • Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-desk.taviportal.com, builds index-PA6o3K2s.js and index-7qe5X0Gd.js

  • Account: Desk Agent fedelav803 (Customer Support)

  • Observed: 26 Oct 2026, cases ACT-C1 and ACT-B4

  • Reference: Zoho Desk portal taviportal, Tasks › Add Task (live, read-only): Status "Not Started" by default

  • Automation: automation/…/deskactivities/ActivityApiTest#newTaskGetsDefaultStatus

  • Gap list: NDC-2635

  • Evidence: annotated image attached.

The task is saved with no status (API read: status = null).

raw_module_items.name: Activities | Completed Time is set by the browser: the API leaves it empty and lets clients backdate it
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A task's Completed Time (completed_time) is only filled when the screen's "Mark as Complete" sends it. Completing a task through the API (and so through imports, integrations or rules) leaves it empty, and any client can write any date into it.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Create a task with status Not Started.

  2. PATCH /api/v1/modules/{Tasks}/records/{id} with status = "Completed"; read the record.

  3. On another open task, PATCH completed_time = "2001-01-01T00:00:00Z"; read the record.

Expected Result

  • The server sets Completed Time when the status becomes Completed (and clears it on reopen); clients cannot write it. In Zoho Desk completedTime is a read-only attribute.

Actual Result

  • After step 2: completed_time = null.

  • After step 3: 200 and completed_time = 2001-01-01T00:00:00Z on an open task.

  • "Mark as Complete" in the screen does fill it (sent by the browser).

Environment

  • Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-desk.taviportal.com, builds index-PA6o3K2s.js and index-7qe5X0Gd.js

  • Account: Desk Agent fedelav803

  • Reference: Zoho Desk API (Task completedTime read-only)

  • Automation: automation/…/deskactivities/ActivityApiTest#completedTimeSetByServer, #completedTimeIsReadOnly

raw_module_items.name: Ticket Replies | "Save draft" keeps the draft only in this browser; nothing is saved on the server
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

"Save draft" in the reply composer closes the composer and puts a DRAFT badge on Reply All, but the draft is only kept in the browser's localStorage (key desk.composer.draft:<user>:<ticket>). No request reaches the server, so the draft is lost on another browser or device, and other agents cannot see that someone is drafting. The server already has a drafts API (PUT /desk/tickets/{id}/drafts/mine works and is used by Send for review). Related: NDC-2179 (scheduled-reply draft not shown in the reply box, Done).

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Sign in as a Desk Agent; open an email ticket; click Reply All and type some text.

  2. Click Save draft.

  3. Call GET /api/v1/desk/tickets/{id}/drafts/mine (or open the ticket in another browser as the same agent and click Reply All).

Expected Result

  • The draft is stored on the ticket on the server and comes back for the same agent anywhere (Zoho Desk also auto-saves every 2 minutes and shows "Edit Draft").

Actual Result

  • No request to /drafts when Save draft is clicked.

  • GET drafts/mine → 404 "You have no draft on this ticket."

  • The text exists only in localStorage of this browser; another browser shows no draft.

Environment

  • Tenant: NDC-Staging — staging-desk.taviportal.com, builds index-PA6o3K2s.js and index-7qe5X0Gd.js

raw_module_items.name: Ticket History | Creation row shows "department_id" and the raw department id instead of the department name
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary. When a ticket is created, Ticket History writes a "Department changed" row that shows the internal field key department_id and the department's raw id (e.g. 7e1ac409-58b0-41ab-97e1-0e7d5c8c5158) instead of the department name, attributed to "System". Same in Arabic. A later move between departments is shown correctly with names.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Desk › Tickets › New Ticket (layout Standard), Department = Customer Support, fill Email, Subject, Status = Open › Save.
  2. Open the ticket › History tab › scroll to the rows at creation time.
  3. Switch the language to العربية and look at the same row.
  4. Control: on another ticket use the department chip › Move ticket › HR › Move, then open History.

Expected

  • The creation entry names the department: e.g. "Department: Customer Support" (or the department listed in "Ticket was created by …"), never a field key or an id. Zoho Desk (live, portal taviportal, ticket #101): the creation entry "… submitted a new ticket via email" lists "Department Anyware Software" — the name, no id, no separate "changed" row.
  • The same in Arabic (قسم: Customer Support).

Actual

  • #657 (27 Oct 15:52): "Department changed · Field department_id · Old blank · New 7e1ac409-58b0-41ab-97e1-0e7d5c8c5158 · by System"; the "Ticket was created by mahmoud.mahamed1515" row lists Subject and Status but no department.
  • Arabic: "تغيّر القسم · الحقل department_id · القديم فارغ · الجديد 7e1ac409-… · بواسطة النظام".
  • Same on every ticket created by form or API in this round (#598, #651, …).
  • Control #656: a real move shows "Ticket moved to another department · From Customer Support · To HR" and "Department was updated · Old Customer Support · New HR" — names are resolved there.

Impact

Agents and admins see an unreadable id and an internal field key in every ticket's history; it looks like a system change rather than the creator's choice.

Suggested fix

  1. Resolve the department id to its name (as the Move rows already do) and show the field label "Department", not department_id.
  2. Prefer recording the department inside the "Ticket was created" entry instead of a separate "changed from blank" row by System.

Environment: staging-desk.taviportal.com, tenant NDC-Staging, Edge, account mahmoud.mahamed1515 (Desk Administrator), 27 Oct 2026. Found while retesting NDC-2203.

Evidence: NDC-new-dept-history-BUG.png (attached).

raw_module_items.name: Tickets | Save shows "Permission denied." although the ticket is created — users save again and create duplicates
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary. When a user saves a ticket that, after the save, they are no longer allowed to see (owner = a colleague, a team they are not in, or a workflow rule moves it there), Desk answers 403 PERMISSION_DENIED and shows "Permission denied." — but the ticket is created / the edit is saved. On the New Ticket form the form stays open, so users click Save again and create duplicates.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Sign in as a user who is not an agent of Customer Support but can create tickets (here: Desk Administrator mahmoud.mahamed1515; sees own + unassigned tickets).
  2. Tickets › New Ticket (Standard) › Department Customer Support, Email, Subject, Status Open, Ticket Owner = a colleague (Customer Experience Specialists 2) › Save.
  3. Click Save again.
  4. Sign in as the colleague and open All Tickets.

Expected

  • The ticket is saved once with a success message; if the saver can't open it afterwards, say so ("Ticket created. You don't have access to it.") and leave the form (go back to the list). Never report an error for a write that succeeded.
  • API: 201 with the id (or a documented response for "created but not visible"), not 403.

Actual

  • Step 2: toast "Permission denied." (POST /api/v1/modules/{Tickets}/records → 403), form stays open. Ticket #675 exists.
  • Step 3: same 403 again → a second ticket. #676 and #677 both exist with the same subject.
  • Same 403 with the record created: API create with another owner (#671) or with a team and no owner (#672); a Create rule "Assign to team" (#605, #616, #617, #658); an Edit rule that moves the ticket to a team (#650, edit saved).
  • A Create rule "Assign to specific user" returns 201 (#673) because it runs after the create; the creator silently loses access.
  • Control: the same form with no owner/team (unassigned) → 201, the ticket opens (#657).

Impact

Duplicate tickets (customers may get two acknowledgements), users believe the save failed, API clients retry. Any admin or agent creating a ticket for a colleague or a team hits it.

Suggested fix

  1. Check visibility of the response separately from the write: return 201/200 with the id and a flag (e.g. accessible:false) instead of 403 after committing.
  2. UI: on that flag show "Ticket created and assigned to …" and close the form.

Environment: staging-desk.taviportal.com, tenant NDC-Staging, Edge + API, 27 Oct 2026. Found while retesting NDC-2203 (D1 Assign to team).

Evidence: NDC-new-false-permission-denied.png (attached).

raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary. A workflow rule on Tickets with trigger "On create" whose condition uses a computed rule fact — Is Overdue, Execution Time, Recent Comment (and its type), Number of Threads, Number of Comments — runs and its actions are done, but Ticket History gets no "Workflow rule ran" row. The same rule with a normal field in the condition writes the row, and the same fact in an "On edit" rule writes it too.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Setup › Automation › Workflow Rules › Tickets › new rule: On create, condition Is Overdue is true, action Add comment (private) › Save & Activate.
  2. Create a ticket with a due date of yesterday.
  3. Open the ticket › History.
  4. Repeat with the condition Status is Open instead (control).

Expected

  • Every rule run writes "Workflow rule ran · Rule <name> · Triggered by A new ticket · Actions …" (as fixed in NDC-2203), whatever fields the condition uses.

Actual

  • Is Overdue (#653), Execution Time (#654), Recent Comment (#661), Thread count (#666), Comment count (#667), and description AND Is Overdue (#662): Execution History shows Fired, the comment is in History "by workflow rule …", but there is no "Workflow rule ran" row (waited 45–60 s).
  • Control: no condition (#651), description (#652), Due Date before now (#655), Status (#668), Priority (#669) → the row is written.
  • Is Overdue in an On edit rule (#665) → the row is written. Execution records are identical with and without the row.

Impact

History does not explain why a ticket changed for rules that use these conditions; audits and support investigations miss the rule.

Suggested fix

Write the "Workflow rule ran" history entry from the same place for every Create-rule execution, including the path that evaluates rule facts.

Environment: staging-desk.taviportal.com, tenant NDC-Staging, Edge + API, 27 Oct 2026. Found while retesting NDC-2203 (F4).

Evidence: NDC-new-rule-ran-row-missing.png (attached).

raw_module_items.name: Web Forms | Form added with the website code doesn't appear on the website (Desk and CRM)
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

A web form added to a website with the "Add it to your website" code (the Recommended option) never appears. The page shows an empty space where the form should be. This happens for both Desk and CRM forms, even when the website is listed in the form's settings.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. In Desk, go to Settings, open Web Forms and open the form "Tech Support".

  2. Open the "Publish & how to use" tab and copy the code under "Add it to your website".

  3. Make sure the website is listed in the form's settings.

  4. Paste the code into a page on that website and open the page in a browser that isn't signed in.

  5. Repeat with the CRM form "Potential Leads" (Settings › Web Forms › Embed code › "Add it to your website").

Expected Result

  • The form appears on the website and visitors can fill it in and send it.

Actual Result

  • No form appears. The space where it should be stays empty, for both the Desk and the CRM form.

  • There's no message telling the visitor or the admin that anything is wrong.

Environment

  • App: TAVI Desk (staging-desk.taviportal.com) and TAVI CRM (staging-crm.taviportal.com), Settings › Web Forms; tenant Anyware

  • Forms: Desk "Tech Support", CRM "Potential Leads"

  • Test page: http://127.0.0.1:5500/feedback-form.html, the website listed on both forms

  • Browser: Edge (headless), signed out

  • Observed: 1 Nov 2026

  • Dev note: the browser blocks the form's session request with "No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource". The server does accept the request (200, session issued), but its response only allows https://staging-crm.taviportal.com, so no customer website can use it. The browser's pre-check (preflight, 204) also has no access headers.

  • Related: NDC-1488 (the hosted link opens an nginx 404); NDC-2732 (the iframe form failed to load; it works again as of 1 Nov).

Attachment

Evidence images: the empty test page (embed-check.png) and the console errors.

raw_module_items.name: Desk Skills: missing functions vs Zoho Desk
raw_module_items.description_html:
Goal

Make Desk Skills work like Zoho Desk. An admin defines skills with a type, criteria and agents, and Desk adds the matching skills to each ticket. Skill-based round robin then sends the ticket to an agent who holds them. This ticket lists only the skills setup that is still missing. Routing rules are in NDC-2275 (RR-9, RR-18).

Already in TAVI Desk (checked 1 Nov 2026)

  • Setup → Assignment Rules → Skills tab with Preferences: "Add skills to tickets by their criteria" (off by default), and where added skills go (top, bottom, or the order of the list).

  • Skill types: add, rename and delete. Deleting a type keeps its skills and leaves them untyped.

  • Each skill has a type, a description and criteria (AND / OR). A skill removed from the field shows "Removed from the field", with Clear.

  • Skills are the options of the Tickets "Skills" field, added and renamed in Modules & Fields.

  • Agent Skills tab: tick the skills each agent holds.

  • Skill-based round robin: only agents who hold every skill on the ticket are eligible, and offline agents are skipped.

  • Workflow actions: Add skills, Remove skills (1–25), Recalculate skills, Reassign ticket based on skills.

Missing compared with Zoho Desk

  1. Skills per department. Zoho sets skills, the skill preference and the skill order per department (up to 30 active skills per department), and maps agents to skills per department. TAVI has one list and one set of preferences for the whole company.

  2. Active / Inactive status. In Zoho, an inactive skill is not added to tickets and is not used for assignment. TAVI has no status; the only way to stop a skill is to delete the field option.

  3. Add Skill on the Skills page, with a required type. Zoho's Add Skill asks for Skill Name and Skill Type (both required), Description, Criteria and Agents, and a type can be added inline. TAVI has no Add Skill button: the name comes from Modules & Fields and the type is optional.

  4. Agents on the skill form. Zoho: "Associate agents with this skill…". TAVI: agents can only be picked one agent at a time on the Agent Skills tab.

  5. Search and filters. Zoho has separate Skills and Skill Types tabs, with filters for Name, Skill Type, Agents and Status. TAVI shows a plain list with no search or filters.

  6. Reorder skills. Zoho reorders skills per department, and its "order in settings" placement follows that order. TAVI offers the "list order" option but has no way to reorder.

  7. Recalculate and assign one ticket. Zoho can run Recalculate Skills and skill-based assignment on a single ticket. TAVI has these only as workflow actions.

  8. Show where a skill is used. Zoho lists the rules that use a skill. TAVI gives no warning about the workflows or rules that still use a deleted skill.

  9. Limits. Zoho allows at most 10 skills on a ticket, with the first having the highest priority. TAVI has no limit on the field, and the workflow action allows 25.

Evidence

  • 01-skills-list-vs-zoho.png: Skills page, TAVI vs Zoho (Add Skill, Skill Types tab, filters and status, department, preferences).

  • 02-skill-form-vs-zoho.png: skill form, TAVI vs Zoho (name, required type, description, criteria, agents).

  • tavi-01-skills-tab.png, tavi-02-agent-skills-tab.png, tavi-03-skill-editor.png: TAVI screens, 1 Nov 2026.

raw_module_items.name: Title: Blueprint | Running a transition with an attached file fails: “File … does not belong to you” (422)
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary
Some ticket blueprint transitions let the agent attach a file. When the agent uploads a file there and clicks Run, the transition fails with “File … does not belong to you.” and the ticket stays in its current state, even though the agent uploaded the file a moment earlier.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Go to Desk › Tickets and open a ticket that’s in a blueprint, at the Open state.

  2. Click the transition Open To On Hold.

  3. In the transition window, click Add attachment and choose an image, for example “images.png”.

  4. Wait for the file to finish uploading, then click Run.

Expected Result

  • The transition runs, and the ticket moves to On Hold.

  • The uploaded file is saved with the transition and shows on the ticket.

Actual Result

  • An error appears: “File dace0562-650c-4327-b3c7-9ec44a858e39 does not belong to you.”

  • The ticket stays in Open, and the transition isn’t recorded.

  • The agent can’t complete any transition that needs an attachment.

Environment

  • staging-desk.taviportal.com › Tickets › ticket › Blueprint transition “Open To On Hold”

  • Edge 156.0.8078.48; Windows 10; 1590×591

  • Reporter Mahmoud Mohamed; captured 1 Nov 2026, 4:20 PM (Cairo)

Attachment — Attachment

Settings

  • Status Bug, priority urgent, start date 1 Nov 2026.

  • Assignees: Hegazy, Mahmoud, mfathy.

  • Label Blueprint; Desk module.

  • Sprint: the current one, once I can see it.

raw_module_items.name: Blueprint (with SLA tie-in): features Zoho Desk has that Desk is missing
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary

We compared Desk's new Blueprint feature, and how its step time limits work next to the SLA, with Zoho Desk (Enterprise trial, checked live). This ticket lists what Zoho has and Desk does not have yet. The feature spec is NDC-1974; it has only two lines and no requirements, so no item can be given a phase yet. SLA gaps already in NDC-2266 are not repeated here.

Already done in Desk

  • Blueprints page grouped by department, with layout, number of states, Draft badge and tickets in progress.

  • Activate, deactivate, include tickets, revoke tickets and delete (delete is refused while tickets are inside).

  • Drag to set the order; a ticket enters the first blueprint that matches.

  • One department and one layout per blueprint, with entry criteria or all tickets.

  • States are ticket statuses; Add State creates a new status. Up to 16 connections per state, same as Zoho.

  • Common transitions and continuous blueprints.

  • Save Draft, Save and Publish, and a list of problems to fix before publishing.

  • Before: owners can be agents, teams, the ticket owner, or another department with Full, Read only or Restricted access. Criteria decide when the button shows.

  • During: reply, comment, attachment, resolution, required fields, checklist and message, each required or optional, in the order you set.

  • After: field update, notification, task, webhook, Desk email and custom action.

  • Time limit per state with a warning, business or calendar clock, actions when it runs out, and an automatic move when it runs out.

  • A transition can run on its own when the customer replies or rates.

  • Ticket page: blueprint pill, progress bar, Steps card with due and overdue times. Status is locked and a reply does not close the ticket.

  • Revoke one ticket, a list of tickets, or all tickets. Ticket history shows every blueprint event.

  • Desk also has things Zoho does not have: include existing tickets at a chosen state, version history with restore, parallel steps, webhook and notification after-actions, actions at the warning time.

Missing — blueprint settings

  1. Strict Mode: agents can act on the ticket and edit fields only through transitions (lock all, lock selected, or lock all except selected). Today only Status is locked.

  2. Change transition owners from inside a ticket (Zoho "Dynamic Transition Owner Assignment"). Today owners are fixed in the blueprint.

  3. Order of the transition buttons for each state (Zoho: drag and drop in the state settings). No order setting in the Desk designer.

Missing — during a transition

  1. Field check with your own error message, for example "Amount must be more than 0". Today a field can only be required. The CRM designer has "validations", but Desk turns it off and fieldValidations is always empty in the API.

  2. Submit for approval as a step in the transition.

  3. Share the ticket with another department as a step the agent fills in. Today sharing only happens automatically for owners in another department.

  4. Widgets (extensions) inside the transition form.

  5. Save a half-done transition as a draft and finish it later. Today closing the form loses what was typed ("The reply and notes were not saved. Leave without saving them?").

  6. Different required items for different agent groups (Zoho "Custom Mandatory").

Missing — automatic transitions

  1. Run only on certain ratings (Good or Bad) or certain replies. Today "When the customer rates / replies, run" fires on any rating or reply.

Missing — state time limits (SLA tie-in)

  1. Several escalation levels per state, each before, on or after the due time, with its own people and email template. Today a state has one warning and one set of actions when the limit runs out.

  2. Choose which business-hours set (and holidays) a state counts in. Today only "Business hours" or "Calendar time", although Desk can have several business-hours sets.

Missing — where agents see results

  1. Blueprint views in the ticket list: Active Blueprint Tickets, All Transitions, My Transitions, My Team Transitions, Unassigned Transitions. Today none, and no blueprint or state column or filter.

  2. Blueprint dashboard: active and completed tickets, tickets and states over their time limit, met vs missed, average time per blueprint and per state, how often each transition runs. Today no blueprint report; /modules/{tickets}/blueprints/reports, /blueprints/{id}/stats, /desk/blueprints/dashboard and /desk/blueprints/reports return 404.

Missing — permissions

  1. A separate "Revoke Blueprint" profile permission. Today one permission, desk:blueprints:manage, covers designing, including and revoking.

Could not be checked

  • The tenant's only business-hours set is 24×7 and both holiday lists are empty, so business and calendar time give the same due times. Please add a QA business-hours set (for example Sun–Thu 09:00–17:00 with one holiday), or allow us to add one, so we can test state time limits, warnings and automatic moves in business hours.

  • Whether a state on an On Hold status pauses the department SLA and the state's own timer. It needs transitions run on QA tickets. Please approve the functional run so we can test it.

  • Transitions on instant-messaging tickets. We could not see an IM channel. Please tell us if WhatsApp or Telegram is connected to a department so we can test a transition with a required reply on an IM ticket.

Additional notes

  • Not gaps: clone a blueprint, roles as transition owners and changing department as an action (Zoho has none of these); Zoho edition limits.

  • Same engine as CRM: NDC-2540, NDC-2420 and NDC-2730 will be re-checked on Desk in the functional run.

  • Possible bug to check separately: the On Hold state of "Demo · Refund approval" closes tickets after 3 days (the canvas shows "3d"), but the state panel shows "No limit", so saving the state may drop the auto-close.

  • Possible bug to check separately: the time-limit example always says "Monday to Friday, 9 to 5", although this tenant's business hours are 24×7.

  • Possible bug to check separately: the status "Reopened" has the type Closed, so a "Reopened" state may end the blueprint.

  • Possible bug to check separately: ticket #805 is inside a blueprint and still shows the "Close ticket" button.

  • Please add acceptance criteria to NDC-1974 so these items can be given phases.

  • Screenshots: TAVI vs Zoho side by side for every item are attached; the full report is docs/desk-blueprint/desk-blueprint-missing-list.html in the QA repository.

  • Test spec: docs/desk-blueprint/spec-desk-blueprint.md in the QA repository (Group Z rows Z1–Z15 = items 1–15).

  • Nothing was changed on the Desk tenant.

Environment

staging-desk.taviportal.com (org Anyware), Edge, 1 November 2026, owner account. Zoho Desk Enterprise trial, admin account.

raw_module_items.name: Blueprint | A state's automatic close after its time limit is not shown in the state panel ("No limit"), so it can be lost or not noticed
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary
In blueprint "Demo · Refund approval", the On Hold state is saved to move tickets on their own to Closed after 3 days ("Close after 3 days without an answer"). The canvas shows "3d" on the state. When you open the state, the panel says Time limit "No limit" and does not show the "When it runs out" setting, so the admin cannot see or change the automatic close there.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Go to Desk › Setup › Automation › Blueprints and open "Demo · Refund approval".

  2. Look at the On Hold state on the canvas. It shows a 3-day timer ("3d").

  3. Click the On Hold state to open its panel.

  4. Look at Time limit and the settings under it.

Expected Result

  • The panel shows the state's automatic move: after 3 days, run "Close after 3 days without an answer".

  • The admin can see, change or remove it from the panel.

  • Saving the state without changes keeps the automatic close.

Actual Result

  • Time limit shows "No limit" and "Warn before" is empty.

  • The "When it runs out" setting is not shown at all.

  • The saved blueprint still has the automatic close (autoTransitionId: auto-close, autoTransitionAfterMinutes: 4320, no slaMinutes), so it can't be seen or changed in the screen. Not checked yet: whether pressing "Save state" on this panel removes the automatic close.

Environment

  • staging-desk.taviportal.com (org Anyware) › Setup › Automation › Blueprints › Demo · Refund approval

  • Edge, Windows 10, 1600×1000

  • Owner account, 1 Nov 2026. Found during the Blueprint gap analysis (NDC-2754).

raw_module_items.name: Blueprint | The time-limit example always says "Counted on a Monday to Friday, 9 to 5 week", not the tenant's real business hours
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary
When a blueprint state has a time limit counted in business hours, the panel shows an example of when a ticket gets the warning and is due. The example is always worked out on a Monday to Friday, 9 to 5 week. This tenant's business hours are 24×7, and the real ticket timers follow 24×7, so the example shows different times from what will really happen.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Go to Desk › Setup › Business Hours and check the hours: Default, 24×7, Africa/Cairo.

  2. Go to Setup › Automation › Blueprints and open "Demo · Refund approval".

  3. Click the Escalated state (Time limit 8 hours, Warn before 1 hour, Clock "Business hours").

  4. Read the example under Clock.

Expected Result

  • The example uses the tenant's business hours. With 24×7 hours, a ticket that enters on Monday 16:00 gets the warning on Monday 23:00 and is due on Tuesday 00:00, matching what the ticket timer does.

Actual Result

  • The example says: "A ticket that enters on Monday 16:00 gets the warning on Tuesday 15:00 and is due on Tuesday 16:00. Counted on a Monday to Friday, 9 to 5 week."

  • Real tickets in this state follow 24×7: ticket #805 entered Escalated on 30 Oct 16:51 UTC and its time limit ran out on 31 Oct 00:51 UTC, exactly 8 hours later.

Environment

  • staging-desk.taviportal.com (org Anyware) › Setup › Automation › Blueprints › Demo · Refund approval › Escalated

  • Edge, Windows 10, 1600×1000

  • Owner account, 1 Nov 2026. Found during the Blueprint gap analysis (NDC-2754).

raw_module_items.name: Blueprint | "Close ticket" button is still shown on a ticket that is inside a blueprint
raw_module_items.description_html:
Summary
Ticket #805 is inside blueprint "Demo · Refund approval" at state Escalated. Its Status is locked ("Set by blueprint Demo · Refund approval"), and the reply box already refuses to close it ("The ticket stays open because it follows blueprint …"). Even so, the "Close ticket" button at the bottom of the ticket is still shown.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Go to Desk › Tickets › All Tickets and open ticket #805 "[Demo Refund] Order #1002 arrived damaged".

  2. Check the header: it shows "Demo · Refund approval / Escalated", and Status shows "Escalated" with a lock and "Set by blueprint Demo · Refund approval".

  3. Look at the bottom right of the ticket.

Expected Result

  • While a ticket is in a blueprint it can only be closed through the blueprint's transitions, so "Close ticket" is hidden or disabled, with a hint to use the transitions (as the Status field and the reply box already do).

Actual Result

  • The "Close ticket" button is shown and looks active.

  • Not checked yet: what happens when it is clicked (whether it closes the ticket outside the blueprint or shows an error).

Environment

  • staging-desk.taviportal.com (org Anyware) › Tickets › #805

  • Edge, Windows 10, 1600×1000

  • Owner account, 1 Nov 2026. Found during the Blueprint gap analysis (NDC-2754).
